jobs.occupation: Mechanical Engineer in Production [Mid-Senior; F/M/D] (Ingenieur/in - Maschinenbau)
jobs.description: About us Global protein consumption is skyrocketing—especially meat.And that’s creating massive challenges for health, climate, andanimal welfare. At Project Eaden, we’re tackling this head-on withour patented fiber spinning technology: plant-based meat withauthentic texture and taste. Our LEKKA products are already inmillions of homes across Germany, Austria, and Switzerland. Yourmission If you're a mechanical engineer and want to apply your skillsto food production technology, this is your chance to developinnovative mechanical systems for plant-based meat manufacturing, thisis your chance to take the next step and take operationalresponsibility. Join us now as we scale operations in a fast-growing,purpose-driven startup. Key responsibilities Machinery Installation &Commissioning: Support installation of new food processing equipment,perform commissioning and validation procedures, and conductfunctional testing to ensure proper operation before production use.Continuous Modification & Improvement: Analyze existing processes andequipment performance, identify improvements, and design modificationsto increase efficiency, reliability, and food safety compliance.Implement optimizations in the production environment. EquipmentRepair & Troubleshooting: Diagnose and repair mechanical, electrical,integrated and pneumatic equipment failures. Troubleshoot complexissues in mixers, conveyors, industrial machines, and automationequipment. Implement timely repairs to minimize production downtime.Mechanical Design & Process Optimization: Build and test mechanicalprototypes and operational processes, validate design performancethrough testing and prototyping, iterate designs based on productionfeedback and food safety requirements. Cross-functional Collaboration:Work closely with production, R&D and quality teams to optimizeequipment performance and resolve complex production challenges.Communicate equipment status and maintenance needs to productionplanning and leadership. Technical documentation: Develop and maintaincomprehensive technical documentation including S.O.P.s, schematics,mechanical drawings, process diagrams, and system specifications.Vendor & Contractor Management: Manage relationships with externalvendors, contractors, and service providers. Coordinate procurementactivities, oversee contractor performance, and ensure projectdeliverables meet specifications. Your profile In this role, you'll beresponsible for designing custom food processing equipment, developingmechanical solutions for plant-based protein manufacturing, andsupporting the mechanical engineering needs of our productionoperations. As a hands-on mechanical engineer, you'll work oneverything from equipment design to production support. RequirementsProfessional Experience: 5-8 years of mechanical engineeringexperience in production or manufacturing environment, preferably withexposure to food processing, manufacturing equipment, or automatedsystems. Educational Background: Bachelor's degree in MechanicalEngineering, Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, orrelated technical field. Strong foundation in equipment maintenance,reliability engineering, and manufacturing processes. Knowledge offood industry applications preferred. Technical Skills: Knowledge ofmanufacturing processes and production optimization techniques,familiarity with lean manufacturing principles. Strong troubleshootingabilities with hands-on experience developing mechanical solutions anddiagnosing and repairing mechanical equipment failures. Proficiencywith CAD software, process modeling tools, and manufacturing softwaresystems. Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solvingabilities with experience in root cause analysis and processtroubleshooting. Ability to interpret production data and developlonglasting cost effective engineering solutions. Operational Agility:A proactive, solutions-oriented mindset with the ability to adaptquickly in a fast-paced, dynamic startup environment. LanguageProficiency: Fluency in English and/or German, with professional levelin the later, with excellent written and verbal communication skills.Why us? Why you should apply now Scaling Big: We’re at an excitinginflection point, transitioning from a pilot phase to scalingoperations. Be part of something transformative and build it from theground up. Top-Tier Backing: We’re supported by world-class VCs andangels who share our vision and believe in our mission. The Time isNow: Food needs a massive transformation. Join us in creatingirresistible, sustainable food that inspires billions to switch awayfrom animal-based meat, fast! A word on Diversity, Equity & InclusionWe embrace diversity and equal opportunities for all. Shared valuesand alignment with Project Eaden’s purpose matter most to us. Wewelcome applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of age,color, national origin, race, religion, gender, sexual orientation,gender identity, or marital status. Workspace and culture We’rebuilding something massive—a gentle giant in the food industry. Ourteam thrives on collaboration, and we believe in the power offace-to-face communication to move fast and work effectively.Currently, we spend most of our time together at our workplace inBerlin to nurture our team spirit and culture. As we grow over thenext few years, we aim to evolve into a more distributed workplace,blending the flexibility of remote work with the strength of ourshared values and connection.

jobs.occupation: Forward Deployed Engineer: Ai Solution Architect (f/m/d) (Informatiker/in)
jobs.description: As a Senior AI Solution Architect in our Forward Deployed Engineering team, you see the whole board before a single line of code is written. You partner directly with business leaders across Siemens to map complex challenges to existing data, design cross-platform architectures spanning cloud and enterprise systems, and make critical build-versus-buy decisions in days rather than quarters. You bridge deep technical AI expertise with systems thinking, acting as a force multiplier that enables agile engineering teams to deliver high-impact solutions reliably and repeatedly.What we offer you:- An attractive remuneration package- Access to Siemens share plans- 30 days of paid vacation and a variety of flexible work schedules that allow time off for you and your family- Flexible training opportunities for both your professional and personal development that you can tailor to your interestsSince each of over 300,000 team members feels that other benefits are particularly important, and we cannot list our entire benefit portfolio here, you can find more information here (https://www.siemens.com/de/en/company/jobs/benefits-what-we-offer.html) .The individual benefits are subject to regulatory, contractual, or corporate conditions.You’ll make an impact by:- Driving rapid solution architecture as the first technical expert in every engagement, translating complex business problems into viable technical blueprints within days. - Designing interconnected solutions across the entire enterprise landscape, leveraging SDC for workloads while integrating seamlessly with SAP, Salesforce, and cloud-native services. - Owning crucial architecture decisions regarding cost, latency, scalability, and stack selection, while documenting clear justifications for every trade-off. - Evaluating emerging AI technologies with rigorous skepticism, providing evidence-backed adoption recommendations and having the courage to say "not ready yet." - Staying actively involved in the codebase through technical spikes, prototype development, and pull-request reviews to ensure your architectures remain grounded in reality. - Designing from day one for seamless handover, establishing explicit interface contracts, evaluation harnesses, and operational runbooks so domain teams can run systems autonomously.Your defining qualities:- Education: You hold a university degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, AI/ML, or a comparable quantitative field, where a proven track record of shipped systems outweighs advanced degrees. - Experience & Skills:- You bring 8 or more years of experience in software architecture, AI/ML systems design, or solution architecture, including at least 3 years focused on complex enterprise AI solutions. - You demonstrate a robust history of customer-facing delivery and technical leadership, especially when navigating demanding or high-pressure stakeholder environments. - You posses hands-on coding capabilities in Python alongside TypeScript or JavaScript, allowing you to write production-grade code and build functional prototypes. - You provide expertise in cross-platform system design by successfully integrating disparate enterprise environments like SAP, Salesforce, and modern cloud services. - You exhibit deep knowledge of the modern AI stack, covering LLM failure modes, RAG architectures, evaluation metrics, vector stores, and prominent agent frameworks. - You bring working knowledge of at least one major cloud provider (Azure, AWS, or GCP) sufficient to design scalable multi-platform workloads.- Ways of working:- You demonstrate the critical ability to evaluate emerging technologies objectively, separate genuine value from hype, and communicate technical realities clearly. - You display exceptional live communication skills to sketch defensible architectures in real-time meetings and explain them fluently in business terms.- Languages: You have fluent English language skills, complemented by strong German proficiency as an advantageous asset for local stakeholder engagements.You are much more than your qualifications, and we believe in the potential of every single candidate. We look forward to getting to know you!At Siemens, we believe that feeling valued and included is the foundation for doing great work. That’s why we aim to create an inclusive workplace where everyone feels a sense of belonging, and where individual perspectives and experiences are celebrated. Our commitment to fairness and respect extends to every applicant.As an equal opportunity employer (http://www.siemens.com/global/en/company/sustainability/social-commitments/belonging.html) , we welcome applications from individuals of all backgrounds and particularly encourage applications from persons with disabilities.About usWe know that our business thrives only when our people thrive and unlock their full potential. That’s why you are always our top priority. Our global, diverse team is ready to support, challenge, and inspire you, helping you grow in countless ways. Together, we’ll embark on an exciting journey of discovery. Who knows where this path will lead? Join us and take an active role in shaping your future!www.siemens.de/careers (http://www.siemens.com/de/en/company/jobs.html) – if you would like to find out more about jobs & careers at Siemens.FAQ (https://www.siemens.com/en-us/company/jobs/faq/) – if you need further information on the application process.

jobs.occupation: PhD position (m/f/d) on immune reset through CAR T in chronic inflammatory diseases (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: State-of-the-art medicine and nursing care you can rely on! - Since being founded in 1815, Universitätsklinikum Erlangen has offered medicine of the highest standard and incorporated the latest insights from medical research and state-of-the-art equipment into diagnosis and therapy. More than 10.000 employees from approximately 50 different occupations are needed to provide the wide range of services offered by Universitätsklinikum Erlangen, ensuring our patients receive the very best care around the clock.As a PhD student, you will investigate how human immune-cell networks shape tissue inflammation, regeneration and response to cellular therapies. The project will focus primarily on the human immune system and combine patient-derived material with experimental models to address mechanistic questions in cellular immunology.Your tasks:- Characterizing human immune-cell populations and their functional states using multiparameter flow cytometry and high-dimensional immune phenotyping.- Investigating cellular interactions and immune networks by integrating phenotypic, functional and molecular data from immune cells and tissues.- Studying immune responses to cellular therapies, including the mechanisms underlying immune depletion, reconstitution and tissue regeneration following CD19 CAR-T-cell therapy.- Generating and analyzing molecular data using approaches such as bulk and single-cell RNA sequencing and other transcriptomic or spatial technologies.- Establishing and applying experimental models to investigate mechanisms identified in human samples, including selected mouse models of intestinal inflammation, immune reconstitution and tissue regeneration after CD19 CAR-T-cell therapy.- Developing and combining experimental and analytical approaches ranging from established methods such as ELISA, Western blotting and flow cytometry to advanced multidimensional cytometry, UMAP-based analysis and transcriptomic approaches.- The project offers substantial scope to develop an individual scientific profile. Previous experience with these techniques is welcome, but curiosity, scientific independence, willingness to learn, and enthusiasm for understanding how immune cells interact in human disease are similarly important.Essential experience/ qualifications:- Above the average motivation and work ethics- Strong theoretical and practical background in standard methods of molecular and cellular biology as well as cellular immunology- English writing and speaking skills- Ability to work together in a multi-national team that is supportive of one another- A master degree (M.Sc.) in immunology, biology, molecular biology, molecular medicine or equivalentadditional advantages:- Experience in omics data science- Hands-on experience in human immunologyWe offer:- The position is full-time and will be payed according to salary group TVL-E 13, 65% (DFG-typical rate)- Intended pay grade depending on qualifications and personal requierements- Initially, the position is limited for one year, with the possibility of an extension till the degreee is achieved- The head of the department guaranties in writing that there is funding till the degree is achieved.- Hiring process opened and will be completed asap.- An enthusiastic, interdisciplinary team of scientists and doctors- High end translational research- State-of-the-art laboratories- Two-Stepp mentoring with a hands-on mentor (post-doc) plus the PI as supervisor with high frequent project discussions for efficient development- Structured program for hard- and soft-skills in research (paper and grant writing classes, paper clubs, soft-skill training)- Notes for applicants (f/m/d) ( https://www.karriere.uk-erlangen.de/bewerbung/hinweise-fuer-bewerbende/ )- Comprehensive health promotion offers- All benefits of the public service incl. supplementary pension plan of the Versorgungsanstalt des Bundes und der Länder (VBL) (Federal and State Government Employees' Retierment Fund)- Family-friendly enviromentFurther information:Prof. Dr. med. habil. Fabian MüllerMedizinische Klinik 5Phone: 09131 - 85 43107Applications:Universitätsklinikum ErlangenMedizinische Klinik 5 -Hämatologie & Internistische OnkologiePD Dr. med. habil. As AI-assisted coding grows, the need for deep, static code analysis is more critical than ever.In this role, you’ll join our Qodana Core team to expand our static analysis engine and design new algorithms for complex, inter-procedural code analysis. Familiarity with languages and ecosystems beyond the JVM – such as C++, Rust, JavaScript or TypeScript, Python, .NET, or Go – would also be valuable.What you’ll need- Deep, practical knowledge of JVM development (such as Kotlin or Java).- Experience designing and implementing complex algorithms or handling performance-critical backend architectures.- Fluent communication skills in English to collaborate with team members globally.What success looks like- **First 3 months:** You will get familiar with the Qodana codebase and the IntelliJ Platform architecture, delivering your first set of analysis rules and integrations.- **First 6 months:** You will take full ownership of specific analysis features, collaborating with neighboring teams to design robust solutions for complex codebases.- **Long term:** You will help shape the technical direction of Qodana Core, continuously raising the bar for static analysis performance and developer experience.Why join JetBrains?- Strong base salary – We offer competitive pay that reflects your skills and experience.- Flexible work schedule – Enjoy the freedom to work from home or from the office.- Extra time off – More days to relax, recharge, and do the things you love.- Learning and development opportunities – Access to conferences, courses, and language classes.- Relocation support – Assistance to help make your move as smooth and stress-free as possible.- Free meals and snacks – Lunch and refreshments provided to keep you fueled.- Health and wellness – On-site gyms or sports club stipends.- Internal events – Company-wide celebrations and team gatherings.We are an equal opportunity employer. jobs.occupation: Research Software Engineer (all genders) HPC & Pferformance Portability (Softwareentwickler/in)
jobs.description: The German Climate Computing Centre (DKRZ) is the central simulation and data processing facility for the German climate and Earth system modelling community and one of the leading institutions in this field worldwide. DKRZ not only operates supercomputers of the highest performance class and one of the largest data and archive systems, but also participates in many national and international projects aimed at improving the software and infrastructure for climate modelling. Here we are offering a position asResearch Software Engineer (all genders) HPC & Performance PortabilityYour tasksA key focus for DKRZ is the development of the climate and weather model ICON, and its further preparation for current and future HPC systems. Within the European PHOENIX project, we aim to develop a maintainable, performance-portable version of ICON that runs efficiently on heterogeneous CPU and GPU architectures. In this context, you will contribute to the development, integration, and optimisation of ICON on the largest European supercomputers.Your work will focus on several aspects of performance-portable scientific software, depending on your background and interests. PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d): Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre (SBiK-F), starting as of 01 January2027:PhD position or Postdoctoral researcher (m/f/d):Effects of global livestock management on wildlife movementitel (m/f/d)(Part-Time)Location: Frankfurt am MainEmployment scope: PhD position (65%) / PostDoc (up to 60%)Type of contract: Temporary, limited to 4 years, until 31.12.20230Remuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E 13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The mission of the Senckenberg Biodiversity and Climate Research Centre is to study the complex interactions between biodiversity, climate and society.As part of the Centre, the group “Global Land Systems and Biodiversity” takes a system perspective on how production, trade and consumption of food and other biomass products affect ecosystems and people.The VEBITA project, conducted jointly by SGN, the Marburg University and the Institute for Social-Ecological Research (ISOE) brings together researchers and practice partners to work towards utilizing animal movement data for early-warning systems for nature conservation. By analyzing GPS and sensor data from animals with statistical and AI-based methods, VEBITA aims to detect how animal behaviors change in response to land use, climate change, habitat loss, infrastructure development, and other environmental pressures.The adverstised position focuses on the effects of livestock management on wildlife movements contributes a use-case for state-of-the art animal movement data. Currently, livestock keeping has the largest spatial footprint of all land uses and the global biomass of mammalian livestock exceeds that of all remaining wild mammals by an order of magnitude. How and where livestock are kept greatly impacts the movements of the remaining wild mammals.In this context, we seek to develop a refined biodiversity footprint approach that captures how different livestock management strategies impact movement of wild mammals and how management can be adapted to achieve more sustainable outcomes. This subproject is part of VEBITA’s transdisciplinary focus, and the design of the novel footprint approach will consider perspectives of different relevant societal stakeholder groups such as livestock farmers, conservationists, and regulators. Results and insights of this work will also feed back to international science-policy debates on how conservation and human activities can be aligned in the future.Your tasks- Advance existing biodiversity footprint approaches in the context of livestock production and wildlife movement- Classify global livestock management systems- Analyze global patterns of how livestock keeping influences movements of wild mammals- Actively engage in exchange and cooperation within VEBITA’s inter- and transdisciplinary project team- Participate in project meetings and contribute to project reporting- Publish results in international journals in cooperation with the project teamYour profile- MSc degree (or equivalent) for application for a PhD position or PhD degree for application as postdoctoral researcher in a relevant field, e.g., sustainability science, physical geography, ecology or another relevant field- Programming skills (R, Python or similar), familiarity in working with heterogenous datasets and their analysis- Excellent English language skills- Interest in working in an inter- and transdisciplinary project- Interest in applied science at the science-policy interfaceDesirable skills- Experience with stakeholder interactionsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of ethnic or cultural origin, age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion or belief, age, sexual identity or and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application as a single PDF by 19 November 2026, stating the reference number Ref. #11-26021, including:- cover letter describing your motivation to apply for this position- detailed CV- contact details of two potential references- all academic credentials and certificatesPlease submit your application via our online application system. Senckenberg – Leibniz Institution for Biodiversity and Earth System Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at its Department of River Ecology and Conservation in Gelnhausen, starting as soon as possible2 Postdoctoral Researchers (ecologists) (m/f/d)(full-time / part-time)Location: GelnhausenEmployment scope: full-time / part-time options are availableType of contract: limited two years / an extension is be possibleRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) E 13Senckenberg is one of the world’s leading research institutions in the field of Biodiversity and Earth System Research, with eight research institutes and three natural history museums across Germany and scientists from over 40 nations. Our headquarter is located in the thriving commercial metropolis of Frankfurt in the heart of Germany, which also hosts one of our most famous facilities, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum. The location of the available position is in a Senckenberg institute about 40 kilometers east of Frankfurt in Gelnhausen, a historic town accessible via public transport (rail and bus).We are looking for enthusiastic ecologists with a background in broad-scale biodiversity change, community ecology, macroecology, metacommunities, and/or analysis of ecological time series.The two positions are embedded in one or more of the following projects:1. Synthesis Center on Freshwater Biodiversity Change in Europe The Synthesis Center brings together and supports a broad variety of researchers and practitioners investigating a broad variety of fundamental and applied ecological questions, with a particular focus on broad-scale and long-term biodiversity change, community ecology, freshwater ecology, time series analyses, multiple stressor impacts, and conservation (see doi.org/10.1038/s41586-023-06400-1 for an example). Data for > 30,000 freshwater biodiversity time series across 30 European countries have already been compiled from rivers and lakes, covering invertebrates, fish, macrophytes, diatoms, and benthic algae, in collaboration with a large pan-European network of > 200 researchers. Positions involved in this project are expected to pursue similar questions using the already available data.2. EU Horizon Europe project BEAGLE (started on 1st October 2026)BEAGLE (Biodiversity methods for advanced monitoring at large scales) is an EU-funded project using new technology to enhance biodiversity monitoring across terrestrial, freshwater, and marine environments. Specifically, the project uses sensors, environmental DNA (eDNA) and AI, as well as citizen science to collect large-scale and high-quality biodiversity data across a consortium of 17 partners. Positions involved in this project will focus on several tasks, including European-scale biodiversity data mobilization activities (e.g., tracking down datasets and preparing them for use), and the learning and deployment of field-based methods for data collection (e.g., Malaise traps). Participating researchers will gain experience in broad-scale biodiversity data collection and management, biodiversity monitoring, and participation in European-scale research networks.Your tasks• Contributing scientifically to one or more of the above-described projects (you can indicate a preference in your application if you have one)• Analyzing spatial and temporal biodiversity data, and accompanied environmental data, to elucidate spatial patterns and temporal trends and drivers thereof• Preparing scientific manuscripts• Attending project meetings and preparing project reports• Mentoring graduate students• Giving oral presentations at national and international conferences• Attending virtual and physical project meetingsYour profile• PhD in Ecology or a related field• Solid background in fields related to the above expected tasks for a given project or projects.• Advanced skills in statistical analyses, using R• Skills in project management and report writing are preferred but not essential• Strong publication record for your current career level• Excellent written and oral communication and project presentation skills in EnglishWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. jobs.description: Create your own happiness!Are you a passionate early childhood educator (m/f/d)? Do you put your heart and soul into your work, but haven’t been satisfied with your working conditions so far?Come check us out—maybe you’ll like what you find here?What you can look forward to…The basics: pay, vacation time, and working hours.We are actually offering a fixed-term full-time position. The full-time workweek is 38 hours. Initially, the contract would be fixed-term, but an extension is possible.Pay is based on the TVöD SuE collective bargaining agreement and depends on your professional experience and qualifications. A 13th month’s salary (at 100%, instead of 85%) is paid after one year of service. We have between 32 and 34 days of vacation per year. Christmas Eve and New Year’s Eve are paid holidays. The cost of an HVV/Deutschlandticket is fully covered, and if interested, you can participate in a fitness program.The Position: Responsibilities and Working Conditions.We are looking for at least one new early childhood educator with a perfect command of the English language.Your responsibilities include the attentive care, nurturing, and support of the children (age 1-6) entrusted to us in line with our educational approach, working closely with the children, parents, and the entire team. In your daily work, you would speak mainly English.We would appreciate at least some experience in this field and a preference for this age group would be advantageous.Our working conditions are truly worth highlighting: In the elementary section, four colleagues together care for 35 children; in the nursery section, four additional colleagues care for 16 children. In addition, we employ a housekeeping staff member with educational qualifications and, in the future, a substitute.We hold weekly team meetings to discuss weekly schedules, activities, and specific situations, as well as to plan parent-teacher conferences and developmental meetings. Our sponsoring organization places great emphasis on providing good working conditions.The Team: One for all, all for one!Some of us have been working together successfully and happily for over ten years. It goes without saying that we support one another and treat each other with care. Our sense of humor and our willingness to stand up for one another carry us through the sometimes hectic daily routine of the daycare center.On concept days, we discuss educational topics, engage in professional development, and reflect on our work. Regular weekly team meetings, preparation time, and supervision are just as much a part of our routine as extended get-togethers during company outings and Christmas parties.Has this piqued your curiosity? Then you should definitely keep reading…Important: Empathy, joy, and qualifications.To ensure we comply with legal requirements, it is very important that our new team member holds a completed, state-recognized qualification as an early childhood educator (m/f/d), a degree in early childhood education or early childhood development, or a degree as a social pedagogue (m/f/d). It would be helpful if you have a good understanding of the English language, as we are a bilingual facility.We are looking for an empathetic person with a Reggio Emilia approach (including a child-centered perspective) and someone who genuinely enjoys working with children, because we want you to look forward to coming to work.Feel free to get to know us!The Daycare Center: Location. Concept. Focus Areas.The daycare center is located in the heart of Planten un Blomen and is surrounded by plenty of greenery. It is easily accessible by public transportation from all parts of Hamburg (Gänsemarkt, Dammtor, Stephansplatz).There are two groups, a nursery group and an elementary group, in which 42-48 children are currently cared for by nine early childhood educators. Our facilities allow us to organize various projects and activities in workshops and specialized rooms.The foundation of our concept is the Reggio approach. Above all, it reflects our attitude toward others and how we wish to approach life’s changes. Our daycare is a place for self-directed, holistic learning, and we foster a respectful approach not only toward the children entrusted to us, but toward all people.We integrate key areas such as yoga, woodworking, art studio work, language development, music, relaxation and movement, and preschool preparation into our daily routine. Do you have a particular focus? A passion? Let’s find out together if we can integrate this into our daily routine as well…Start up initiative: Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.Our small operator, “Kindertagesstätte an der Bucerius Law School e.V.”, was founded in 2008 and is a member of the Paritätischer Wohlfahrtsverband Hamburg. Loki Schmidt was the founding patron of our daycare center.Our organization consists of a single facility. This means that decisions can be made and implemented quickly, easily, and on an individual basis. Here, people are still allowed to be people; they are heard and are not just a personnel number.As a member of the Bucerius family and an initiative of the ZEIT STIFTUNG BUCERIUS, our work makes an important contribution to promoting an open, democratic society.The Future: Do you think we’re a good fit for you?Then please send us your application materials. We would love to get to know you.If you’re interested, feel free to check out our website (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita (https://www.law-school.de/services/kita) ) or our Instagram account (kita.buceriuslaw).Thank you for your attention, and we hope to see you soon!

jobs.description: Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX projectSenckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position in the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Center (SDMC) at the Senckenberg Research Institute and Natural History Museum Frankfurt, starting as soon as possible:Full-Stack Software Developer (m/f/d): TETTRIX project(Full-Time / Part-Time)Location: FrankfurtEmployment scope: Full-Time / Part-Time options are availableType of contract: Temporary, initially limited to 2 yearsRemuneration: Collective agreement of the state Hesse (TV-H) / E11- E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The city of Frankfurt, where the Senckenberg Society was originally founded, hosts the organization’s central administrative services along with two research institutes housing extensive scientific collections and one of Senckenberg’s most renowned institutions, the Senckenberg Natural History Museum Frankfurt. Senckenberg is as much a part of the city’s identity as its skyline and its traditional apple wine.The position is within the Geobiodiversity Information and Data Management team of the Senckenberg Data and Modelling Centre and contributes to a project funded by the European Union, TETTRIX – TETTRIs neXt level for the taxonomy of tomorrow. The team works at the interface of biodiversity informatics, ecological modelling, and data management, focusing on integrating, analysing, and making biodiversity data accessible for research and conservation. The TETTRIX project aims to strengthen taxonomic capacity for biodiversity research by developing, validating, and scaling innovative tools, workflows, services, and training pathways, while addressing critical knowledge and capacity gaps across Europe. Within the TETTRIX project, the position will develop a web-based, open-access biodiversity mapping and Species Distribution Modelling (SDM) platform that enables reproducible data and modelling workflows and transforms biodiversity data into actionable knowledge for biodiversity monitoring and conservation. The role combines full-stack software development with biodiversity data integration and close collaboration with researchers and technical partners.Your tasks- Develop the platform's web application end-to-end: SPA frontend (interactive map, species/variable selection, model-run monitoring) and REST API backend.- Integrate the application with the PostgreSQL/PostGIS metadata layer and the AWS-side batch and data-lake services.- Co-design and implement the data infrastructure of the Open Modular SDM Platform, including a columnar lakehouse (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask on AWS Batch) covering the full GBIF and OBIS datasets.- Develop and operate the hybrid infrastructure, integrating AWS-based services with the institute's internal serving layer (PostgreSQL/PostGIS, map tiles and APIs), and coordinate the associated technical tasks.- Implement map-tile serving, caching and optimise frontend performance.- Set up and maintain CI/CD, automated tests and containerised deployment (Docker) in cooperation with central IT.- Participate in project and team meetings and coordinate closely with the scientific team on a day-to-day basis.Your profile- Degree in Computer Science or comparable practical experience.- Solid skills in TypeScript/JavaScript and a modern framework (React, Vue or similar).- Backend experience in Python (e.g. FastAPI/Flask) or Node.js; sound REST API design.- Experience with SQL/PostgreSQL; PostGIS and web-mapping libraries (MapLibre GL, Leaflet, OpenLayers) are a strong plus.- Experience with cloud-based data infrastructure, particularly AWS services (S3, Batch).- Knowledge of columnar data storage and lakehouse technologies (Parquet, DuckDB, Dask).- Experience with data pipelines, batch processing and the integration of large-scale datasets.- Knowledge of hybrid infrastructure architectures and the integration of cloud-based and on-premises services.- Experience with Docker, Git and CI/CD.- Very good command of English.- Willingness to work on site in Frankfurt (up to 40% remote work is possible).Desirable skills- Familiarity with open-access biodiversity databases such as the Global Biodiversity Information Facility (GBIF) and the Ocean Biodiversity Information System (OBIS), Darwin Core standards, and biodiversity data life cycles- Familiarity with species distribution modelling and associated statistical/machine-learning approaches (e.g. GLM/GAM, MaxEnt, Random Forest)- A track record in scientific publications, reproducible scientific computing, or open-source projectsWe offer- access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- an attractive job within the inspired and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution- flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. The Max Planck Society is Germany's premier research organization. The 86 Max Planck Institutes conduct research at highest levels, in the service of the general public, in the natural sciences, life sciences, social sciences, and the humanities.The Max Planck Institute for the Structure and Dynamics of Matter (MPSD) is located at the Science Campus Hamburg-Bahrenfeld and investigates dynamical phenomena within matter down to the elementary timescales of atomic and electronic motions, the femtosecond or attosecond timescale. The focus is on the use of short wavelength ultrafast probes, such as X-rays or electron pulses, which are capable of measuring atomic and electronic structures in matter of all kinds.The MPSD currently consists of five scientific departments focusing on solid state physics and theoretical methods in these fields. The MPSD is a partner in the Center for Free-Electron Laser Science (CFEL), collaborating with the Deutsches Elektronen Synchrotron (DESY), European XFEL (EuXFEL) and the University of Hamburg in the development of science based on the X-ray Free Electron Lasers (XFELs).To strengthen our support for experimental research, the MPSD is seeking a highly motivatedElectronics Engineer (m/f/d)Your positionAs an Electronics Engineer, you will support cutting-edge experimental physics research by developing reliable, high-performance electronic systems in close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff.- Develop, design and implement analogue and digital electronic systems for experimental physics applications.- Translate scientific and technical requirements into robust electronic concepts, circuits and complete devices.- Design, assemble, commission and test printed circuit boards (PCBs) and electronic instruments, from initial concept through prototyping to deployment in the laboratory.- Diagnose, troubleshoot and optimise existing electronic systems and measurement equipment.- Develop firmware for microcontrollers and support the integration of hardware, firmware and software components.- Work closely with researchers and engineers to provide practical, user-oriented technical solutions for a broad range of experimental setups.- Prepare and maintain technical documentation, including circuit diagrams, PCB layouts, assembly instructions and test procedures.- As the role involves hands-on development, assembly, testing and support of laboratory equipment, regular on-site presence is an essential part of the position.Your background and skills- A university degree (Master’s degree or Diplom) in electrical engineering, electronics or a closely related field.- Sound practical experience in the development of analogue and digital electronic systems, including circuit design, PCB layout and the assembly, commissioning and testing of electronic devices.- Proficiency in common ECAD tools for schematic capture and PCB design, ideally including KiCad or Autodesk EAGLE, as well as familiarity with circuit-simulation tools.- Knowledge of firmware development for microcontrollers, ideally using C/C++. Experience in developing user software for the control, operation and monitoring of electronic devices is also desirable.- Experience with FPGA development and VHDL is an advantage. Familiarity with CAD systems for mechanical design is also desirable.- A strong understanding of the requirements and working practices of a diverse scientific and technical environment, combined with intercultural competence and effective communication skills.- Excellent written and spoken German and English skills.- Experience in laboratory electronics, measurement technology, scientific instrumentation or experimental physics is desirable.Our offer- A varied and responsible position in an international and interdisciplinary scientific environment, with the opportunity to contribute directly to innovative experimental research.- Close collaboration with scientists, engineers and technical staff on challenging and diverse technical projects.- A family-friendly working environment with flexible working arrangements, in line with the practical requirements of laboratory-based work.- Opportunities for professional development and further training.- Attractive remuneration and social benefits in accordance with the applicable public-sector collective agreement, depending on qualifications and professional experience.- An initial contract for two years, with the possibility of permanent employment thereafter.- The opportunity to work in a collaborative, inclusive and forward-looking research environment.- A subsidy for the Profiticket as a Germany ticketYour applicationThe Max Planck Society strives for gender equality and diversity. jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN), headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years; the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum program. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleaguesYour tasks- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.- Secure external research funds.- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programs of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.Your profile - Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team- Very good command of German (B2)- Fluency in English, both spoken and written- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstancesDesirable skills - Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology- Knowledge in research data management and databases- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum workWe offer - Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card  with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement  – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply? Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/.For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/ (https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/)For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.de (http://www.senckenberg.de)Contact Senckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.Homeoffice:Umfang: Maximal 40%

jobs.occupation: 23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany, offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science covering physics, chemistry and biology.23 Interdisciplinary PhD positions in Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials – IMPRS UFAST – HamburgResearchThe program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. The use of ultrafast imaging over the relevant length and time scales generates new levels of understanding of the interplay between structure and dynamics. Specific areas include the theoretical and experimental aspects of quantum materials and atomically resolved dynamics, fundamental light-matter interaction, accelerator-based light sources, coherent controlled molecular and solid state dynamics, molecular imaging, extreme timescale spectroscopy, ultrafast optics and X-ray scienceWe offer:- A range of PhD positions in these areas: open positions (https://www.mpsd.mpg.de/350422/open_phd_projects)- State-of-the-art research facilities on an extensive science campus- Cross-disciplinary research in a vibrant, international scientific environment- First class supervision and mentorship by a team of internationally renowned experts- Outstanding training in your scientific subject and transferable skills (in English)- A 3-year employment contract based on the German federal pay agreementRequirementsWe seek applicants with an excellent academic background. jobs.occupation: W2 Professorship “Sustainable Freight Transport Systems and Transport Logistics" (Ingenieur/in - Verkehrswesen)
jobs.description: W2 Professorship “Sustainable Freight Transport Systems and Transport Logistics"Application deadline:30.12.2026Date of hire:as soon as possibleVacancy number:39565We are seeking an academically outstanding individual (m/f/d) who will make an independent inter- and transdisciplinary contribution to research in the field of sustainable freight transport systems and logistics. The content focus is at the intersection of value chains, freight transport, and sustainable production systems. The professorship shall connect and strengthen the sustainability-related systems analytical topics at the Kassel Institute for Sustainability and the transportation science topics in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Moreover, there is an aim to foster networking in the fields of supply chains and intralogistics with the relevant departments of Economics and Mechanical Engineering. This is intended to further the interdisciplinary interaction between technical and societal research approaches and to advance the research focus on sustainable transformation at the University of Kassel.The professorship should focus on at least one of the following topics:1. Systemic analysis of the interdependencies between freight transport systems, trade, and economic development: Origin of freight transport, economic and ecological evaluation of interregional division of labor, interactions between infrastructure (e.g., rail), regional production clusters and division of labor, as well as sustainable design of these relationships.2. Modeling of the freight transport system: Development and application of scenarios and models for the origin, development, and management of freight transport, infrastructure development and the associated policy instruments, as well as the advancement of corresponding methods.3. Development and application of comprehensive approaches for sustainability evaluation of the ecological, social, and economic effects of strategies and interventions in freight transport, as well as, based on these, the design of a sustainable freight transport system.Experience in the collection, analysis, and management of data in the context of the transformation towards a sustainable freight transport system is also desirable, including the consideration of AI methods: development of data collection procedures and methods of data analysis and data-driven forecasts based on statistical and AI methods, issues regarding the (public) availability and use of data.In teaching, the professorship should supplement and enhance existing degree programs in the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, and to develop new or emerging study programs with a focus on sustainability. Teaching responsibilities are to be divided, with 50% in sustainability-related degree programs and 50% in offerings within the Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering. Some courses must be taught in English. It is expected that the appointee, especially regarding official duties in teaching and academic self-administration, will acquire sufficient proficiency in the German language in due course, if not already possessed.The main location for the professorship will be at the Kassel Institute for Sustainability.Special notes: The department aims to increase the proportion of female professors and expressly encourages female scientists to apply.The requirements for appointment and performance are in accordance with §§ 67, 68 HessHG. Specifically, a completed, qualified doctorate as well as a habilitation or equivalent additional academic achievements, as evidenced by scientific publications, are required. You should also possess pedagogical aptitude and commitment to academic teaching, as well as a pronounced willingness for interdisciplinary collaboration.Please submit a curriculum vitae, certificates, diplomas, a list of scientific works, three selected publications, a research and teaching concept (maximum three pages each), as well as a list of previous courses taught, existing teaching evaluations, and any higher education didactic trainings with your application. Additionally, please submit a brief concept (maximum three pages) outlining your ideas for a professional and institutional connection to the Kassel Institute for Sustainability.For questions, please contact Prof. Dr. Angela Francke, Tel.: +49 561 804-7703, Email: angela.francke(at)uni-kassel.de. We kindly ask you to submit the complete application documents as a single PDF document via the University of Kassel's application portal.

German is an asset but not required.Our offerWe are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. jobs.occupation: PhD Position on Femtosecond Spectroscopy of Chiral Molecular Ions (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Job available in 2 locations: Kassel, BremenWork ScheduleStandard (Mon-Fri)Environmental ConditionsOfficeJob DescriptionA PhD position is available in Germany within the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network TRILOGY, funded under Horizon Europe. The selected doctoral candidate will work on an interdisciplinary research project focused on ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions, combining expertise in physics, chemistry, engineering, mass spectrometry, and ultrafast science.The position is offered through a collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific. The doctoral researcher will be employed by Thermo Fisher Scientific for the full three-year duration of the PhD project. The doctoral thesis will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jochen Mikosch at the University of Kassel. During the first 24 months, the doctoral researcher will be based at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen, Germany. This will be followed by an 12-month research period at the University of Kassel.About the TRILOGY Doctoral NetworkTRILOGY is a Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network advancing research in the emerging field of ultrafast chirality. The network aims to exploit attosecond light-driven electron dynamics to overcome limitations associated with conventional chiroptical methods.The research targets potential applications in life sciences and advanced technologies, with the goal of developing next-generation, highly sensitive spectroscopic tools for studying chiral molecules.The network brings together institutions and partners from across Europe and will train 16 doctoral candidates at the intersection of experimental and theoretical ultrafast science. Researchers will work in an interdisciplinary environment spanning physics, chemistry, engineering, and related areas while gaining experience through collaboration between academia and industry.The PhD project in Germany contributes to the TRILOGY work package focused on the design, development, and testing of an instrument for chiral photoelectron spectroscopy of molecular ions.About the PhD ProjectThe selected candidate will conduct research on the ultrafast spectroscopy of chiral molecular ions.The project will involve close collaboration between the University of Kassel and Thermo Fisher Scientific, a company active in the field of mass spectrometry.During the first approximately 24 months, the main workplace will be at Thermo Fisher Scientific in Bremen. The researcher will work on adapting an electrospray ion source and related instrumentation.The researcher will subsequently relocate to the University of Kassel to perform experiments involving chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses. The experiments will use a novel momentum spectrometer ion target developed at the University of Kassel together with the ion source developed in collaboration with Thermo Fisher Scientific.Key Research Activities- The doctoral candidate will take a leading role in several research and technical activities, including:- Adapting the hardware and software of a high-resolution Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer equipped with an electrospray ion source and radiofrequency-based ion trap or ion accumulation system.- Developing an ion guide transfer system for extracting molecular ions to an external spectrometer.- Establishing protocols for producing and accumulating negatively charged chiral molecular ions of pharmaceutical relevance.- Conducting ion-optical simulations to optimize ion trap performance and improve ion accumulation efficiency.- Integrating the experimental control systems of the adapted Orbitrap Mass Spectrometer and the home-built momentum spectrometer at the University of Kassel.- Performing, analyzing, interpreting, and publishing Photoelectron Circular Dichroism (PECD) photo-detachment experiments involving negatively charged chiral molecular ions and femtosecond laser pulses.- Exploring opportunities to translate fundamental research in atomic, molecular, and optical physics into real-world applications.- The selected researcher will also collaborate closely with international partners across the TRILOGY consortium and undertake two funded research stays with partner organizations within the network.- Through the program, the doctoral candidate will have opportunities to strengthen their research profile through scientific publications, conference presentations, collaborative project activities, and interaction with academic and industrial researchers across Europe.Candidate ProfileApplicants should have:- A Master's degree or equivalent in physics, engineering, chemistry, or a related discipline.- A strong interest in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, and scientific instrumentation.- A strong background in atomic, molecular, and optical physics.- Proven experience with experimental laboratory research in one of the following fields: Femtosecond lasers, Ion transfer optics / ion traps, Charged particle detection- Excellent written and spoken English.- Good written and oral communication skills.- An interest in conducting experimental and theoretical research within an interdisciplinary research environment.- Previous experience in chirality, molecular ions, ultrafast optics, or instrumentation will be considered an advantage.- Experience with Python programming is also preferred.MSCA Mobility and Eligibility RequirementsAs the position is funded through the MSCA Doctoral Network, applicants must meet the relevant eligibility requirements.Applicants must satisfy the MSCA mobility rule. In general, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or studies, in Germany for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Certain exceptions may apply under MSCA rules.Applicants must also be doctoral candidates and must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.Candidates are encouraged to carefully verify their eligibility under the applicable MSCA Doctoral Network conditions before applying.Application DocumentsApplications should include:- Cover letter- Detailed curriculum vitae- Academic transcripts- Copy of the Master's thesis- Scientific publication, if available- Applicants may also optionally include one letter of recommendation.Selection ProcessCandidates will initially be pre-selected based on their qualifications, experience, and suitability for the research project.Shortlisted applicants may then be invited to an online or in-person interview involving representatives from the academic and industrial partners participating in the project.Key InformationPosition: PhD Researcher / Doctoral CandidateNumber of positions: 1Research areas: Physics, Engineering, ChemistryResearcher profile: First Stage Researcher (R1)Contract: Temporary, full-timeWorking hours: 35 hours per weekCountry: GermanyWork locations: Bremen and KasselFunding: Horizon Europe – Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral NetworkProject: TRILOGYMarie Curie Grant Agreement: 101226887If you are interested, please apply online with your CV and Motivation Letter.At Thermo Fisher Scientific, each one of our 100,000 extraordinary minds has a unique story to tell. Join us and contribute to our singular mission—enabling our customers to make the world healthier, cleaner and safer.Thermo Fisher Scientific is an EEO/Affirmative Action Employer and does not discriminate on the basis of  , color, religion, ___ ,   orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability or any other legally protected status.Apply today! http://jobs.thermofisher.com (http://jobs.thermofisher.com)

Your applicationPlease submit a cover letter describing your motivation and relevant research experience, a CV, academic certificates/transcripts, and contact details of two referees via the UMG application portal. Please indicate relevant programming projects or publications where applicable.We look forward to receiving your application!Travel and application expenses cannot be reimbursed.Your tasks•  Design and perform multielectrode in vivo electrophysiological recordings from the inferior colliculus of the Mongolian gerbil.•  Develop and validate computational and data-driven models of auditory information processing and optogenetically evoked neural responses.•  Integrate experimental measurements into a digital-twin framework and assess model generalization, uncertainty and biological plausibility.•  Design and optimize sound-processing algorithms that map acoustic signals to spatial and temporal optical stimulation patterns, and benchmark their performance in vivo and in silico.•  Collaborate with experimental neuroscientists and engineers; present and publish scientific findings and contribute to interdisciplinary project meetings.Your qualifications•  Completed MSc or equivalent in neuroscience, biomedical/electrical engineering, biology, physics or a related field.•  Enthusiasm for in vivo electrophysiology. No prior in vivo experience is required; full training in electrophysiological techniques will be provided.•  Good programming skills (preferably MATLAB/Python) and experience in signal processing, scientific computing or machine learning.•  Strong analytical skills, curiosity about biological systems and enthusiasm for developing experimental and computational research.•  Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in an interdisciplinary, international team; very good written and spoken English.•  Knowledge of auditory neuroscience, PyTorch/JAX or computational neuroprosthetics is an advantage but not a prerequisite.We offer•  A scientifically ambitious PhD project at the interface of in vivo electrophysiology, computational modeling and optogenetic neurotechnology for future hearing restoration.•  Close interaction with teams at IAN and EKFZ-OT developing optical cochlear implants, with access to complementary experimental, computational and engineering expertise.•  An internationally connected Göttingen Campus research environment, opportunities for doctoral training at the Göttingen Graduate Center for Neuroscience, Biophysics and Molecular Biosciences.•  Support for scientific publications, professional development and participation in collaborative research networks and training academies.•  Employment and social benefits in accordance with the applicable TV-L regulations; final contract conditions to be specified.This PhD project is funded by CAIMed (Lower Saxony Center for AI and Causal Methods in Medicine) and will contribute to the Göttingen program developing optical cochlear implants for future hearing restoration.The goal is to establish an experimentally grounded digital twin of the auditory system and use it to generate, optimize, and benchmark sound-coding strategies for optogenetic stimulation of the auditory nerve. Combining in vivo electrophysiology, computational neuroscience, and generative modeling, the project investigates how acoustic signals can be transformed into spatiotenporal light patterns for stimulation via the optical cochlear implant under development at IAN and EKFZ-OT.

jobs.description: Become a part of our journey and join the Constructor Community as:PhD Researcher (m/f/d): AI for Semantic Structures, Reasoning Flows & Personalized Content GenerationYou are expected to contribute to the development of internationally visible, foundational research in AI-driven semantic structure extraction, automated reasoning-flow modeling, and adaptive content generation. The research focuses on methods for analyzing and representing deep semantic and pedagogical structures in scientific and educational materials; high-fidelity extraction of conceptual and reasoning blocks; inference-time rationale generation; and adaptive, learner-aware sequencing of content. This includes work on semantic parsing, structured NLP, graph-based neural models, metacognitive prompting, ontology alignment across disciplines, and human-in-the-loop optimization.In this context, interdisciplinary research is strongly encouraged—particularly collaborations spanning computer science, computational linguistics, cognitive science, and the learning sciences. You will contribute to developing datasets, baseline models, personalized learning engines, reasoning-graph representations, cross-domain mapping algorithms, and RLHF-style feedback loops that improve system interpretability and instructional quality. The successful candidate will also contribute to high-quality publications, release research prototypes, and support demonstrator systems that deliver structured semantic extraction, rationale-aware content generation, and cross-domain transfer of reasoning structures.Additionally, the successful candidate is expected to support teaching activities in areas such as Machine Learning, Natural Language Processing, AI in Education, Knowledge Representation, and Python-based analytical seminars at the BSc, MSc, and PhD levels. Responsibilities include assisting in course delivery, advising students, supervising Bachelor/Master theses, and engaging in methodological innovation for online, hybrid, and in-person learning environments. The university provides strong support for early-career researchers, including mentorship, administrative assistance, access to computational resources, conference funding, and opportunities to collaborate with other research groups and industrial partners working at the intersection of AI and digital education.Your Profile- Master’s or PhD degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Machine Learning, Computational Linguistics, or a related field.- Strong research interest and practical experience in one or more of the following areas: - jobs.occupation: PhD positions - Statistical Physics and Active Matter - (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: In the Department of Living Matter Physics (LMP) we seek to fill a number ofPhD positions.- Statistical Physics and Active Matter -The Max Planck Institute for Dynamics and Self-Organization (MPI-DS) at Göttingen, Germany, is an international, interdisciplinary and collaborative environment offering an exceptional research setting. It hosts a range of theoretical and experimental fundamental scientific research and a diverse group of researchers. Altogether, it employs about 300 people. The LMP department engages in a wide range of theoretical research aimed at understanding the dynamics of living systems from a physical perspective. The department is headed by Ramin Golestanian and hosts a number of group leaders, postdoctoral researchers, students, and visitors.The researchThe PhD students will engage in theoretical and/or computational research in Nonequilibrium Statistical Physics and Active Matter, under the supervision of Ramin Golestanian. For more information concerning our current areas of research activity, visit our website (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp (http://www.ds.mpg.de/lmp) ).Your profileWe are looking for excellent, enthusiastic and self-motivated early-career researchers with good communication skills to join our research team. The PhD candidate should have:- A Master’s degree (or comparable) in theoretical physics, applied mathematics or related disciplines from a recognized university;- Strong interest in nonequilibrium statistical physics and the physics of living systems across scales;- Ability and desire to work in an international team on inter-disciplinary research topics;- Good command of English, which is the working language of the department. German is an asset but not required.Our offerWe are offering excellent working conditions in a highly interdisciplinary and stimulating research environment. Salary and working hours are in accordance with the funding guidelines of the Max Planck Society for junior scientists. Working hours are fulltime; salary is 2/3 of E13 TVöD-Bund. Furthermore, we offer opportunities regarding work life balance as well as health promotion services. The PhD position is limited to three years. The starting date is flexible.The Max-Planck Society is committed to achieving the highest level of excellence and diversity. We encourage applications from women, especially in areas where they are underrepresented, which includes theoretical physics. Moreover, we are committed to providing suitable working environment for everyone including individuals with disabilities.Your applicationTo apply, please follow this link (https://jobs.b-ite.com/en/jobposting/64bbb9935c7fc269f86d9f96bf4a8e06636784110/apply)  and submit your CV, your academic records, a statement of your research interests, and contacts of two referees. Processing of applications will start after the deadline of 1st December 2026. While we may continue to receive applications until 1st April 2027, the positions will be filled as soon as suitable candidates are identified. Therefore, you are encouraged to apply as soon as possible.For questions, please contact:Prof. Dr. Ramin Golestanian Tel. +49 551 5176-100Email: golestanian-office@ds.mpg.de (https://mailto:golestanian-office@ds.mpg.de)  Max Planck Institute forDynamics and Self-OrganizationProf. Dr. Ramin GolestanianAm Faßberg 1737077 GöttingenGermanyErgänzende Informationen:Anforderungen an den Bewerber: Expertenkenntnisse: Physik, Theoretische Physik
