jobs.description: Job posting no. 20261009The GWDG is seeking aStorage Expert (m/f/d)to join an interdisciplinary team of HPC experts in the working group “Computing” (AG C) with a regular working week of 39 hours (100%). Remuneration is in accordance with the collective agreement for the German public service (federal government); depending on qualifications, the position will be grade TVöD E 13. The position is suitable for part-time work and initially limited till 31rd December 2029. The GWDG strives for long-term cooperation. If interested, there is the possibility of a doctorate.The Gesellschaft für wissenschaftliche Datenverarbeitung mbH Göttingen (GWDG) is the university computing center for the Georg-August-Universität Göttingen and a computing and IT competence center for the Max Planck Society. The provision of high-performance HPC systems has been one of its tasks for over 40 years. In 2020, the University of Göttingen / GWDG was accepted as one of eight computing centers in the National High-Performance Computing (NHR) network. The GWDG operates the HLRN-IV system “Emmy”, one of the most powerful computers in the world.As a national supercomputing center, the GWDG offers technical support to researchers and students from various science domains using sophisticated computer codes, including earth system science, life science, and engineering. We also participate in both national and international research projects. At the same time, we aim to improve our close collaboration with the German Aerospace Center (DLR), and specialized computing centers including the German Climate Computing Center (DKRZ) and the Institute for Advanced Simulation Jülich (IAS-JSC).As part of our AI Service Center for Sensitive and Critical Infrastructure (KISSKI) we have created a number of AI-based services that offer high levels of security and privacy due to being processed on our own hardware. The position will be located within the subproject “KISSKI-EvoKS” and closely collaborate with customers from SMEs and Startups to develop prototypes and workflows that lead to PoCs and Blueprints. Those customers will come predominantly from sectors with high data protection requirements.The GWDG together with the Faculty of Mathematics and Computer Science and the Campus Institute Data Science (CIDAS) of the University of Göttingen provides a stimulating research environment in Scientific Computing, with an opportunity to conduct research in the intersection of applied computer science, High-Performance Computing, AI, and Machine Learning.ResponsibilitiesWe have a wide range of potential responsibilities that we would like to discuss with you. Your responsibilities in our team could include, for example:- Design, implement, and optimize high-performance storage solutions tailored for AI and HPC workloads- Conduct research on scalable, cost-effective storage architectures suitable for AI training and HPC simulations in resource-constrained environments- Develop and deploy data management strategies for large-scale AI datasets, including data lifecycle management, versioning, backup, and security (e.g., GDPR-compliant data handling)- Investigate and prototype AI-optimized storage systems leveraging technologies such as NVMe, SSD caching, and distributed storage (e.g., Ceph, MinIO, Lustre)- Support SMEs in evaluating and selecting appropriate HPC and AI storage solutions- Collaborate with data scientists and engineers to ensure storage systems meet the demands of AI model training, inference, and real-time processing- Develop best practice guidelines and toolkits for SMEs to manage AI/HPC data efficiently and security- Provide technical advisory and training to SME teams on data storage, performance monitoring, and data governance- Monitor and benchmark storage performance, ensuring low latency, high throughput, and cost-efficiency for AI/HPC applicationsRequirements- Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Data Science, or a related field- Experience in HPC systems, storage infrastructure, and AI data engineering- Proven experience with high-performance storage technologies (e.g., Lustre, GPFS, Ceph, NFS, S3-compatible storage)- Strong knowledge of AI/ML data pipelines, including data ingestion, preprocessing, and model training workflows- Hands-on experience with containerization (Docker, Kubernetes) and orchestration tools in HPC/AI environments- Familiarity with cloud storage platforms- Experience in data lifecycle management, data versioning, and metadata management- Solid understanding of data security, privacy (GDPR), and compliance in AI applications- Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills- Excellent communication skills and ability to translate technical concepts for non-technical stakeholders- Very good German skills (C1)- Very good English skills (C1)- Willingness to travel on businessDesirable- Experience in research or innovation projects related to HPC, AI, or data infrastructure- Knowledge of AI-driven storage optimization (e.g., predictive data placement, auto-tiering)- Familiarity with open-source HPC/AI frameworks (e.g., Slurm, Singularity, MLflow, Kubeflow)- Proficiency in scripting languages (Python, Bash) and system administration (Linux/UNIX)Our offer- Flexible working hours and opportunity for mobile working- A modern, diverse, and exceptional work environment with close proximity to academia and research at the intersection of several innovative technology sectors- An interesting, versatile job in a large, internationally operating IT competence center- Collaboration in a competent and committed team- Qualification and further development of your skills- Social benefits of the public sectorYour applicationHave we sparked your interest? Then please send us your application by 08.11.2026 via our online form:Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: About usAirbus pioneers sustainable aerospace for a safe and united world. The Company constantly innovates to provide efficient and technologically-advanced solutions in aerospace, defence, and connected services. In commercial aircraft, Airbus offers modern and fuel-efficient airliners and associated services. In helicopters, Airbus provides the most efficient civil and military rotorcraft solutions and services worldwide.Job descriptionIn order to support the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department, Airbus Operations is looking for aMaster student (d/f/m) in the field of Aerodynamics in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics departmentYou are looking for a master thesis and want to get to know the work of a job title? Then apply now! We look forward to you supporting us in the Gust Loads & Aeroelastics department as a master student (d/f/m)!- Location: Hamburg- Start: 01.06.2025- Duration: 6 monthsYour opportunity- Are you passionate about aircraft physics?- Are you keen to master the way we compute external loads acting on the vehicle due to maneuvers, flight in turbulence, landing impact, ground-handling?- Do you like to work in an empowered manner?- Do you enjoy connecting people and collaborating with many different interfaces?- This job will give you the opportunity to work internationally with several internal flight physics departments and with teams located in Europe and India.About usWe are a team of 16 multicultural and passionate engineers who perform the gust calculations for overall aircraft design for all aircraft types. Our team is involved from a very early design stage until certification and also in-service support. We are responsible for running build model activities such as finite element modeling, creating mass and aerodynamics models. We perform gust loads calculation, including failure cases, and deliver to internal interfaces. On top, we are deeply involved in research and technology aspects with new aircraft configuration assessments, model based system engineering, automation and machine learning.IntroductionThe current industry approaches of modeling unsteady aerodynamic flow for the prediction of gust loads typically assume linear flow conditions. Linearity greatly reduces the computational time required to evaluate all the flight points and gust conditions required by the certification specifications (CS-25). At the same time, disregarding non-linearities such as boundary layer separation arising from the high angles of attack induced by strong gusts can lead to an over-estimation of loads and thus to an increased structural weight of the aircraft.Your locationYou will be working at the largest production site for civil aircraft situated in Hamburg. Its location on the southern banks of the river Elbe includes the option to commute by ferry. Experience the special flair of Hamburg in your spare time where vibrant cosmopolitan culture meets nautic legacy.Your benefits- Work-life balance with a 35-hour week (flexitime).- International environment with the opportunity to network globally.- Work with modern/diversified technologies.- At Airbus, we see you as a valuable team member and you are not hired to brew coffee, instead you are in close contact with the interfaces and are part of our weekly team meetings.- Opportunity to participate in the Generation Airbus Community to expand your own network.Your tasks and responsibilitiesDuring this six months Master thesis you will develop and evaluate an unsteady aerodynamic model that includes the effect of flow separation in a piecewise linear approach. The model will be built using linearized computational fluid dynamics (CFD) of a complete flexible aircraft and adapted using aerodynamic data obtained in the non-linear flow region at high angles of attack. You will evaluate the model by comparison against higher-fidelity models, such as obtained from non-linear time domain simulation, with respect to gust loads.You will contribute to:- Optimize the design of Airbus commercial aircraft in the frame of new wing technologies- the development of new approaches to model unsteady aerodynamics considering non-linearities for gust loads and flutter computation- Actively support us as a new member of our team on our journeyDesired skills and qualifications- You are a fulltime enrolled master student (d/f/m) within Engineering, Mechanical Engineering or equivalent- You have good knowledge in aerodynamics, CFD and potential flows- Ideally you already have first experience in CFD using TAU or CODA- You have knowledge in coding using Python and/or Matlab- You bring basic knowledge in overall aircraft design and basic competencies in flight loads calculation and flight mechanics- You are passionate to understand physical aspects and to use your engineering judgement- If you are familiar with tools like MSC.NASTRAN or ALTAIR HyperWorks, this is beneficial- You are a highly motivated, proactive and open-minded person with a great sense of initiative- You are keen to deepen your technical knowledge while enjoying to work in a multicultural team- Your English is at negotiating levelPlease upload the following documents: cover letter, CV, relevant transcripts, enrollment certificate.Not a 100% match? We are looking to support our rapidly growing team as soon as possible: Postdoctoral Fellow in Computational Cancer Evolution (f/m/x)Department I of Internal Medicine - CECADYour tasksWe are looking for an ambitious postdoctoral researcher with a proven track record in computational cancer evolution to join our Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory at the CECAD Research Center in Cologne. In this role, you will reconstruct the clonal and subclonal architecture of chronic lymphocytic leukemia (CLL) and track its evolution under targeted therapies. Using bulk and single-cell sequencing data, you will infer tumour phylogenies and quantify intratumour heterogeneity, subclonal selection and genomic instability (e.g. copy-number alterations, whole-genome doubling and chromothripsis).You will identify evolutionary trajectories leading to treatment resistance, relapse and Richter transformation. Furthermore, you will develop and apply computational methods based on evolutionary principles and integrate genomic, transcriptomic and spatial data with clinical outcomes. Your analyses will link evolutionary features to treatment response, MRD kinetics and survival.For this work, the lab has access to blood and bone marrow samples from more than 900 patients with CLL treated within prospective clinical trials of the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), including samples taken before treatment and at relapse, linked to detailed clinical and measurable residual disease (MRD) data.You will lead your own projects, contribute to collaborative projects within the lab and with external partners, and co-supervise PhD and Master students.Your profile• A PhD in bioinformatics, computational biology, statistics, physics, computer science or a related field• A proven track record in computational cancer evolution, demonstrated by first-author publications• Hands-on experience in reconstructing clonal and subclonal tumour evolution from sequencing data (e.g. clonal deconvolution, phylogenetic inference, mutational signatures)• Experience in copy-number and structural variant analysis from whole-genome or whole-exome sequencing data; experience with single-cell DNA or RNA sequencing data is a plus• Fluency in Python and/or R, and experience with reproducible workflows (e.g. Snakemake, Nextflow) on high performance computing clusters• Experience with longitudinal or clinical trial data and with haematological malignancies is a plus• Ability to work independently and in close collaboration with clinicians and wet-lab scientists• Excellent communication skills in English, both written and spokenOur offer• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.Your future in detailThe Integrated Cancer Research Laboratory (www.al-sawaf-lab.com), led by Prof Othman Al-Sawaf and based at the CECAD and Department I of Internal Medicine, was founded in 2024 and is funded by a large Emmy-Noether-Grant of the German Research Council (DFG). The focus of the lab is to integrate multimodal analyses to study the plasticity, evolution and prognosis of cancer with a special focus on hematological malignancies. To this end, the lab utilizes a unique biobank with blood and bone marrow samples from patients treated within large (>900 patients) prospective clinical trials. The group is embedded in a network with many local collaborators, including the Collaborative Research Center (CRC) 1530 and the German CLL Study Group (GCLLSG), as well as many national and international partners in academia and industry. Previous work has been frequently cited (Al-Sawaf et al, N Engl J Med 2025; Al-Sawaf et al, Nature Medicine 2024; Al-Sawaf et al, Nature Medicine 2023; see Pubmed) and the aim of the lab is to continue producing highly impactful and patient-relevant results.ContactProf. Dr. Othman Al-SawafTel: +49 221 478-84816Universitätsklinikum Köln AöRGeschäftsbereich PersonalKerpener Str. 6250937 KölnUniklinik Köln Karriere Application deadline: 29 November 2026Job-ID: 3ftptfctWe look forward to receiving your application and getting to know you!

jobs.occupation: Doctoral Fellowship in the fields of Applied Linguistics and Digital Humanities (Germanist/in)
jobs.description: In the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, researchers from the Social Sciences and Humanities as well as artists explore the relationships between technology, science, and society. The Lab was initiated by The Schaufler Foundation together with TUD Dresden University of Technology. The Lab's guiding theme for the upcoming third funding phase (April 2027–September 2030) is "Energy Cultures in Transition". The guiding theme is investigated from a humanities, cultural, social, and educational science perspective, explored through artistic practice, and communicated to the public. For the third funding phase, the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden comprises eight doctoral fellowships and an annually changing Artist in Residence program.TUD embodies a university culture that is characterized by cosmopolitanism, mutual appreciation, thriving innovation and active participation. For TUD, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.The Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden offers, subject to the availability of resources, aDoctoral Fellowshipfor a period of 2 years, with the option of extension by 1.5 years, starting on April 1, 2027. The fellowship (EUR 1,850 per month, plus a grant for material costs of EUR 150 and, where applicable, a family supplement of EUR 315 per child) is aimed at early-career researchers in the fields of Applied Linguistics and Digital Humanities. Primary supervision will be provided by Prof. Dr. Simon Meier-Vieracker, Chair of Applied Linguistics.The guiding theme Energy Cultures in Transition understands energy as a cultural phenomenon deeply inscribed in aesthetic, historical, political, ecological, economic, and socio-technological practices and systems. Building on the dynamically growing research fields of the Energy Humanities, Science & Technology Studies, and the Digital Humanities, the aim is to examine how modern energy regimes—from petromodernity, to nuclear culture, and post-carbon futures—have shaped not only material infrastructures but also subjectivities, power relations, progress narratives, geopolitical orders, ecologies, and knowledge systems, while simultaneously being shaped by them. Interdisciplinary perspectives from the social sciences, cultural studies, humanities, and educational research represented at the Schaufler Kolleg@TU Dresden enable the analysis of the multifaceted entanglements of energy, culture, and society. The focus is on questions concerning the representation, communication, and aesthetics of energy transitions and resource paradigms as well as continuities between resource economies and information economies, the relationships between energy, labor, environment, and consumer culture, and the role of colonialism, gender, nationalism, geopolitics, education, and social justice in deciding energy futures and navigating collective transformation processes. In the fields of Applied Linguistics and Digital Humanities, the following research areas and questions are of particular relevance to the guiding theme:- Discursive negotiations, conceptualisations and metaphorisations of energy relations and energy transformations in various social domains (politics, the economy, technological development, civil society, etc.) and media contexts, including multimodal aspects- Formats, practices and impacts of science communication (analogue and digital) relating to energy-related researchTasks:Your tasks include independent research and academic further qualification with the goal of completing a doctorate at TUD, as well as writing a dissertation on a topic within the guiding concept "Energy Cultures in Transition" in the disciplines of Applied Linguistics or Digital Humanities. The fellowship requires a high degree of willingness to engage in interdisciplinary dialogue, particularly with the STEM partnerships of the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, as well as to conduct joint research with artists within the framework of the Schaufler Residency. In addition, engagement in the areas of science communication and outreach is expected. Shared office spaces will be made available to the fellows. Participation in the Kolleg's English-language training program is mandatory.Requirements:You hold an excellent university degree (Master’s or equivalent) in German Studies, Linguistics, Digital Humanities or a comparable discipline. Furthermore, you have relevant prior experience in the linguistic, cultural or media studies analysis of discourses on environmental, technological or energy-related issues. Experience with digital research methods (such as corpus linguistics, text mining and network analysis) would be an advantage. You have a strong ability to work in teams and enjoy interdisciplinary collaboration. As the training program is conducted in English, you have English skills at a minimum of C1 level. In accordance with the doctoral regulations of the Faculty of Linguistics, Literature and Cultural Studies, the dissertation may be written in either German or English—if you choose to write it in German, corresponding German language skills are required. Beyond this, German language skills are desirable but not mandatory.We offer:The opportunity to pursue a doctorate within the Schaufler Kolleg with a structured qualification program and integration into an interdisciplinary research project. You will receive a fully equipped office workspace on the premises of TUD and access to an excellent research infrastructure, including participation in Research Studios and writing retreats. The Graduate Academy and other central institutions of TUD offer numerous further training and qualification opportunities. In addition, within the limits of the available project funds, the Schaufler Lab will cover the costs of conference travel. Inclusion and equal opportunities are important to us. We therefore look forward to receiving applications from people regardless of gender, origin, sexual orientation, worldview, or disability. TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The University is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment. The fellowship does not constitute an employment relationship.Application:Your detailed application, in German or English, should contain, in addition to the completed online application form (https://tu-dresden.de/gsw/schauflerlab/schaufler-kolleg/phase-3/anmeldung-registration) , a letter of motivation, a curriculum vitae in tabular form including an account of your academic career, a copy of your most recent university degree certificate, an exposé of your research project including a work and time schedule (max. 20,000 characters). Please send us your application documents, including the online application form, quoting the reference number s26-005, by November 24, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de (https://securemail.tu-dresden.de/)  by sending it as a single pdf file to schaufler.lab@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:schaufler.lab@tu-dresden.de) or to:TU Dresden, Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, Prof. Dr. Simon Meier-Vieracker, Helmholtzstr. 10, 01069 Dresden, Germany.Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis (https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis) .

jobs.description: Weitere Berufsbezeichnung:Anthropologie (Studienberuf)Stellenbeschreibung:In the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, researchers from the Social Sciences and Humanities as well as artists explore the relationships between technology, science, and society. The Lab was initiated by The Schaufler Foundation together with TUD Dresden University of Technology. The Lab's guiding theme for the upcoming third funding phase (April 2027–September 2030) is "Energy Cultures in Transition". The guiding theme is investigated from a humanities, cultural, social, and educational science perspective, explored through artistic practice, and communicated to the public. For the third funding phase, the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden comprises eight doctoral fellowships and an annually changing Artist in Residence program.TUD embodies a university culture that is characterized by cosmopolitanism, mutual appreciation, thriving innovation and active participation. For TUD, diversity is an essential feature and a quality criterion of an excellent university. Accordingly, we welcome all applicants who would like to commit themselves, their achievements and productivity to the success of the whole institution.The Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden offers, subject to the availability of resources, aDoctoral Fellowshipfor a period of 2 years, with the option of extension by 1.5 years, starting on April 1, 2027. The fellowship (EUR 1,850 per month, plus a grant for material costs of EUR 150 and, where applicable, a family supplement of EUR 315 per child) is aimed at early-career researchers in the field of Cultural Studies. Primary supervision will be provided by Prof. Dr. Orit Halpern, Chair of Digital Cultures.The guiding theme Energy Cultures in Transition understands energy as a cultural phenomenon deeply inscribed in aesthetic, historical, political, ecological, economic, and socio-technological practices and systems. Building on the dynamically growing research fields of the Energy Humanities, Science & Technology Studies, and the Digital Humanities, the aim is to examine how modern energy regimes—from petromodernity, to nuclear culture, and post-carbon futures—have shaped not only material infrastructures but also subjectivities, power relations, progress narratives, geopolitical orders, ecologies, and knowledge systems, while simultaneously being shaped by them. Interdisciplinary perspectives from the social sciences, cultural studies, humanities, and educational research represented at the Schaufler Kolleg@TU Dresden enable the analysis of the multifaceted entanglements of energy, culture, and society. The focus is on questions concerning the representation, communication, and aesthetics of energy transitions and resource paradigms as well as continuities between resource economies and information economies, the relationships between energy, labor, environment, and consumer culture, and the role of colonialism, gender, nationalism, geopolitics, education, and social justice in deciding energy futures and navigating collective transformation processes. In the field of Cultural Studies, the following research areas and questions are of particular relevance to the guiding theme:- AI and Energy- Histories/STS studies of Finance, Digitalization, and Energy- Energy Infrastructures - Environment, Energy, and Design- Cybernetics and Energy CulturesTasks:Your tasks include independent research and academic further qualification with the goal of completing a doctorate at TUD, as well as writing a dissertation on a topic within the guiding concept "Energy Cultures in Transition" in the discipline of Cultural Studies. The fellowship requires a high degree of willingness to engage in interdisciplinary dialogue, particularly with the STEM partnerships of the Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, as well as to conduct joint research with artists within the framework of the Schaufler Residency. In addition, engagement in the areas of science communication and outreach is expected. Shared office spaces will be made available to the fellows. Participation in the Kolleg's English-language training program is mandatory.Requirements:You hold an excellent university degree in Cultural Studies or a comparable field such as Geography, Anthropology or History. We especially welcome studies with global perspectives, particularly from North America, Asia or Africa. You possess strong teamwork skills and a willingness to collaborate across disciplines, and demonstrably excellent English language skills (C1 level minimum). Knowledge of German is desirable but not a requirement.We offer:The opportunity to pursue a doctorate within the Schaufler Kolleg with a structured qualification program and integration into an interdisciplinary research project. You will receive a fully equipped office workspace on the premises of TUD and access to an excellent research infrastructure, including participation in Research Studios and writing retreats. The Graduate Academy and other central institutions of TUD offer numerous further training and qualification opportunities. In addition, within the limits of the available project funds, the Schaufler Lab will cover the costs of conference travel. Inclusion and equal opportunities are important to us. We therefore look forward to receiving applications from people regardless of gender, origin, sexual orientation, worldview, or disability. TUD strives to employ more women in academia and research. We therefore expressly encourage women to apply. The University is a family-friendly university. We welcome applications from candidates with disabilities. If multiple candidates prove to be equally qualified, those with disabilities or with equivalent status pursuant to the German Social Code IX (SGB IX) will receive priority for employment. The fellowship does not constitute an employment relationship.Application:Your detailed application in English should contain, in addition to the completed online application form (https://tu-dresden.de/gsw/schauflerlab/schaufler-kolleg/phase-3/anmeldung-registration) , a letter of motivation, a curriculum vitae in tabular form including an account of your academic career, a copy of your most recent university degree certificate, an exposé of your research project including a work and time schedule (max. 20,000 characters). Please send us your application documents, including the online application form, quoting the reference number s26-002, by November 20, 2026 (stamped arrival date of the university central mail service or the time stamp on the email server of TUD applies), preferably via the TUD SecureMail Portal https://securemail.tu-dresden.de (https://securemail.tu-dresden.de)  by sending it as a single pdf file to schaufler.lab@tu-dresden.de (https://mailto:schaufler.lab@tu-dresden.de) or to:TU Dresden, Schaufler Lab@TU Dresden, Prof. Dr. Orit Halpern, Helmholtzstr. 10,01069 Dresden, Germany.Please submit copies only, as your application will not be returned to you. Expenses incurred in attending interviews cannot be reimbursed.TUD is a founding partner in the DRESDEN-concept alliance.Reference to data protection: Your data protection rights, the purpose for which your data will be processed, as well as further information about data protection is available to you on the website: https://tu-dresden.de/karriere/datenschutzhinweis

jobs.occupation: Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d)  of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track) (Biologe/Biologin)
jobs.description: Senckenberg Society for Nature Research (SGN) , headquartered in Frankfurt am Main, is seeking to fill the following position at the Senckenberg Museum of Natural History in Görlitz, ideally as of April 1, 2027:Research Scientist and Curator (m/f/d) of the section Vertebrata (Tenure Track)(full time / part time options available)Location: GörlitzEmployment scope: full time / part time options are availableType of contract: initially limited to three years;the type of time limitation depends on individual profile and legal framework (maximum 3+3 years). A permanent employment is planned after a positive evaluationRemuneration: collective agreement of the German Länder, TV-L E13The Senckenberg Society for Nature Research is a member of the Leibniz Association and has been investigating the “Earth System” worldwide for more than 200 years, examining the past, analysing the present, and developing projections for the future. We conduct integrative geobiodiversity research with the aim of understanding nature in all its complexity and diversity in order to preserve it as the foundation of life for future generations and to ensure its sustainable use. Across eight institutes and five research stations throughout Germany, scientists from more than 40 countries conduct research at the highest international level.The renowned Senckenberg Museum of Natural History, located in the medieval town of Görlitz, combines research at an international level with extensive collections and an engaging museum programme. The surrounding Upper Lusatia region offers a large variety of opportunities for experiencing nature.Senckenberg is committed to study the causes and effects of biodiversity loss in the Anthropocene. As part of our strategic development, we launched an ambitious long-term research effort in “Anthropocene Biodiversity Loss” encompassing the modules “Collectomics”, “Biodiversity Genomics”, and “Solution Labs”. Objectives include the transformation of natural history collections into the digital era, studying biodiversity from the genome to the ecosystem levels and offering exploratory spaces for science and society to develop common solutions to Anthropocene challenges.For the Görlitz vertebrate collection, which comprises approximately 70,000 specimens (preserved using dry, cryogenic, and liquid preservation methods, with the focus on mammals; birds make up a smaller proportion, while other vertebrate groups represent only a small fraction), we are seeking an internationally recognized scientist with a solid track record in mammal research, possibly supplemented by work on another vertebrate groups.Potential research topics may include various aspects such as mammalian diversity, functional morphology, phylogeny, or biological interactions. Curation and collection-based research should play a significant role in the applicant’s research approach. The selected candidate should be open to research collaborations with SGN colleaguesYour tasks- Scientific curation and development of the vertebrate collection and the associated resources as an important international research infrastructure through international networking, growth, and improved accessibility.- Develop a visible portfolio of collection-based research with basic and applied aspects in the broad field of mammalogy and possibly other vertebrate groups by using a range of established and innovative methods and approaches.- Taking responsibility for the relocation of the collection items, including the infrastructure of the Mammalogy/Vertebrate Section, to the new campus at Bahnhofstraße 30 at Görlitz.- Secure external research funds.- Publish results of your research in international scientific outlets.- Establish collaborations with ongoing projects, regional and national (region (e.g., long-term projects on wolf, lynx) and international (e.g., Africa, Mongolia), including with other sections and departments in Görlitz and further Senckenberg institutes.- Communicate with external stakeholders such as scientific associations, conservation agencies, local and regional authorities, as well as citizen scientists.- Participate in teaching in the MSc level programmes of International Institute Zittau/ Dresden University of Technology.Your profile- Doctoral degree in biology/zoology or a related field- Expert knowledge of mammals, including native species (the biogeographic focus of the mammal collection is currently the Palearctic), additional expertise in other vertebrate groups- Proactive willingness to implement innovative research approaches, such as in the field of genomics, morphometrics, AI, imaging, 3D methods, pollutant analysis in a collection context- Ability to identify attractive research questions and make use of synergies through collaborations- Excellent academic track record adequate to your career stage- Experience in the acquisition of third-party funding and project management- Experience in supervising staff (doctoral candidates, BSc., MSc., students, technical staff), ability to work in a team- Very good command of German (B2)- Fluency in English, both spoken and written- Class B driving licence (international driving licence)- Willingness to travel on occasion to the extent possible considering your personal circumstancesDesirable skills- Knowledge in molecular, biochemical or biophysical techniques in taxonomy and ecology- Knowledge in research data management and databases- Experience in curation and management of zoological collections, and in museum workWe offer- Access to an international network of scientists, policymakers and research organizations- An attractive job within the inspiring and dynamic working environment of an internationally recognized research institution with excellent infrastructures and collaborations opportunities, e. g. in morphology, genomics, evolutionary biology, (paleo-)ecology- A working place in completely new building with dissection and other laboratories, collection rooms, in the historic town of Görlitz with rapidly developing local research community (DZA, CASUS, IHI/TUD, HiLusatia), yet situated very close to nature with high mammal diversity and opportunities for field work- Opportunities to participate in teaching and outreach activities, e.g., in our museum and with collaborating universities- Opportunities for establishing an independent academic working group and acquiring further academic qualifications- Flexible working hours – mobile working options – employee ID card with free admission to Senckenberg museums – annual special payment – collectively agreed vacation entitlement – company pension planSenckenberg is committed to diversity. We benefit from the different expertise, perspectives and personalities of our staff and welcome every application from qualified candidates, irrespective of age, gender, ethnic or cultural origin, religion and ideology, sexual orientation and identity or disability. Women are particularly encouraged to apply as they are underrepresented in the field of this position; in the case of equal qualifications and suitability, they will be given preference. Applicants with a severe disability will be given special consideration in case of equal suitability. Senckenberg actively supports the compatibility of work and family and places great emphasis on an equal and inclusive work culture.How to apply?Please upload your application (letter of motivation with a short description of your previous and current research foci, a CV, certificates of academic achievements, list of publications as well as letter(s) of recommendation, if available) as a single PDF file by November 10, 2026.https://www.senckenberg.de/de/stellenanzeigen/For data protection information on the processing of personal data as part of the application and selection process, please refer to the privacy policy on our homepage at https://www.senckenberg.de/en/imprint/For further information about the Senckenberg Gesellschaft für Naturforschung please visit www.senckenberg.deContactSenckenberg Gesellschaft für NaturforschungSenckenberganlage 2560325 Frankfurt a.M.For specific questions about this role please contact Prof. Dr. Hjalmar S. Kühl.E-Mail hjalmar.kuehl@senckenberg.de

Working closely with Finance, Controlling, Manufacturing, and global program teams, you steer critical decisions across project controlling, product costing, manufacturing controlling, and financial closing.From shaping target processes and driving testing activities to coordinating cutover, go-live, and change management, you combine strategic leadership with hands-on execution to deliver a successful and sustainable business transformation.How You’ll Make an Impact * Lead the Finance transformation and co-lead the S4Energy rollout for Large Steam & Syncons, ensuring alignment across stakeholders and program objectives* Drive end-to-end Finance implementation activities, including requirements management, process design, Fit-Gap workshops, testing, data migration, cutover, go-live, and hypercare* Harmonize Finance & Controlling processes by balancing business requirements with SAP S/4HANA standards and scalable best practices* Coordinate cross-functional rollout activities and manage dependencies across Finance, Manufacturing, Supply Chain, and IT* Build and leverage a global Siemens Energy transformation network to share best practices and accelerate implementation success* Lead stakeholder engagement and change management initiatives to ensure organizational readiness and sustainable adoptionWhat You Bring* Bachelor's or Master's degree in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Information Systems, or a related field* Extensive experience in SAP S/4HANA Finance & Controlling, including leading complex implementation and business transformation programs* Strong expertise in Record-to-Report, Project Controlling, Product Costing, Manufacturing Controlling, and Financial Closing* Solid understanding of Engineer-to-Order (ETO) business processes and end-to-end value flows across project execution and manufacturing* Excellent stakeholder management, analytical thinking, and leadership skills with experience aligning global cross-functional teams* Fluency in German and English, enabling effective collaboration in an international environmentAbout the TeamOur Gas Services division offers Low-emission power generation through service and decarbonization. Zero or low emission power generation and all gas turbines under one roof, steam turbines and generators. Decarbonization opportunities through service offerings, modernization, and digitalization of the fleet. Who is Siemens Energy? At Siemens Energy, we are more than just an energy technology company. With ~100.000 dedicated employees in more than 90 countries, we develop the energy systems of the future, ensuring that the growing energy demand of the global community is met reliably and sustainably. The technologies created in our research departments and factories drive the energy transition and provide the base for one sixth of the world's electricity generation.Our global team is committed to making sustainable, reliable, and affordable energy a reality by pushing the boundaries of what is possible. We uphold a 150-year legacy of innovation that encourages our search for people who will support our focus on decarbonization, new technologies, and energy transformation.      Find out how you can make a difference at Siemens Energy: https://www.siemens-energy.com/employeevideoOur Commitment to Diversity Lucky for us, we are not all the same. Through diversity we generate power. We run on inclusion and our combined creative energy is fueled by over 130 nationalities. Siemens Energy celebrates character – no matter what ethnic background, gender, age, religion, identity, or disability. We energize society, all of society, and we do not discriminate based on our differences. Rewards/Benefits * In addition to an attractive remuneration package in line with the market, you can expect an attractive employer-financed company pension scheme* We also offer the opportunity to become a Siemens Energy shareholder* We offer our employees the opportunity to work flexibly and remotely, and our inspiring offices provide space for collaboration and creativity* The professional and personal development of our employees is very important to us. We provide them with the opportunities to learn and develop in a self-determined way, various attractive programmes and learning materials are available for this purpose* In relation to the "compatibility of family and work", we have a wide range of offers, e.g. flexible working time models, childcare places at many locations, the possibility of trial part-time work or even a sabbatical  We value equal opportunities and welcome applications from people with disabilities.https://jobs.siemens-energy.com/jobs

jobs.description: teamZUKUNFT gGmbHteamZUKUNFT gGmbH is a recognized provider of independent youth welfare services in accordance with §75 SGB VIII and has been supporting children, young people and families in challenging life situations for many years. With a wide range of inpatient and outpatient educational support, equestrian education and therapy, and targeted time-out measures, we respond individually to the needs of our clients. fixed-term contract under the WissZeitVG; plus a 1-year extension for a third-party funded projectYour salary will be based on TV-LYour tasks• Planning, conducting and analyzing the biological evaluation of newly developed PET and SPECT radiotracers• Contributing to the establishment, optimization anddocumentation of biological test systems and preclinical evaluation protocols• Performing in vitro studies, including stability, binding and cellular uptake assays as well as studies using models of the blood-brain-barrier• Preclinical evaluation of tracer candidates in suitable in vivo models, including support of small-animal imaging studies• Performing and analyzing ex vivo studies, e.g., autoradiography, biodistribution studies and complementary tissue analyses• Quantitative analysis of biological and imaging data andinterpretation of results in close interaction with the other project partners• Evaluation, documentation, and scientific presentation of experimental results in project reports, publications, and presentationsYour profile• Completed university degree and Ph.D. in biology, life sciences, neuroscience, biochemistry, pharmacy or a related field• with cell culture, in vitro assays, autoradiography, ex vivo analyses and BBB models is desirable• Interest in radiopharmaceutical tracer development, molecular imaging and translational research• Willingness to work with unsealed radioactive substances and to become familiar with radiation protection-related workflows• Willingness to conduct biological and preclinical experiments within an interdisciplinary team• Good written and spoken English skills• Structured, independent and conscientious working style• Ability to work in a team, strong communication skills and interest in interdisciplinary collaboration between chemistry, radiochemistry, biology, medicine and imagingOur offer• Everything but ordinary: You can expect a secure job in a challenging, innovative environment – including company pension schemes and regular working hours without business trips.• Work-life balance: Whether full-time or part-time, with or without children – with numerous support options, we will find the right path together.• Team spirit in R(h)ine culture: You will be warmly welcomed by an interdisciplinary team that values mutual respect and helpfulness.• Strong perspectives: We offer extensive training opportunities – so you can continuously grow and set new goals.Your future with usWe are one of the leading university hospitals in Germany and network research, teaching and health care at the highest level. That's why many things are a lot bigger for us: the spectrum of exciting development opportunities. The limitless openness with which specialists from all over the world work together here. Or our commitment as an employer to support all employees as best we can in reconciling their job with their goals and life situations.This is the University Hospital of Cologne: Everything but ordinary.Your future in detailThe Institute of Radiochemistry and Experimental Molecular Imaging (IREMB) is seeking a postdoctoral researcher for a translational research project in the field of radiopharmaceutical tracer development and molecular imaging. The postdoc position will initially be embedded for one year in the internationally funded IMAGESTRO project. There is an option of extension for another year. The focus of the work will be on the biological validation of newly developed PET or SPECT radiotracers.The IMAGESTRO project aims to develop novel 18F-labeled PET tracers for the non-invasive imaging of estrogen receptors in the brain, to characterize them preclinically, and to translate them into human applications. The project focuses on the organic synthesis of suitable precursor and reference compounds, the development and optimizationof radiofluorination strategies, and the comprehensive analytical and preclinical characterization of the resulting radiotracers. The work will be carried out in close cooperation between the University Hospital Cologne and Forschungszentrum Jülich and offers an interdisciplinary research environment at the interface of organic chemistry, radiochemistry, radiopharmacy, molecular imaging, biology and neuroscience.Applications from female candidates are expressly welcome and will be given priority in the event of equal suitability, competence and professional performance. People with disabilities are welcome to apply and will be treated preferentially in the event of equal suitability and qualification. jobs.employer_name: Boehringer Ingelheim Pharma GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: OUR COMPANYAt Boehringer Ingelheim we develop breakthrough therapies and innovative healthcare solutions in areas of unmet medical need for both humans and animals. As a family owned company, we focus on long-term performance. We believe that, if we have talented and ambitious people who are passionate about innovation, there is no limit to what we can achieve; after all, we started with just 28 people. Now, we are powered by 50,000 employees globally who nurture a diverse, collaborative and inclusive culture.The PositionAre you passionate about innovation, finding cutting-edge solutions and creating value where it matters, around the globe? At the BI global Inflammation team, we strive to deliver innovative Therapeutic and patient centric solutions by putting the patient in the center of everything we do. We foster innovative thinking as well as an agile and collaborative way of working to advance our novel programs and capabilities in Therapeutic Area Inflammation.The Global TA Inflammation, (Senior) HEOR  Manager, brings technical expertise, driving Outcomes Research (HEOR) and Patient Related Outcomes fostering our patient centric drive. His/she will support the TA Market Access Head by providing oversight, direction, and functional support on HEOR & PRO & Access projects. He/she will be working closely with Value and Evidence Networks within our Global Business Unit and with external stakeholders.Tasks & responsibilities- In your new role, you develop and execute on health economics outcomes research (HEOR) & PRO strategies, demonstrating the medical and economic payer-relevant needs to optimize value of BI products.- In this function, you generate evidence that secures optimal market access, successful HTA assessments, optimal pricing, reimbursement and formulary listing for BI products on a global scale.- Additionally, you ensure insights to further inform development of the Target Product Profile (TPP), clinical development plan of our pipeline compounds.- In consideration of regulatory body request and trial development, pre and post launch you will ensure relevant and new patient-reported outcome (PRO) measurement strategies to ensure that the patient perspective is captured in our clinical trial program and interact with regulatory authorities, closely collaborating with other functions.- Besides, you ensure efficient and timely development of key HEOR deliverables (i.e. payer value stories, payer engagement tools, GVDs, economic models, retrospective database analyses, indirect comparisons, real world evidence data) for assigned BI products.- Finally, yet importantly, you develop and maintain relevant partnerships with payers, academic research institutions, contract research organizations and other HEOR thought leaders in order to optimize the impact of HEOR & PRO research.Additional responsibilities as Senior Manager:- You will define long-term global development strategies for the assets, in close collaboration with the global Marketing and global Medical counterparts, to ensure optimal patient access.- In addition, you will draft long-term publication strategies, considering the long-term global market development.Requirements- Graduate degree, preferably PhD in health economics, Medicine (MD), public health, pharmacy, focusing on Health Technology Assessment, PRO, Pharmacy, Medicine, Public Health- Several years of pharma industry experience, with positions in areas of relevance for HEOR, PRO consulting or payer authorities- Multiple years of direct experience undertaking Health Technology Assessments (HTA) & PRO including Evaluations for Regulatory and health authority interventions of pharmaceutical products- Conducting or being part of a team working on non-interventional studies and RWE programs- Demonstrated experience of successful regulatory, reimbursement negotiations for launching new products in key markets- Proven track record of delivering value demonstration materials that resulted in timely patient access and adoption- Proven ability in appraising clinical evidence (both RCTs and operational evidence)- Profound knowledge and expertise to formulating COA strategies including validation methods, administration of measures and statistical analyses of COA data- Excellent communication and influencing skill both in internal and external contextAdditional requirements as Senior HEOR Manager:- Long-term pharma industry experience, with positions in the areas of health economics, pricing & reimbursement, consulting, or payer authorities- Several years of exposure to international business on a day-to-day basis- Strong track record in value generation, demonstration and/or communication- Highly experienced in conducting health economics/outcomes research across multiple specialty disciplines (e.g. patient reported outcomes, health economic modelling, real world data generation)For employees with a current contract of limited duration, legal / labor agreement requirements for contract extension will be considered.With us, you can develop your own path in a company with a culture that knows our differences are our strengths - and break new ground in the drive to make millions of lives better.Here, your development is our priority. Supporting you to build a career as part of a workplace that is independent, authentic and bold, while tackling challenging work in a respectful and friendly environment where everyone is valued and welcomed.Alongside, you have access to programs and groups that ensure your health and wellbeing are looked after - as we make major investments to drive global accessibility to healthcare. By being part of a team that is constantly innovating, you'll be helping to transform lives for generations.Want to learn more? Visit https://www.boehringer-ingelheim.com﻿Ready to contact us?If you have any questions about the job posting or process - please contact our HR Direct Team,Tel: +49 (0) 6132 77-3330 or per mail: hr.de@boehringer-ingelheim.comPlease submit your application documents in English.

A focus of our research are Engineered Living Materials (ELMs), an emergent class of materials from the combination of inert materials and living organism, with huge potential for sustainable innovation in different technological fields. Across the institute, materials scientists, synthetic biologists and biophysicists cooperate to understand living and inert matter, and to realize new materials with unprecedented functions from a synergistic interfacing.We are strongly linked to collaborative initiatives in the ELM field including the Leibniz ScienceCampus LifeMat, Living Therapeutic Materials, the Priority Program SPP2451 “Living Materials with Adaptive Functions”, and the MaterialVital Hub.As part of our ELM research community, we are seeking aPostdoctoral Researcher with expertise in Microbial Biophysics (f/m/d)with interest in the fundamental understanding of microbial communities within synthetic microenvironments. The candidate will be part of an interdisciplinary research team within the Department Dynamic Biomaterials at INM.Your roles:- Experimental research to understand microbial behaviour in confined spaces (synthetic hydrogels) and dynamic environments using imaging, microfluidics and molecular biology methods.- Scientific cooperation with researchers in materials science and synthetic biology at INM, and with external partners in bioanalytics/bioinformatics within running funded projects.- Compilation and presentation of research results in the form of progress reports and presentations at project meetings and scientific conferences.- Communication of research results within the scientific community at conferences and scientific events, and publication in scientific journals.- Co-supervision of students and doctoral researchers.- Support and promote the digitalization of ELM research in collaboration with dedicated experts in the group.Your profile:- PhD degree in biophysics/cell biology or related discipline.- Experience during your PhD or previous postdoctoral stay as experimental researcher in the field of microbial biophysics.- Interest in collaborative and interdisciplinary research challenges.- Self-driven and hands-on personality. Organization and prioritization skills.- Very good communication skills in English.We offer:- Work in an emergent research topic, with multiple opportunities to develop a competitive research profile.- An interdisciplinary research environment with complementary expertise and ready to share knowledge and support your work.- State-of-the-art infrastructure, including access to Core Facilities run by experts.- Access to a broad international network with vibrant scientific collaborators and exciting cooperation projects.- A highly professional and supportive working environment with an open and international culture.- A well-structured on-boarding process and clear responsibilities.- Transparent opportunities for career development.- Flexible working hours and mobile working opportunity.- A family-friendly working place.- A EG 13 TV-L position (full time). A part time position is also possible.The position is initially for 2 years.Interested?We look forward to your application! Please upload your CV and motivation letter, by October 15th, 2026 via the online application system. For further information on this position, please contact INM Scientific Director and Head of the Research Department Dynamic Biomaterials Prof. Dr. Aránzazu del Campo (aranzazu.delcampo@leibniz-inm.de ).The INM practices an open and appreciative corporate culture in which the existing diversity is promoted and lived. The institute is an equal opportunity employer with a certified family-friendly policy, and it provides offers for a better work-life balance, flextime, and mobile working. We promote professional opportunities for women and strongly encourage them to apply. Full time jobs can be generally divided. People with disabilities are expressly encouraged to apply and will be given priority if equally qualified.

GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The research group Plankton Imaging Technology and Deep-Sea Zooplankton Ecology at GEOMAR (in cooperation with Kiel University’s Marine Data Science Group) is offering a position in the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” starting at the earliest possible date.The position is offered for a duration of 3 years, with the possibility of extension. In the first year, the successful candidate will be employed by GEOMAR at 75%, supplemented by a 25% contract at Kiel University. Years two and three are fully funded at 100% (pay grade E13 according to the collective agreement for the public sector, TVöD, depending on experience).The position offers the opportunity to pursue a doctoral degree in natural or computer science as a member of the “Helmholtz School for Marine Data Science” (MarDATA). MarDATA’s interdisciplinary focus spans supercomputing, modeling, (bio)informatics, robotics, statistics, and big data methodologies. Doctoral researchers benefit from a structured training program that promotes cross-disciplinary collaboration and provides in-depth scientific insight as well as a systematic approach to marine data science. For more information, visit: https://www.mardata.de/. As part of the MarDATA doctoral network, the project “MegaRays - Deciphering Underwater Light Fields for 3D Plankton Characterization” aims at exploring the use of underwater light field cameras for observing and characterizing plankton organisms (zooplankton) in the ocean. Light field cameras deviate from off-the-shelf cameras in that all rays have to pass through an extra microlens array that changes their direction. Effectively, this means photographing the object from several slightly different perspectives, allowing focussing or 3D reasoning after image capture. The effects intertwine with refraction at the underwater housing and light-medium interaction in front of the camera.The successful applicant willcombine mathematical models for light field cameras and physical principles of refraction and underwater light propagation in order to simulate the image formation processemploy and extend methods of inverse rendering to visually reconstruct plankton from light field imagesdevelop workflows to extract ecological variables from light field imageryinvestigate, how automated classification can be improved by the extra 3D or raw information contained in light field imagesdevelop techniques for geometric co-calibration of light field images with a bioluminescence-sensitive camera in order to create 3D plankton models of bioluminescent deep-sea organismsIt is also expected that the successful applicant will create and contribute to creation and presentation of scientific publications, develop software for calibration, simulation and reconstruction, and is willing to perform and support data acquisition in the lab or at sea during scientific research cruises and collaborate with colleagues from other disciplines as well as the marine technology. Required:Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Computer Science or a related fielddocumented successful participation in classes in Computer VisionProfound knowledge in programmingAbility to use Computer Vision and Machine Learning libraries on HPC-machinesvery good English skills (written and spoken)If the university degree has not yet been completed at the time of application, credible evidence must be provided that the degree can be obtained by the start date spec...Homeoffice:Umfang: Nach Vereinbarung

jobs.description: The postdoctoral candidate will work within an international research project focused on improving the performance and long-term stability of aqueous batteries through the development of advanced electrolyte additives.The central objective of the project is to establish an integrated high-throughput workflow combining robotic electrolyte preparation, automated electrochemical testing, and machine-learning-assisted analysis.The work involves extensive experimental laboratory activities, automated testing, electrochemical characterization, data analysis, and close cooperation with industrial project partners. of aqueous electrolyte formulations.- Systematically screen a broad range of electrolyte additives and generate high-quality datasets linking electrolyte composition to battery performance.- Perform electrochemical characterization using techniques such as galvanostatic cycling, cyclic voltammetry, and electrochemical impedance spectroscopy.- Analyze large experimental datasets and contribute to the development and validation of machine-learning and quantitative structure-property relationship models.- Publish your results in leading peer-reviewed journals and present them at international conferences, write project reports.- Collaborate closely with researchers, data scientists, and industrial partners working on electrolyte synthesis, battery development, modelling, and scale-up.Your profileRecruitment requirement- A PhD in the subject areas of Materials science, Electrochemistry, Chemical Engineering, Energy Engineering, or similar.Required knowledge and personal skills- Strong background in electrochemistry and aqueous battery technologies.- Hands-on laboratory experience and interest in experimental research.- Experience with electrochemical measurements and data analysis.- Interest in automated experimentation and data-driven materials research.- Ability to work independently and as part of an interdisciplinary research team.- Knowledge of techniques such as EIS, cyclic voltammetry, hydrogen evolution,  and electrode degradation.- Very good English language skills (at least B2/C1 level according to CEFR).Desired knowledge and personal skills- Experience with aqueous batteries, metal-anode batteries, or electrolyte development.- Experience with materials characterization techniques, such as microscopy, X-ray methods.- Experience with automated experimentation, robotics, data science, or machine learning is advantageous.Reach out with your CV and motivation letter expressing your interest and experience in the proposed topic. Got questions before applying? Contact Prof. Zheludkevich (Mikhail.zheludkevich@hereon.de), Dr. Lamaka (Sviatlana.lamaka@hereon.de) or Dr. Snihirova (darya.snihirova@hereon.de).Our offer- Access to state-of-the-art (robotic) labs, unique scientific and technical infrastructure- Access to a large international research and industrial network.- Funding for conferences, summer schools and courses needed or research stays- An exciting job in a research center with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations- International Welcome Office with guest accommodation- 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's Day- social benefits according to the collective agreement of the public service and remuneration up to EG 13 (according toEntgO Bund)- very good work-life balance; options for mobile and flexible work- A green campus on the Elbe River, well-connected with Hamburg (public transport), subsidy for the Deutschlandticket if certain conditions are met (job ticket), charging facilities for electric vehicles- family-friendly company policy with childcare facilities, e.g. nursery/kindergarten close to the company- Operational Health Management, e.g. Employee Assistance Program (EAP)- Corporate BenefitsSeverely disabled persons and those equaling severely disabled persons who are equally suitable for the position will be considered preferentially within the framework of legal requirements.Interested? GEOMAR Helmholtz Centre for Ocean Research Kiel is a foundation under public law jointly financed by the Federal Republic of Germany (90%) and the State of Schleswig-Holstein (10%). It is one of the internationally leading institutions in the field of marine research.Through our research and our commitment to the transfer of knowledge and technology, we contribute significantly to the preservation of the function and protection of the ocean for future generations.The Research Unit Magmatic and Hydrothermal Systems (MuHS) of the research division 4 - Dynamics of the Ocean Floor is offering a position preferably starting as soon as possible. The position offers the possibility to attain a doctoral degree in natural sciences.The position is within the framework of the project “Understanding Core-Mantle Interaction Through Global Mapping of Ultra-Low Velocity Zones in Mantle Convection Models”, which is part of the German Science Foundation's Priority Programm SPP 2404 DeepDyn (https://www.geo.lmu.de/deepdyn/en/) about reconstructing the deep dynamics of planet Earth over geologic time.Ultra-Low Velocity Zones (ULVZs) are thin patches at the base of Earth’s mantle-only tens of kilometres high yet 100 to 1000 km wide-where seismic shear waves exhibit extreme reductions of 20-30%. They are archives of Earth’s thermochemical evolution, potentially reflecting its early differentiation or interactions with the core, but also more recent mantle flow patterns. Yet these interpretations depend critically on ULVZ composition, which remains poorly constrained.The doctoral researcher will numerically model ULVZ evolution and properties in plate-guided global mantle convection simulations. They will develop a framework that quantitatively evaluates these simulations by inferring ULVZ properties from mineral physics and comparing them to seismic constraints, including ULVZ geometry, geographic location and distribution. will lead payer-relevant evidence planning in partnership with HEOR, Medical and Clinical colleagues, identifying evidence needs, risks and opportunities.- By providing strategic guidance, you will develop global pricing recommendations that support launch planning, lifecycle management, indication expansion and long-term value optimization.- When evaluating market dynamics, you will lead the generation and interpretation of payer, HTA, reimbursement and competitive insights, translating findings into actionable recommendations.- Within your area of responsibility, you will drive access launch readiness across regions and markets, ensuring global strategies and value communications are effectively translated into local implementation.- Through close collaboration with internal and external stakeholders, you will ensure payer and access perspectives are reflected in development, evidence and commercialization planning.Requirements- Graduate degree in Medicine, Life Sciences, planning.- Deep understanding of global healthcare systems across major markets and the ability to adapt strategies to market-specific requirements.- Proven ability to independently lead complex cross-functional market access initiatives and translate ambiguity into clear recommendations and actionable plans.- Fluent English communication, presentation and stakeholder engagement skills.As We also offer a comprehensive benefits and wellbeing package.Applications from persons with severe disabilities are warmly welcomed. jobs.description: Position for a Postdoc (m/f/d) at the Chair of International Political StudiesUniverisity of Witten/HerdeckeWitten/Herdecke University (UW/H) is Germany’s first privately funded university. Today, the university employs more than 900 staff members, and a total of 3,700 students are enrolled in the Faculties of Health Sciences and of Economics and Social Sciences in Witten.Job descriptionThe team at the Chair of International Political Studies examines the causes and consequences of political violence. jobs.occupation: Research Associate (PhD position) for the DFG project (Wissenschaftliche/r Mitarbeiter/in)
jobs.description: Ihre AufgabenThe University of Bonn is an international research university offering a broad range of subjects. With a 200-year history, some 31,500 students, more than 6,000 employees and an outstanding reputation in Germany and abroad, the University of Bonn is one of the leading universities in Germany and has been awarded the status of a University of Excellence.The Department of Southeastasia is looking to fill the following position from January 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible, initially on a fixed-term contract according to § 2(1) WissZeitVG until December, 31, 2029Research Associate (PhD position) for the DFG project (65%)Working the Plantationocene. Ecological Labour Regimes of the Palm Oil Value Chain (PALMWORK)PALMWORK examines the relationship between labour and the environment along the palm oil value chain, particularly in the areas of production (plantations and oil mills) and social reproduction. The project is designed as a qualitative comparative analysis of case studies from Northeast India, Ghana and Colombia. It builds on re-search from the fields of labour regime analysis, (feminist) labour geography, environmental labour studies and political ecology on the materiality of nature and the society–nature metabolism. The project is being carried out as part of the DFG Priority Programme 2575 'Sustainability and Resilience of Agri-Food Chains' and consists of three sub-projects located at the University of Bonn, the Free University of Berlin and the University of Kassel. The position is for the sub-project in Northeast India, and is based at Bonn University.Tasks:- Field research with plantation and mill workers in North-East India- Contribution to joint publications- Contribution to science communicationProfile:- A completed academic degree (Master's) in the social sciences or earth sci-ences (political science, human geography, regional studies, sociology or equivalent)- Willingness to conduct independent field research in Northeast India- Very good spoken and written English- Good communication and teamwork skills- Intercultural and diversity competenceDesirable:- Experience of conducting independent research in India- Good knowledge of qualitative research methods- Experience with working and researching with (palm oil) workers- Good command of a language spoken in Northeast India (e.g. Assamese, Bengali, Nepali)- Good knowledge of the project's research area (political ecology, political economy, analysis of labour regimes, environmental labour studies, labour ge ography)What we offer:- Opportunity to pursue a PhD- Be part of a cutting-edge research team- Be part of a larger network of scholars in the DFG Special Programme- Flexible working hours and the ability to work from home- Remuneration in accordance with TV-L pay grade 13The University of Bonn promotes an open, respectful, and non-discriminatory academic culture and is actively committed to equal opportunity and family friendliness. We aim to eliminate structural disadvantages and to strengthen diversity in research, teaching, and administration. Therefore, we welcome all applications, regard-less of ethnic or social background, gender, sexual orientation, religion or belief, disability, or age.Applications from women and people with a documented severe disability (or equivalent status) will be given preferential consideration in accordance with the State Equality Act (LGG) NRW and Social Code (SGB) IXProject start is January 1st, 2027. Please send your application (with motivation letter, CV and writing sample (if available) with the application code 2026/447 to opye@uni-bonn.de. Application deadline is 22th November, 2026.

jobs.occupation: Ph.D. student (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholds (Physiker/in)
jobs.description: In order to fill a fixed-term position in part-time (26.2878 hours/week = 66%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1Ph.D. student (m/f/x): Data analysis for exotic hadrons at hadronic thresholdsThe work of the chair of experimental physics 1 focuses on basic research: Oneof the most essential elements of todays education and research is to gain abetter understanding of the structure of matter and the fundamental principles ofnature. In this process the basic research of physics plays an important role as itprovides a base for technical innovations and development. Hadron Physicsdeals with strong interacting particles consisting of quarks and gluons. Amongthose hadrons also rank the building blocks of the atomic nucleus, the protonand the neutron. There are many other hadrons that can only be created viacollisions of high energetic particles in big particle accelerators. The created hadrons are detected by modern and complex detectors to examine their composition and interactions.The position is embedded in two research programs. DEMOS ("Democratizing Models") is an ErUM research initiative developing a federated, interoperable standard for describing, sharing and re-evaluating physics models across particle, hadron, nuclear, neutrino and astroparticle physics. Hadronic coupled-channel amplitudes are one of its flagship applications: they are analytically intricate and rarely reproducible from the publication alone, which makes them an ideal test case for the new standard. HADRON 2030 is an intercollaborative research network dedicated to studies of hadron physics. Within the ExHAT (Exploration of Heavy Hadrons at Thresholds) project, we will explore heavy hadrons at thresholds using spectroscopy methods with LHCb data and inclusive production studies with ALICE. The flagship case is the doubly charmed tetraquark Tcc(3875)+, which lies a fraction of an MeV below the D0D*+ threshold. Line shape, pole position, three-body DD-pi dynamics and isospin breaking have to be disentangled in a joint effort of theory and experiment.Scope: part-timeDuration: fixed-term, 3 yearsStart: at the earliest possible dateApply by:  2026-11-15Your tasks:- Application of advanced methods of data selection, efficiency and resolutionstudies within LHCb data analysis.- Construction, fitting and analytic continuation of coupled-channel scatteringamplitudes.- Decipherment and serialization of the complex amplitudes in the DEMOS / amplitude-serialization format.- Collaboration within the DEMOS / HADRON 2030 networks.- Exchange with the experimental collaborations [LHCb, BESIII, Belle II, GlueX, ...] and with EFT/lattice QCD groups.Your profile:- Master's degree (or equivalent) in physics, completed by the starting date.- Background in experimental particle physics or hadron physics, and familiarity with quantum field theory and scattering theory.- Good scientific programming skills (Julia, Python or C++) and experience with version control and reproducible workflows.- Very good command of written and spoken English.- Interest in working at the interface between theory and experiment and inopen, reusable research software.https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA (https://jobs.ruhr-uni-bochum.de/jobposting/cfcd29d29c6781afa43ea9ee698bf39148ca1c4f0?ref=AfA)

internal and external stakeholders.- Experience in an administrative, executive support, banking, legal operations, paralegal, corporate services or similar coordination role.- Strong organisation and follow-through, with the confidence to chase people, manage deadlines and keep multiple workstreams moving.- Experience handling confidential information and formal documentation with accuracy and discretion.- Comfort working with banks, lawyers, advisers, notaries, corporate service providers or other external stakeholders.- Ability to work independently, prioritise changing requests and administration.Nice to have- Professional proficiency in French.- Experience supporting a CFO, finance leader, executive team or European corporate function.- Experience in a bank, financial
