Should you have any special requirements for the interview, please let the Hiring Manager know upon accepting the invitation to the interview.

**How to apply?

**Use the ‘APPLY’ link no later than November 15. Applications are assessed continuously, so don’t wait to send yours.

**Join us in bringing people closer

**GN brings people closer through our advanced intelligent hearing, audio, video, and gaming solutions. Inspired by people and motivated by innovation, we deliver technology that enhances the senses of hearing and sight. We enable people with hearing loss to overcome real-life problems, improve communication and collaboration for businesses, and provide great experiences for audio and gaming users.

**We hope you will join us on this journey and look forward to receiving your application.

_Are you passionate about defining and realizing complex technical systems? Do you thrive at the intersection of architecture, development, integration, and validation? Do you want to play a key role in shaping the technical foundation of Kamstrup’s next generation of smart metering solutions?

**Here Is What The Job Entails

**In the role as our next Lead Systems Engineer, your job will be to drive the technical definition and realization of complex smart metering solutions across hardware, firmware, connectivity, and cloud domains, ensuring robust and verifiable solutions throughout the product lifecycle.

You will act as a key technical authority between architecture and implementation, governing the system's perspective across disciplines and ensuring that system requirements, interfaces, integration, and validation are aligned from concept to deployment.

More specifically you will be:

• Defining and maintaining system requirements, system behavior, and technical specifications.

• Leading technical alignment across hardware, firmware, software, connectivity, and cloud domains.

• Driving system integration and supporting cross disciplinary troubleshooting.

• Ensuring traceability between requirements, design, verification, and validation activities.

• Playing a central role in technical reviews, risk assessments, and critical engineering decisions.

You will experience the opportunity to join a growing Systems Engineering capability and help shape how future smart metering solutions are developed at Kamstrup. Therefore, you will work with advanced connectivity and Internet of Things technologies while collaborating closely with Solution Architects, developers, and product teams. This is a highly visible technical role with significant influence on product direction, engineering excellence, and the future development of the Systems Engineering discipline.

**Meet your future team

**With direct references to the Director of Connectivity, you will become part of the Solutions Architects team within the Water Division. Together with colleagues in Connectivity Development and Connectivity Technology, the team is responsible for defining the solution foundations that enable smart metering products across the Kamstrup portfolio. In the team you will experience an informal and collaborative environment characterized by technical excellence, strong knowledge sharing, and a shared ambition to continuously improve the way we develop products and solutions.

Did you know? Our teams bring together specialists within architecture, connectivity, embedded systems, and product development, creating a unique environment where complex technical challenges are solved through close collaboration across disciplines.

**Less About Us, More About You

**We are looking for an experienced Systems Engineer with a proven track record of delivering complex technical solutions in multidisciplinary environments. You achieve work-related goals by combining strong systems thinking with the ability to influence technical direction, drive alignment across engineering domains, and take ownership of technical outcomes.

In order to succeed, we imagine that you:

• Hold a degree in Systems Engineering, Software Engineering, Embedded Systems, Computer Science, or a similar field.

• Bring extensive experience developing and delivering complex embedded or hardware-based products.

• Possess strong knowledge of systems engineering, requirements engineering, system integration, verification, and validation.

• Demonstrate the ability to drive technical decisions across hardware, firmware, software, connectivity, and cloud domains.

• Have a proven track record of leading technical alignment across multiple teams and stakeholders.

As an added advantage, you may also have experience with requirements management tools, system specification, verification and validation, and wireless communication technologies; familiarity with IoT connectivity solutions across short-range, long-range, and cellular networks; knowledge of standardized interoperability protocols and industry frameworks and the ability to apply a structured and analytical approach to solving complex technical challenges.

As we are an international organization it is important that you are fluent in English. Danish proficiency is considered an advantage.

Whilst you may not meet all the qualifications listed above, you could still be a good candidate for the position. If you find the role intriguing, do not hesitate to apply.

**We are more than the ordinary workplace

**We cherish the good colleagueship which we all contribute to, the only limit is your engagement. As we are a big organization you are bound to find one or more colleagues who share the same interest as you. This might be in our board game club, cycle team, during our yearly summer festival or on the padel court. For example, is our Head of System Engineering and Information Technology Denmark also our volunteer padel instructor while our Software Test Engineer runs weekly spinning classes.

Besides the best colleagues you could imagine, we also offer:

• Work life balance through flexible working hours.

• Employee benefits include a healthy canteen, fitness facilities, in house dental clinic, hairdresser, and a free health clinic

• An active employee association that fosters a collaborative and supportive workplace community.

• Beneficial health care and insurance package.

**Do you want to be a part of Kamstrup?

**Please submit your application by using the link below. Applications are reviewed on a continuous basis, and you can expect a response within six weeks.

The job will be located at Kamstrup's headquarters in Stilling, between Aarhus and Skanderborg.

If you have any questions about the position, please contact Director, Connectivity, Kristen Kasper Hansen, by phone: +45 89 93 10 00.

**_Get to know us

_**At Kamstrup, you'll become part of a close-knit community that genuinely cares about one another, fostering connections both in and out of the workplace. Our team comprises innovators, dreamers, and doers, united by an unyielding passion to challenge the status quo, find better solutions, and constantly push the boundaries of what's possible all with the purpose of securing clean water and energy to the maximum number of people. With an unwavering commitment to growth, we offer opportunities for you to leverage your skills and drive our business to new heights, empowering you to leave your mark on our future and grow with us. Explore more on our website, see our annual report, and stay updated through LinkedIn for the latest news and job openings.

NG Nordic is a leading provider of circular solutions and environmental services in the Nordics. By transforming waste into valuable resources and removing hazardous substances from the material cycle, we reduce emissions, protect natural ecosystems, and increase access to circular materials. NG Nordic is an important part of the Nordic industrial infrastructure, generating revenue of EUR 1.3 billion with a team of around 3,400 employees and 90 facilities.

Health & Safety Specialist, Nyborg, Denmark

Do you want to be the Safety Shoulder and make a real difference to safety in one of Europe’s most complex industrial environments?

Be the trusted Health & Safety voice in daily operations at NG Nordic’s hazardous waste treatment facility in Nyborg.

As Health & Safety Specialist, you will work close to the operational teams, helping managers and employees turn safety requirements into practical actions. You will be part of a five-person team in Nyborg and work as an integrated partner to Operations.

Nyborg is a Seveso III facility and is described as the EU’s largest hazardous waste treatment plant. Here, health and safety is not simply a compliance exercise: the risks are real, and your work can have a direct impact on people, processes and operational reliability.

Your role combines visible presence in the plant with reporting, statistics, procedures, training and improvement projects. You will advise and challenge Operations constructively, build trust across functions and help ensure a safe, professional operation.

The position is based in Nyborg and requires regular engagement with employees, supervisors and managers throughout the facility.

You will turn safety requirements into practical improvements in daily operations

You will participate in daily and weekly operational meetings, identify and prioritise EHSQ risks, and help the organisation address the issues that matter most. You will balance proactive safety work with administrative responsibilities and timely follow-up.

Your key tasks will include:

• Acting as the Health & Safety partner to Operations, advising managers and employees and participating in daily and weekly operational meetings

• Conducting safety walks, workplace inspections, toolbox talks and awareness activities, and following up on identified risks

• Preparing safety reports, statistics and KPI follow-up, identifying trends and recommending actions

• Developing and implementing practical safety procedures, training programmes, onboarding and contractor inductions

• Supporting risk assessments, audits, investigations and structured root-cause analyses of incidents and near misses

• Driving and prioritising safety improvement projects, monitoring corrective actions and supporting compliance with Danish legislation, internal standards and Seveso-related requirements

Experience from health and safety in industrial operations

We imagine that you have a relevant technical or health and safety qualification and approximately five years or more of experience in a comparable operational environment. Experience from process industry, chemicals, hazardous waste, energy or other high-risk facilities is especially relevant.

You understand occupational health and safety legislation, operational risk assessments, incident investigation, safety management systems and the importance of effective training and documentation. You are comfortable working with reports, statistics and digital tools.

You can translate complex safety requirements into clear, workable solutions. You communicate confidently in Danish and English, both verbally and in writing, and you know how to engage colleagues across functions and organisational levels.

You build credibility through presence, sound judgement and constructive dialogue. You have the natural authority to challenge unsafe practices while maintaining trust and respect, and you are robust enough to handle disagreement and pressure.

You are structured, proactive and able to prioritise competing tasks. You enjoy combining hands-on operational work with analysis, administration and continuous improvement, always keeping the most significant risks in focus.

Interested?

If you want to help create a safer and more professional operation in an environment where safety genuinely matters, we would like to hear from you.

NG Nordic is partnering with Brinch & Partners on this recruitment. For questions about the role, contact Partner Jens Chr. Jensen at +45 7020 2328. Please submit your CV and application in English.

We interview candidates on an ongoing basis.

All enquiries will be treated confidentially.

We want our recruitment process to be fair and inclusive. That is why we do not ask for photos or lengthy cover letters. Instead, we use screening questions to ensure comparable applications. We do, however, ask for gender information to help us ensure good gender balance in the recruitment process.

**Product Development Technician, NGP

Location: Svendborg, Denmark

Working hours: Full-time

Work model: On-site

Contract type: Permanent

_Are you passionate about product development and hands-on laboratory work? Do you enjoy transforming innovative ideas into products that reach consumers? Then you might be the person we are looking for.

_As our new Product Development Technician, NGP, you will be part of the Next Generation Products (NGP) Product Development team and play an important role in supporting the development, testing, and commercialization of nicotine pouch products. You will work closely with colleagues across Product Development, Quality Assurance, Manufacturing, Regulatory Affairs, Procurement, and external laboratory partners to help deliver high-quality products from concept through market launch. This is a great opportunity to gain exposure across the full product development lifecycle while working with innovative products in an international organization.

**What Your Day Will Look Like

**In this role, you will typically focus on:

• Preparing laboratory batches, prototypes, and product samples according to development plans and specifications.

• Conducting laboratory testing, product evaluations, and analytical assessments while accurately documenting results.

• Supporting pilot-scale and manufacturing trials to facilitate product scale-up and commercialization activities.

• Maintaining technical documentation, specifications, test reports, and development records in line with quality and regulatory requirements.

• Managing laboratory equipment, materials, and inventory while ensuring a safe, compliant, and organized working environment.

• Collaborating with cross-functional teams to support development timelines, technology transfer activities, and continuous improvement initiatives.

**What You'll Bring

**

• Laboratory Technician qualification, Bachelor's degree, or equivalent education in Food Science, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Biotechnology, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Material Science, or a related technical field.

• 2-5 years of experience in product development, laboratory operations, quality, manufacturing support, or a similar technical role.

• Strong laboratory and experimental execution skills, including experience with testing, data collection, and technical documentation.

• Good analytical, organizational, and problem-solving skills combined with proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel.

• A hands-on, detail-oriented, and collaborative approach with a strong commitment to quality and continuous learning.

• Experience within nicotine products, FMCG, food, pharmaceutical, consumer health, or other regulated industries is considered an advantage.

**Working At STG & What To Expect

**At Scandinavian Tobacco Group (STG), we are so much more than what meets the eye. We combine the strength of global brands with the entrepreneurial mindset that allows people to make a real impact. Here you'll have the opportunity to grow your career, collaborate across borders, and help shape what's next.

For this role, the Annual Base Salary ranges from DKK 432,000 to DKK 648,000, corresponding to the level of the position, expected experience and responsibilities.

Incentives and Benefits: The salary package may include short-term and/or long-term incentives as well as other employee benefits based on position level, location, functional area and relevant market benchmarks.

Ready to be part of something bigger? Apply now and discover **much more.

****Our recruitment process

****Requirements

**Before starting our hiring process, your application will be reviewed by a member of our Talent Acquisition team. We assess each application against the key competencies and requirements for the role. If your experience and skills are a good match, you'll be invited to continue through our hiring process, which may include the following steps:

• Recruiter screen

• Interview with the hiring team

• Assessment, case study, or work sample, if relevant

• Final interview with leadership or key stakeholders

_Scandinavian Tobacco Group is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability status, protected veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law.

_Please be informed that this Direct Search is conducted exclusively by Scandinavian Tobacco Group. We do not accept applications from agencies, and we will not provide compensation for unsolicited CVs.

jobs.occupation: Senior Data Engineer (Copenhagen or Remote, CET ±1)
jobs.description:
This role is open to candidates living within one hour of Danish time, all year round: Western, Central or Eastern European Time (WET, CET or EET). Applications from outside these timezones will not be considered.

About Linkfire and the team

Linkfire is the marketing platform the music industry uses to connect fans with the music they love. Every click on our smart links runs through our platform, millions of times a day, and artists and labels rely on our reporting to understand how their campaigns perform.

Our data platform turns that traffic into analytics inside the product, reporting for major labels, and the numbers the business runs on. Data here is part of the product, not a by-product of it.

Engineering is small and distributed, so you get a wide surface area and real ownership. The platform is still taking shape, and you will have a real say in where it goes next: architecture, tooling and the standards we hold ourselves to. You will work alongside the engineers who built this platform, and they will bring you into how it all fits together.

What you will do

• Help steer how the platform evolves, and grow into owning it end to end.

• Build and maintain our production data pipelines on Snowflake and Airflow, along with the Python services that power them.

• Build quality in from the start: everything you ship comes with tests and monitoring, rather than having them added later.

• Help build the AI agents that take repetitive data questions and investigations off the team's plate.

• Work with Product Managers and stakeholders early, so data is designed into features rather than added afterwards, and explain your choices to people who are not engineers.

• Take requests or roadmap items from idea to production, including challenging concepts and decisions early.

• Own the day-to-day flow of data work: requests from product and customer-facing teams, changes to existing pipelines, and new sources and feeds.

• Model data so analysis and reporting are easy. Dashboards stay with our analyst, but you know what they need and you build for it.

• Leave the platform better than you found it: documentation, tests, standardisation, and retiring what we no longer need.

What we are looking for

• Five or more years building production data pipelines.

• Strong Python. You have built services from scratch, with automated tests, sound design patterns and code that stays easy to maintain and scale.

• Deep experience with a cloud data warehouse in production, ideally Snowflake. If your depth is in BigQuery, Redshift or Databricks, we will give you room to go deep on Snowflake in your first months.

• Hands-on with Airflow or a similar orchestrator, and comfortable with Docker, Kubernetes and Argo CD.

How you work

• Product at heart. You see data end to end, from how it is collected to who uses it and why.

• Curiosity beyond your own stack. We work T-shaped: deep in data, interested in everything around it.

• You spot problems and bring solutions, and you find the balance between doing it right and getting it done.

• You use AI daily and have opinions on where it helps. Tell us about it when you apply.

• You communicate clearly and directly, mostly in writing.

The stack

This is what we run today. You don’t need experience with all of it, and we’ll help you get up to speed on the rest.

• Snowflake, with production pipelines in Python on an in-house framework.

• Airflow on Amazon MWAA for orchestration.

• Weld for ELT and reverse ETL, Metabase for internal and embedded dashboards.

• AWS (SNS, S3), Docker, Kubernetes and Argo CD.

• GitHub Actions, Terraform and Atlantis for CI/CD and infrastructure as code.

Nice to have

• Hands-on experience with parts of our stack beyond Snowflake and Airflow, such as Terraform, Weld or Metabase.

• Event-driven ingestion on AWS.

• Building with LLMs, for example tooling that automates investigations or answers questions about data.

Location

Copenhagen office if you want one, fully remote if you do not, as long as you live within one hour of Danish time all year round: UTC+0 to UTC+2 in winter, UTC+1 to UTC+3 in summer. That covers WET, CET and EET, from Portugal in the west to the Baltics and Finland in the east. Full-time, permanent.

Why join Linkfire

• Six weeks' paid holiday. Wherever you are based, plus a 4% company pension contribution if you are in Denmark, and competitive compensation.

• Room to grow. Clear, defined roles and a career framework, with the explicit goal of helping every engineer progress, whether that means going deeper or taking on more scope.

• Experienced peers. Engineers who have built and run this platform for years, and who will treat you as a peer from day one.

• Scale you can see. Your pipelines turn every click on the platform into the numbers artists and labels act on.

• Work you can point at. A small team and a large platform, so what you build matters.

• Remote-first. Flexibility, and colleagues across several countries.

Linkfire is an equal opportunity employer. We welcome applicants of every background and identity, and we hire on skills, experience and how you work.

The engineering team at Chainalysis is inspired by solving the hardest technical challenges and building products that establish trust in cryptocurrencies. We're a global organization that thrives on challenging work and doing it alongside exceptionally talented teammates. Our industry evolves rapidly, and our mission is to build a flexible, AI-driven platform that automates entity resolution, optimizes data labeling pipelines, and creates predictive models that identify illicit patterns before they escalate.

Our data and solutions have been used to solve some of the world's most high-profile criminal cases and grow consumer access to cryptocurrency safely. Now, by pairing the industry's most trusted blockchain data with agents that reason, investigate, and act, we help our customers scale their workflows as the cryptocurrency economy becomes increasingly mainstream.

The Protocols team delivers high-quality, low-latency blockchain datasets that serve as the trusted foundation for Chainalysis’ investigation, compliance, data and security products. We currently support more than 30 blockchains, translating on-chain data into actionable intelligence.

**In This Role, You’ll

**

• Architect and evolve scalable, reliable, and performant systems for ingesting and parsing complex blockchain data.

• Leverage AI-native engineering workflows (LLMs, automated agents) to increase team velocity and code quality.

• Provide blockchain protocol expertise (EVM, UTXO, etc.) to the team and cross-functional stakeholders.

• Manage the full software development lifecycle, including production monitoring, debugging, and maintaining reliability of our pipelines and services.

• Work closely with Product Managers to ensure our datasets meet the evolving needs of the crypto ecosystem.

• Guide junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews, design docs, and technical mentorship.

**We’re Looking For Candidates Who Have

**

• Extensive experience building distributed systems or data-intensive applications.

• Experience working with TypeScript either in a professional or personal capacity

• A bias to ship and the ability to iterate quickly in a fast-moving environment.

• Demonstrated ability to leverage AI assisted development tools to increase velocity while maintaining reliable, maintainable code.

• A deep understanding and experience of at least one Blockchain protocol

**You Might Also Have

**

• Knowledge and experience with non-EVM chains such as Solana, TON, and Sui.

• Experience with indexing and ETL at scale (Spark/Databricks).

• Knowledge of Infrastructure as Code (Terraform) and managing services in Kubernetes.

• Contributions to open-source blockchain projects.

**Technologies We Use

**

• Languages: Java, TypeScript

• Data Processing: Spark, Databricks, PostgreSQL

• Infrastructure: AWS (Serverless & EKS), Kubernetes, Terraform

• CI/CD: GitHub Actions

**AI at Chainalysis

**AI is not a feature at Chainalysis - it is a new way of working. One that turns instructions into work done, and helps us move faster than the threats we're built to counter, and we expect our employees to take ownership of the output and ensure quality. As the world's most trusted blockchain analytics platform, Chainalysis sits at a rare intersection of proprietary data, regulatory relationships and crypto expertise that makes it uniquely placed to shape and lead the next era of AI-driven intelligence - and we expect everyone here, regardless of role, to be an active part of it.

AI fluency is tied directly to how we measure performance and how we plan to win. There is no substitute for your own curiosity. We provide the tools, workflows, and space to experiment - but the expectation is that you develop these capabilities yourself, bring ideas, and collaborate across teams to reinvent the way work gets done. We are not using AI to do less. We are using it to do what was never possible before.

**About Chainalysis

**Chainalysis is the blockchain data platform, making it easy to connect the movement of digital assets to real-world services. Powered by deep blockchain data and AI, organizations can investigate illicit activity, manage risk exposure, and develop innovative market solutions built on the industry's most trusted blockchain intelligence. Our mission is to build trust in blockchains, blending safety and security with an unwavering commitment to growth and innovation.

**You belong here.

**At Chainalysis, we believe that diversity of experience and thought makes us stronger. With both customers and employees around the world, we are committed to ensuring our team reflects the unique communities around us. We’re ensuring we keep learning by committing to continually revisit and reevaluate our diversity culture.

We encourage applicants across any race, ethnicity, gender/gender expression, age, spirituality, ability, experience and more. If you need any accommodations to make our interview process more accessible to you due to a disability, don't hesitate to let us know. You can learn more here. We can’t wait to meet you.

Compensation Range: DKK 856,000 - DKK 1,158,000

About MITS Industries

MITS Industries is an advanced systems and industrialization company developing integrated technology platforms for demanding aerospace, security, and mission-critical applications. Its mission is to transform operationally validated technologies into scalable, ready-to-deploy systems by combining advanced engineering, industrial partnerships, and strong governance.

MITS Industries is establishing an R&D and design site in Copenhagen focused on advanced RF systems, signal intelligence, aerospace technologies, and mission-critical product development. The site will build core capabilities in RF and microwave hardware, antenna systems, RF testing and characterization, rugged mechanical integration, and the industrialization of complex radio-electronic systems.

The Copenhagen team will work closely with strategic partners and engineering teams across Europe, playing a leading role in the development, validation, industrialization, and deployment of advanced technologies for defense, aerospace, and other demanding applications.

One of the initial focus areas will be an advanced aerospace signal-intelligence product platform covering RF and system architecture, antenna-system design, RF and microwave hardware, laboratory validation, mechanical integration, integration with the satellite platform, and preparation for qualification, production, and operational deployment.

The ambition is to build a strong technical design site capable of taking complex RF products, modules, and platforms from architecture and detailed design through prototyping, testing, validation, industrialization, and international deployment.

About the role

MITS Industries is looking for a Senior Mechanical Design Engineer to join the core Copenhagen R&D team and help build the site’s mechanical design capability for antenna and RF systems. The role is intended for an experienced mechanical engineer with prior hands-on experience developing the mechanical implementation of antenna, RF, or microwave hardware.

You will design and develop mechanical solutions for antenna systems and associated RF and electronic assemblies. The work includes antenna supports and mounts, RF-aware enclosures, radomes, fixed and, where applicable, deployable antenna mechanisms, test fixtures, thermal solutions, connector integration, cable routing, sealing, environmental protection, and platform interfaces. Many of these structures can directly affect antenna and RF performance, requiring close co-design with antenna and RF engineers.

The role covers mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing-process selection, structural and thermal analysis, tolerance definition, detailed CAD design, prototyping, assembly, environmental validation, serviceability, and production release. Particular attention will be given to mechanical structures that directly affect antenna performance, integration, alignment, stability, and deployment.

You will work closely with antenna systems engineers, RF and microwave hardware engineers, system architects, RF test and characterization engineers, manufacturing partners, and partner engineering teams. The role requires strong mechanical design expertise, RF-aware product thinking, end-to-end technical ownership, and hands-on implementation experience, taking designs from concept through prototype build and qualification to documented, manufacturable antenna assemblies and integrated systems.

Key responsibilities

• Translate system, antenna, and platform requirements into mechanical architectures, interface definitions, design constraints, and technical trade-offs.

• Design mechanical components and assemblies for antenna systems, including supports, mounts, frames, radomes, RF-aware enclosures, fixed or deployable mechanisms, and platform-integration structures.

• Own the detailed mechanical implementation of antenna and RF assemblies, including 3D CAD models, 2D manufacturing drawings, GD&T, assembly-level tolerance analysis, BOMs, and configuration-controlled documentation.

• Develop mechanical solutions that maintain antenna alignment, dimensional stability, RF clearances, grounding, shielding, cable routing, connector accessibility, and other mechanical conditions required to achieve the intended electromagnetic performance.

• Integrate RF modules, antennas, electronics, connectors, cables, gaskets, thermal interfaces, and environmental sealing into complete mechanical assemblies.

• Perform structural, thermal, and tolerance analyses covering stiffness, strength, mass properties, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, and expected environmental loads.

• Define mechanical requirements and work jointly with antenna and RF engineers to establish electromagnetic constraints for radomes, covers, supports, enclosures, and other structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Design antenna deployment and positioning mechanisms, where applicable, including hinges, latches, restraints, stops, alignment features, and associated interfaces.

• Design test fixtures, alignment tools, handling aids, assembly tooling, and prototype-support hardware for antenna and RF system development.

• Select materials, coatings, surface treatments, fasteners, adhesives, seals, bearings, and manufacturing processes based on structural, thermal, RF, environmental, corrosion, and production requirements.

• Lead mechanical prototype build, assembly, troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Contribute to environmental testing and qualification, including vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, and other relevant mechanical validation activities.

• Apply design-for-manufacture, design-for-assembly, serviceability, reliability, and cost considerations throughout development.

• Work with suppliers and manufacturing partners on technical clarification, process selection, prototype production, inspection, non-conformance resolution, and production release.

• Prepare mechanical specifications, analysis reports, interface-control documentation, design-review materials, assembly instructions, and production handover documentation.

• Collaborate with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and engineering workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

Required qualifications and experience

• Degree in mechanical engineering, aerospace engineering, or a related engineering discipline, or equivalent relevant professional experience.

• 5+ years of professional mechanical design experience, including demonstrated experience developing mechanical hardware for antenna, RF, or microwave systems where mechanical geometry, materials, interfaces, tolerances, or nearby structures directly influence electromagnetic performance.

• Strong hands-on experience and demonstrated technical ownership of complex mechanical assemblies from initial architecture and concept through detailed design, prototype build, verification, qualification, and production release.

• Advanced proficiency with a professional 3D CAD and drafting environment; SolidWorks experience is preferred.

• Strong command of GD&T, engineering drawing standards, assembly-level tolerance analysis, and production-quality mechanical documentation.

• Demonstrated experience designing mechanical components or assemblies for antenna, RF, or microwave systems, such as antenna supports and mounts, frames, enclosures, radomes, mechanisms, fixtures, or other mechanically and electromagnetically constrained structures.

• Experience with mechanical packaging and integration of antennas, RF modules, PCBs, connectors, cables, thermal interfaces, shielding, grounding, seals, and associated electronics.

• Practical understanding of RF-aware mechanical design, including the effects of materials, structures, clearances, alignment, grounding, shielding, cabling, and radomes on antenna and RF performance.

• Experience applying engineering calculations and simulation methods, including finite-element analysis where appropriate, to support structural and thermal design decisions.

• Understanding of stiffness, strength, thermal expansion, heat transfer, vibration, shock, fatigue, and other relevant environmental loads.

• Practical knowledge of metallic materials, engineering polymers, elastomers, composites, adhesives, coatings, and surface treatments.

• Strong understanding of manufacturing processes, such as precision machining, sheet-metal fabrication, additive manufacturing, composite manufacturing, joining, fastening, sealing, and assembly.

• Demonstrated hands-on experience with prototype assembly, mechanical troubleshooting, design verification, and iterative improvement.

• Experience supporting environmental testing and qualification, such as vibration, shock, thermal cycling, ingress protection, or comparable validation activities.

• Experience working with suppliers and manufacturing teams on process selection, technical clarification, inspection, non-conformance resolution, manufacturability, and production handover.

Nice to have

• Experience developing lightweight, stiffness-critical structures with stringent alignment and dimensional-stability requirements.

• Experience with aerospace or space-hardware qualification, including thermal-vacuum testing, outgassing constraints, vibration, and shock.

• Experience with precision mechanical alignment, dimensional inspection, antenna positioning, and calibration or verification fixtures.

• Experience designing IP-rated enclosures or ruggedized outdoor electronic equipment.

• Experience with product data management, configuration control, and release processes for complex mechanical assemblies.

• Experience working with international suppliers and manufacturing partners on low-volume, high-complexity hardware.

• Experience designing radomes, RF-transparent structures, or mechanical structures located within or near the antenna field.

• Experience with mechanically steerable, deployable, foldable, or position-critical antenna systems.

• Experience working directly with antenna or electromagnetic simulation engineers to iterate mechanical geometry, materials, and interfaces based on RF performance.

Success in the first 6 months

• Take end-to-end technical ownership of one or more mechanical subsystems or integration areas for antenna and RF systems.

• Establish the initial mechanical architecture, material and manufacturing approach, and platform-integration plan for the assigned scope.

• Deliver reviewed 3D models, manufacturing drawings, tolerance analyses, interface definitions, and supporting design documentation.

• Develop and support the build, assembly, and verification of initial mechanical prototypes, fixtures, or engineering models.

• Identify key structural, thermal, alignment, sealing, deployment, and manufacturability risks and define practical mitigation actions.

• Establish effective technical interfaces with antenna, RF and microwave hardware, system, test, electronics, manufacturing, supplier, and partner engineering teams.

• Help establish mechanical design standards, CAD practices, documentation templates, and release workflows for the Copenhagen design site.

jobs.occupation: Anesthesia nurse are sought for Anesthesia Department 2
jobs.description:
We are looking for anesthesia nurses who wish to work in a department that provides anesthesia for cardiac, pulmonary, vascular, and gastrointestinal surgery patients. You will become part of a dedicated and interdisciplinary team that values high professional standards, education, and good cooperation.

Anesthesia Department 2
We are organized into two specialty-based teams, with a focus on maintaining specialty-specific competencies while also helping one another across teams to create flexibility and variety in everyday work. We are looking for colleagues who are interested in both teams, but please mention any preference in your application.
Team A:
Handles anesthesia for abdominal surgery, ECT treatment, and interventional procedures (e.g., PTC and Coiling). The team also contributes to internal and external transfers and operates the IV team, specializing in advanced invasive access.
Team TV:
A highly specialized team providing anesthesia for cardiac, thoracic, and vascular surgery, as well as procedures in the cardiology catheterization laboratory, the pulmonary medicine outpatient clinic, and the radiology department. We receive emergency cardiac patients from the pre-hospital team, are part of the hospital’s cardiac arrest team, and provide anesthesiology support in response to emergency calls within the hospital.
Anesthesia Department 2 is a training site for nursing students, nurse anesthesia trainees, physicians in specialist training, and paramedics. During on-call shifts, we are responsible for the same clinical specialties as during daytime hours, but we also work as part of a broad cross-team on-call group. We support one another to ensure that the overall anesthesia workload in the operating suite runs smoothly for the benefit of patients. Regardless of patient category, we focus on maintaining a professional and compassionate nursing relationship with each patient. We would like to hear what, in your view, characterizes a good patient journey.

We are looking for a colleague who...

• Already has or can obtain a Danish Authorization in accordance with Danish law 
• Is fluent in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish (preferably)  
• has a specialized education in anesthesia nursing
• thrives with both highly specialized and general anesthesia nursing
• has a positive, flexible, and professional approach to change
• values professional quality and individual care for the patient
• contributes actively to good cooperation and a healthy work environment
• is eager to participate in our educational tasks
With us, you will receive...

• a thorough and individually tailored introduction program
• Support from experienced colleagues, with a focus on both professional and social integration
• An exciting working environment with a high level of specialization and opportunities for professional discussion and peer support
• A strong emphasis on education, development, and interdisciplinary collaboration
• Great colleagues and room for individual differences
• Language practice with an in-house consultant
 
Working hours and planning
Day shift: 7:30 a.m.– 3:15 p.m. (late shifts until 4:15 p.m., 5:15 p.m., and 6:15 p.m.)
Evening/night shift: Four staff members start at 2:45 p.m. and work actively until 10:45 p.m., followed by an on-call shift from the staff on-call room until 7:30 a.m.
We work with a 16-week rota cycle. Scheduling is carried out in close collaboration between the rota planner and clinical coordinators. Individual preferences are given high priority within the needs of the team and the requirements of the service.
This year, we moved into new, modern facilities in Hospitalsbyen and are currently adapting to the new workflows. In addition, we currently have one abdominal surgery operating list per week at Aalborg Hospital South on Hobrovej.
If you are passionate about anesthesia, professional excellence, and meaningful patient journeys, we look forward to hearing from you.
 
Questions?
For any questions regarding the position please contact Head Nurse Manager Merete Isaksen Dietz by phone on +45 30 56 75 32 or by e-mail at mli@rn.dk.
For any questions regarding Danish authorization or the process hereof and language requirements, please contact HR Consultant Michelle Cederstrøm – m.cederstroem@rn.dk
 
Practical information
Salary and terms of employment are in accordance with the applicable collective agreement for non-managerial staff within the Danish Health Confederation’s area, concluded with the Danish Nurses’ Organization. The position is 37 hours per week.
The application deadline is 31. december 2026, and interviews are expected to take place in january. The preferred start date is 1 of february 2027, or by agreement.

Place of work
Your primary place of employment will be Anesthesia Department 2 in Aalborg. Your employment area is the North Denmark Region, with duties at Aalborg University Hospital, Anesthesia Aalborg. You may also be required to work in other departments within Anesthesia Aalborg, subject to the notice period for changes to the rota specified in the collective agreement.
References will be obtained before an employment offer is made.

About the North Denmark Region
The North Denmark Region provides welfare services to approximately 590,000 people in North Jutland in the areas of healthcare, regional development, and specialized social services. Around 15,000 employees work together on this mission, bringing a wide range of professional expertise to create value every day for patients and citizens in North Jutland and to support a cohesive region. With us, you can build your career, make every day count, and make a difference. Read more about the region at www.rn.dk.

jobs.occupation: PhD scholarship in battery chemistry and magnetic resonance - DTU Chemistry
jobs.description:
If the idea of developing next-generation batteries charges you up, then this PhD position at the Department of Chemistry, DTU, is for you! We use magnetic resonance to understand how batteries work, and why they fail, at the molecular level, so that we can design better materials for safer, longer-lasting and higher-performing energy storage. In this 3-year project, supervised by Assistant Professor Leo W. Gordon, you will learn battery analysis using nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) techniques together with a range of electrochemical methods. The expected start date is on, or close to, 1st April, or by mutual agreement.

As the battery field matures, new materials and chemistries will be needed for specific applications. Getting the best performance out of them requires a clear understanding of the chemistry and dynamics inside the cell: how the components interact, how the local structure changes during use, and what leads to degradation. These processes are hard to study without disturbing the sample, and attributing changes in performance to specific species or components needs chemically specific information. NMR is element-specific and non-destructive, which makes it a powerful tool for providing this insight.

This research will develop and apply a suite of NMR characterisation tools to study battery materials and components. Combined with electrochemical characterisation, these methods will build a detailed picture of structure, dynamics and degradation across a range of representative battery systems. The aim is to establish design principles for next-generation batteries.

Responsibilities and qualifications
This project is primarily experimental has a strong emphasis on NMR spectroscopy and electrochemistry. Prior knowledge of NMR and/or electrochemistry are preferred but not required.

Applicants should have a Master’s degree in chemistry, chemical engineering, materials science, or a related field. The ideal candidate should be driven by clean energy and sustainability goals and have a keen interest in developing innovative new methods to understand physical and chemical phenomena across multiple length scales. They should demonstrate a positive, self-starting attitude, and should have a deep curiosity to drive their science. Proficiency in spoken and written English is essential.

The formal requirements are:

You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
The assessment of the applicants will be made by Assistant Professor Leo W. Gordon.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and terms of employment
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations. Please see DTU’s salary structure for scientific staff: www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The starting date is April 1st or similar, according to mutual agreement and the position is full time. 

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure 
Your complete online application must be submitted no later than Sunday, 29 November 2026 (23:59 Danish time). 

Applications must be submitted as one PDF file containing all materials to be given consideration. To apply, please open the link "Apply now", fill out the online application form, and attach all your materials in English in one PDF file. The file must include:

• 
A letter motivating the application (cover letter)

• 
Curriculum vitae

• 
Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale

• 
A writing sample of a published paper, pre-print, or thesis, with a short (≤ 1page) accompanying statement clearly detailing your contributions and key findings.

You may apply prior to obtaining your master's degree but cannot begin before having received it.

Applications received after the deadline will not be considered.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.

The Department of Chemistry performs research, educational activities, and innovation at a high international level within e.g. energy, catalysis, and materials. The overall aim is to contribute with new knowledge about basic scientific problems and carry out research with vast application perspectives - to the benefit of both society and companies. The department is well-equipped with all of the necessary infrastructure for the position, including NMR spectrometers and electrochemical testing equipment.

Technology for people
DTU develops technology for people. With our international elite research and study programmes, we are helping to create a better world and to solve the global challenges formulated in the UN’s 17 Sustainable Development Goals. Hans Christian Ørsted founded DTU in 1829 with a clear mission to develop and create value using science and engineering to benefit society. That mission lives on today. DTU has 13,500 students and 6,000 employees. We work in an international atmosphere and have an inclusive, evolving, and informal working environment. DTU has campuses in all parts of Denmark and in Greenland, and we collaborate with the best universities around the world.

Location: Odense, Denmark

Come work with us on the most urgent topic for European security and resilience as we build drone technology at scale for the defence of Europe.

Employment requires that the employee must be able to obtain a security clearance by the Danish Defense Intelligence Service. This entails, among others, that the employee's full household, as a minimum, has stayed within NATO/EU countries for the last 7 years, only interrupted by short stays abroad, and that none of the full household members has committed serious criminal offences.

The Senior Mechanical Engineer will be responsible for a significant portion of the mechanical design in the company, including architectural ownership, lifecycle oversight, design, manufacturing of prototypes and handing over to production.

Responsibilities:

• Actively contribute to the design of new products and improvements to existing.

• Define new concepts, iterate on ideas, and maintain development plans.

• Generate well-defined tasks for colleagues, students, assistants, consultants, and contractors.

• Take ownership and responsibility for a subset of products and drive it forward.

Requirements:

• True passion for your craft and tools: CAD/FEA, materials science, manufacturing technologies, related theory and mathematics.

• Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or similar.

• 5+ years of experience working in aerospace, defense, automotive, or other related fields.

• Demonstrated experience working with complex multidisciplinary projects.

• Hands-on experience building/fixing prototypes or other mechanical systems. Not afraid of getting hands dirty, feels home in the workshop.

• Experience in design for mass production, including Design for Manufacture (DFM), Design for Assembly (DFA), and cost optimization initiatives.

• Eligibility to work on defense-related projects; security clearance required.

Very nice to have:

• Some exposure or previous experience working with UAV/FPV, Drones, Robots, etc.

• Passion for flying things, planes, drones, UFOs.

About us:

We're a fast-growing Nordic defence tech company developing and mass-producing pilot-assisted, expendable drone systems at scale.

We're running a flat organization with teams in Odense and Aarhus collaborating daily on tasks within R&D, product development, customer engagement and team activities. We work to make a difference for the defence of Europe and celebrate the many small milestones we as a team overcome as we grow. Our team is guided by a core set of values putting effectiveness of our products and decency as a company culture first.

We're tech-savvy and bring very different backgrounds and experiences into our team. We have the ability to invest as needed and feel the responsibility to give our part in bringing a sense of security back to Europe.

**Senior Discovery & Digital Innovation Engineer

**If you're excited by emerging technologies, enjoy exploring new ideas, and want to help shape the future of healthcare, this could be the opportunity for you.

You will join Ambu's Discovery organization and play a key role in identifying and maturing future growth opportunities beyond our current product portfolio. Working at the intersection of healthcare, technology innovation, business creation, and digital capabilities, you will help uncover and evaluate ideas that could become Ambu's next generation of products, services, and business platforms.

Collaborating with colleagues across engineering, clinical, commercial, and innovation functions, you will engage with clinicians, researchers, hospitals, startups, and innovation ecosystems to understand unmet needs, explore technology trends, and translate insights into opportunity assessments, business cases, prototypes, and strategic recommendations.

This is a unique opportunity to combine technical curiosity, commercial thinking, and stakeholder engagement in a role that offers significant visibility and the chance to influence future strategic decisions. If you thrive in an environment where innovation, creativity, and collaboration are valued, we'd love to hear from you.

We believe the best ideas come from a mix of in-person collaboration and focused individual work. That's why this role is based in Augsburg or Ballerup and follows a **hybrid working model, with three days per week in the office and two days working from home.

****Key Responsibilities

**

• Identify and evaluate adjacent business opportunities, changing clinical practices, unmet needs, reimbursement developments, future healthcare trends, and emerging digital technologies.

• Translate clinical, market, and technology insights into actionable opportunity assessments, strategic recommendations, value propositions, and early-stage business cases.

• Build relationships with clinicians, key opinion leaders, researchers, hospitals, startups, and innovation ecosystems to gain early access to emerging needs, technologies, and opportunities.

• Evaluate and mature emerging technologies and digital capabilities, including AI, machine learning, computer vision, healthcare data analytics, automation, robotics, imaging, and software-enabled medical devices, through fast prototypes and demos to make the idea tangible

• Develop proof-of-concept solutions, innovation demonstrators, and feasibility assessments to support strategic decision-making.

• Collaborate across engineering, clinical, commercial, and innovation functions to assess customer value, market potential, competitive landscape, technical feasibility, and strategic fit.

• Drive promising opportunities through Discovery processes and decision gates, from early insight to validated recommendations and development readiness.

**Suggested candidate profile

**

• Have an educational background in engineering or a related technical field and be comfortable applying engineering principles to evaluate emerging technologies, technical feasibility, and future product opportunities.

• Have significant experience within medical devices, healthcare technology, software, digital health, or other innovation-driven industries, combined with practical experience working in product development, innovation, or business creation environments.

• Have demonstrated the ability to identify, evaluate, and mature new opportunities and to develop strategic recommendations, value propositions, business cases, or innovation initiatives.

• Combine strong technical understanding with commercial curiosity and an interest in how emerging technologies can create future business value.

• Are comfortable navigating complex organizations and collaborating with stakeholders across technical, clinical, commercial, and leadership functions.

• Communicate and influence effectively across diverse audiences and can explain complex concepts in a clear and compelling way.

• Bring a strong understanding of healthcare, innovation processes, and commercial considerations, supported by a master's degree or higher in engineering, medical technology, life sciences, healthcare technology, business, or a similar field.

• Ideally bring experience in one or more of the following areas: digital health, AI or machine learning, computer vision, healthcare data analytics, software-enabled medical devices, in innovation management, product management, workflow automation, robotics, or emerging imaging technologies.

**Ambu - a visionary and international workplace where your efforts matter

**Ambu is a company that expands rapidly and has ambitious growth targets. We meet these targets through interdisciplinary teamwork between motivated and highly skilled employees. Your contributions and efforts are crucial to our success, and by joining us you will get the opportunity to work in an international environment with an informal working culture.

We offer great opportunities for personal development. Furthermore, we offer a wide range of professional, social and financial employee benefits in addition to exciting job challenges and continuous professional and personal development.

Engineering, Full time, Remote (EU), Berlin, Copenhagen, or Milan

**About Apylon And The Opportunity

**Apylon is building agents for the most complex workflow out there - financial admin in healthcare.

Hospitals and payers move billions of euros through fragmented, manual workflows shaped by clinical data, payer rules, contracts, and local coding systems. We believe this is a data, machine-learning, and automation problem disguised as financial operations.

We are live with leading private hospitals and expanding quickly. Every hospital presents a different challenge: EHR systems are configured differently, national coding rules vary, and contracts describe the same clinical event in different terms. Your job is to help us turn that complexity into a system that learns: each new integration should make the next one faster, safer, and less expensive.

Apylon is backed by experienced operators and top-tier investors in healthcare and fintech. Our team draws on experience from Zendesk, Pleo, Wawa Fertility, Sibill, and some of the largest multi-country hospital groups in Europe. You’ll join the first small engineering team, with massive ownership over both what we build and how we build it.

Delivering healthcare is hard. Getting paid for it shouldn’t be.

You’ll be responsible for

• Own EHR integrations end to end: APIs, schemas, undocumented behaviour, operational failure modes, and vendor changes.

• Build reusable integration-platform primitives for extraction, normalisation, versioning, replay, monitoring, and observability.

• Design the canonical data model that connects heterogeneous EHR data, reimbursement systems, national coding standards, and hospital-specific conventions.

• Build reliable inputs for our billing agents, including the constraints, validation, and evaluation systems that make model-assisted decisions safe to use in production.

• Work directly with hospital IT teams and EHR vendors: technical discovery, implementation, joint debugging, and onboarding.

• Take responsibility for the full lifecycle of your work: design, deployment, monitoring, incident response, and iteration from real-world data.

Who you are

• 3+ years building and operating production systems in complex, messy domains. We care more about demonstrated judgment and ownership than an exact number of years.

• Experience using LLMs as production components—not just developer tools. You understand when to use models, when deterministic systems are better, how to constrain outputs, and how to evaluate reliability.

• Strong data-modelling instincts. You know when abstraction creates leverage and when it hides important real-world variation.

• Comfort working from incomplete information. You form hypotheses, test them against data, and distinguish unknowns that can wait from assumptions that could invalidate the system.

• Confidence in customer-facing technical work: discovery calls, debugging sessions, and direct conversations with vendors and hospital IT teams.

• Experience with cloud infrastructure and distributed systems.

• A practical, hands-on approach: equally comfortable designing an integration architecture and writing a quick script to answer an urgent question.

This role may be a strong fit if

You enjoy reverse-engineering systems you do not control, finding structure in messy real-world data, and turning one-off discoveries into reusable software. You are comfortable being the engineer in the room with customers and partners.

What this role is not

• Consulting or bespoke delivery work. Each integration must improve the product and reduce the marginal cost of the next.

• A role insulated from customers or operational reality.

• Pure platform engineering or pure integration work: the value comes from doing both.

• A role where incorrect mappings are merely technical defects. In this domain, they can produce incorrect invoices.

Bonus points

• Experience with healthcare interoperability or coding standards, including HL7v2, FHIR, or national messaging and reimbursement standards.

• Experience building and operating third-party integrations at scale.

• Experience in healthcare, fintech, or another regulated environment.

• Experience in an early-stage or fast-growing company.

• Working proficiency in Danish, or German.

Our tech stack

• Python

• Django

• React

• PostgreSQL

• AWS

• K8s

• Terraform

• Bedrock

• We’re pragmatic. You’ll have a big say in how it evolves.

What Apylon offers

• The chance to solve one of Europe’s biggest healthcare inefficiencies.

• Competitive salary + stock options (you’ll own part of what you build).

• 25 days of annual leave + local public holidays.

• Lunch on us during workdays at the office.

• Regular off-sites and social events. We like building together, not just working together.

• Travel within the EU roughly monthly. Onboarding a hospital, working through an integration with a vendor’s engineers, or spending time on-site to understand how the data is actually produced. If travelling to a hospital basement to figure out why an export is malformed sounds like a bad week, this isn’t your role.

Working at Apylon means embarking on a highly ambitious mission to rebuild the financial infrastructure of European healthcare. We’re already live with leading private hospitals, processing thousands of invoices, proving that complex payer rules can be turned into code, powering transparent, automated, and intelligent revenue systems.

How to apply. If you're excited by the challenge of building intelligent, high-impact systems at the core of European healthcare and enjoy shipping fast, we'd love to hear from you.

**Contact The Hiring Manager

**Nicolò Calcavecchia

CTO & Co-founder

nicolo@apylon.co

Are you looking for new challenges? Would you like to work alongside skilled colleagues in an educational and dynamic environment where professional excellence and high-quality patient care are top priorities?
You can expect a varied, fast-paced and sometimes unpredictable working day, with plenty of responsibility. In return, we promise you a workplace characterised by high job satisfaction and a strong sense of teamwork, where there is always room for humour and a smile, no matter how busy things get.

About Anaesthesia Unit 1
The unit covers several specialties and operates across two hospital sites. You will primarily be based at the new Hospital City East (Hospitalsbyen Øst), with only occasional shifts at Aalborg South. This advertisement describes the position within Anaesthesia Unit 1 East, which will be your primary place of employment.
We bring together two specialties in a combined orthopaedic and neurosurgical anaesthesia unit.

Neurosurgical anaesthesia
We provide anaesthesia for:

• Intracranial surgery
• Conventional spinal and neurosurgery
• Surgery involving pain stimulation electrodes
Orthopaedic anaesthesia
We provide anaesthesia for both children and adults across all orthopaedic subspecialties, covering everything from day surgery to major spinal surgery.
In addition, our responsibilities include:

• Providing emergency anaesthesia services for acutely ill medical patients in the Acute Treatment Centre (ATC).
• Receiving trauma patients as part of the hospital's trauma team.
• Managing patient transfers both within and outside the North Denmark Region.
• Providing anaesthesia for interventional radiology procedures.
• Providing anaesthesia for MRI and CT scans.
We operate a total of eight operating theatres each day.
Our team consists of approximately 34 anaesthetic nurses, including a Nurse Manager, two coordinating anaesthetic nurses, anaesthetic nurses working in the U and UU functions, and specialist pain nurses.
The unit is also a clinical training site for:

• Nurses undertaking specialist training in anaesthesia.
• First-semester nursing students.
• Anaesthesiology doctors undertaking specialist training.
• Ambulance practitioners and paramedics.
• Medical personnel from the Danish Armed Forces.
Make a Difference with Us
As an anaesthetic nurse, your primary responsibility will be to provide anaesthesia for both elective and emergency patients.
You will quickly develop your ability to assess, analyse and make the right clinical decisions, working alongside a broad team of highly skilled colleagues who make a real difference to our patients every day.
What We Offer
You can look forward to a challenging role with considerable responsibility and the opportunity to work across several specialties. You will also be involved in emergency anaesthesia duties throughout the hospital.
The position involves a rotating shift pattern, including weekend shifts.
In addition, we offer:

• Skilled, positive and dedicated colleagues who are committed to their own professional development and to advancing anaesthetic nursing
• A team that places great importance on maintaining a positive working environment
• The opportunity to submit preferences for your shift schedule through our OPTIMA scheduling system
You will be in good hands from your very first day. Throughout your induction period, you will be supported by experienced colleagues who will ensure that you are well prepared to undertake your responsibilities independently.
You will also have opportunities to attend relevant professional development courses, including:

• Courses at Aalborg University Hospital's Skills and Simulation Centre (Nord Sim).
• Simulation-based training within the unit.
• ATCN (Advanced Trauma Care for Nurses).
• Courses offered through FSAIO, both nationally and internationally.
About You
You contribute to a positive and respectful working environment and enjoy collaborating with colleagues in a busy setting involving complex, multidisciplinary care.
You are recognised for your ability to communicate clearly and respectfully, including in challenging situations that require immediate action and sound clinical judgement.
In addition, you:

• Hold a recognized specialist qualification in anaesthetic nursing.
• Already has or can obtain a Danish Authorization in accordance with Danish law
• Are fluent in Danish, Norwegian or Swedish (preferably)
• Can communicate effectively with both patients and colleagues and actively contribute to a positive working environment in an ever-changing workplace.
• Have a positive attitude towards change and development. We experience plenty of both, whether we are refining our daily workflows or adapting to the new facilities and working procedures at Hospital City East.

jobs.description:
As Chief Quantum Officer at the Technical University of Denmark (DTU), you will bring the university’s quantum research communities together around shared priorities. You will build the relationships and partnerships needed to turn those priorities into joint initiatives and secure external funding for them.

DTU hosts internationally recognised research, innovation, and education activities across quantum computing, quantum communication, quantum sensing, quantum materials, and advanced quantum device fabrication. As discoveries in quantum science find new applications in industry and society, you will help shape DTU’s contribution in Denmark and internationally.

You will build on the foundations already in place, developing DTU’s quantum strategy further and leading its implementation. Working across technology, strategy and organisational development, you will turn strategic priorities into concrete initiatives and strengthen DTU’s ability to coordinate work across departments. You will build trust with researchers, industry partners, policymakers and funding organisations and bring them together around shared goals.

As a visible representative of DTU, you will strengthen collaboration with universities and other partners in Denmark and across the Nordic countries. You will also represent DTU’s interests in international policy discussions and help shape strategies that strengthen its position in the global quantum ecosystem.

Quantum DTU is DTU's central platform for quantum activities and serves as a catalyst for collaboration across disciplines, departments, and external partners. It is anchored in the Office of Scientific Advice, Defence and Resilience, which is a part of the Department for Research, Advice and Innovation. You will work closely with DTU’s departments and central administration, drawing on their expertise in research, strategy, partnerships and organisational support.

Primary areas of responsibility

Strategic leadership and organisational development

• Lead the implementation and continued development of DTU's quantum strategy, translating strategic ambitions into concrete initiatives, partnerships, and measurable outcomes.
• Further develop Quantum DTU as DTU's coordinating platform for strategic quantum initiatives across research, innovation, education, and external partnerships.
• Advise DTU leadership on strategic opportunities, investments, and developments within the quantum field. 
• Develop Quantum DTU's organisational capabilities, structures, and networks in close collaboration with DTU's departments and relevant central administrative functions.
• Support the Chair and Steering Committee of Quantum DTU in strategic planning, preparation of decisions, and follow-up on agreed priorities and initiatives.
Partnerships and stakeholder engagement

• Represent DTU in national and international quantum initiatives, networks, and partnerships. 
• Establish and maintain strategic relationships with public authorities, funding agencies, industry partners, investors, and international organisations. 
• Strengthen DTU's position within the Danish, European, and international quantum 
research, innovation, and policy agendas through partnerships and engagement.

Research, innovation, and ecosystem development

• Drive collaboration across DTU's quantum-related research, education, and innovation activities.
• Facilitate internal coordination, knowledge sharing, and collaboration across DTU's quantum research environments and departments.
• Contribute to strategic initiatives, major funding opportunities, and resource planning in collaboration with relevant administrative functions.
• Promote the translation of quantum research into societal, industrial, and commercial impact. 
• Facilitate engagement with key stakeholders through workshops, strategic initiatives, and high-level visits and delegations.
Your background
You bring substantial knowledge of and experience in quantum science or technology. You can discuss scientific and technological developments with researchers, earn their trust and use your expertise to help set a direction for DTU’s quantum activities.

Ideal profile and qualifications:

• You have experience in quantum science or technology or a solid understanding of the scientific and technological developments shaping the field.
• You have significant insight into the quantum field and can engage effectively with leading researchers and build trust across DTU’s quantum research community.
• You combine technical insight with strategic and political awareness, and you understand how academia, industry and public-sector stakeholders work together to drive technological development.

• You have experience building organisations, programmes, partnerships or ecosystems in collaboration with academic and administrative stakeholders.
• You excel at building relationships and have strong communication, facilitation and stakeholder management skills.
• You can communicate complex technological topics to diverse audiences.
• You hold a relevant advanced degree in science, engineering, technology, innovation, public policy or a related field. 
What we offer

• A unique opportunity to shape DTU's future role within quantum technologies.
• A highly visible strategic role with broad internal and external engagement.
• The opportunity to build and develop Quantum DTU as a strategic platform.
• An ambitious, international, and collaborative working environment. 
Salary and appointment terms
The appointment will be based on the collective agreement with the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations (AC). You are employed as an Senior Officer or Senior Executive Officer. In addition, supplements can be negotiated in accordance with DTU’s salary structure for academic staff employed in technical-administrative positions at DTU (AC TAP): https://www.inside.dtu.dk/en/human-resources/during-employment/salary/salary-structures

The position is permanent and full-time (37 hours per week). Starting date as soon as possible (according to mutual agreement).

If you would like additional information about the position, please contact Head of Office, Kasper Dam Schultz, +45 61 33 51 20 kadam@dtu.dk. Read more about DTU at www.dtu.dk.

All interested candidates irrespective of age, gender, disability, race, religion or ethnic background are encouraged to apply. As DTU works with research in critical technology, which is subject to special rules for security and export control, open-source background checks may be conducted on qualified candidates for the position.
