jobs.occupation: PhD Scholarship in Electronic-Photonic Integration: Merging Photonic and CMOS Chips for Scalable Information Processing - DTU Electro
jobs.description:
The rapid growth of artificial intelligence has made data movement a key bottleneck in computing hardware. Integrated photonics is therefore increasingly used to interconnect electronic processors at a far lower energy per bit than electrical links. Scaling up photonic circuits themselves also requires integrated electronics for large-scale control and stabilization of many optical components in applications, such as biomedical imaging and control of atom-based quantum computers. We offer a PhD scholarship at DTU Electro, where you will develop the 3D integration of photonic and CMOS chips forming the foundation for future technologies.

Our photonic circuits are made in thin-film lithium niobate (TFLN), which is transparent from the visible to the mid-infrared. Its electro-optic effect allows fast modulation of light without adding optical loss. Our team has recently shown that photonic crystal cavities in TFLN can serve as ultracompact modulators [1] with electrically controllable coupling to waveguides [2], and they can route light between many ports [3]. Small cavities need little energy to drive, but their resonances drift with temperature and fabrication variations. Scaling up circuits therefore requires alignment and stabilization of all resonators via local electronic feedback in addition to high-speed modulation. We work closely with our collaborators at Harvard University, whose research has shaped the TFLN field [4]. 

In the project EPIC, funded by the Independent Research Fund Denmark, you will contribute to the design, fabrication, and characterization of devices that join TFLN photonic circuits to custom CMOS chips from our microelectronics team by flip-chip bonding. The aim is to keep many resonator-based modulators, driven at gigahertz speeds, stable at visible and near-infrared wavelengths across a chip. This calls for careful co-design of the photonics with integrated photodetectors, feedback circuits, and drive electronics.

Responsibilities and qualifications
You will help drive the experimental work in EPIC from co-design to demonstration. You will work closely with Professor Per Lynggaard's CMOS design team, other PhD students, postdocs, and senior researchers at DTU, and our collaborators at Harvard University. Depending on your interests, you will have the opportunity to:

• Co-design photonic cavities, couplers, and electronic interfaces using optical, thermal, and circuit simulations.
• Fabricate photonic circuits in DTU Nanolab’s state-of-the-art cleanroom.
• Develop flip-chip bonding of photonic and CMOS chips.
• Explore feedback schemes that stabilize many cavities across a chip.
• Characterize assembled devices using high-speed electro-optic measurements.
• Present your results at international conferences and in leading journals.
You enjoy hands-on laboratory work and learning across disciplines, and you take ownership of the progress and quality of your work.

Required qualifications:

• A strong background in photonics, optics, or electronics.
• Experimental experience in photonics, optics, or electronics, e.g., from your master’s project.
• Programming experience in Python.
Desired qualifications:

• Nanofabrication or integrated photonics.
• Analog circuit design or high-speed electronics.
• A letter motivating the application (cover letter)
• Curriculum vitae 
• Grade transcripts and BSc/MSc diploma (in English) including official description of grading scale
You must have a two-year master's degree (120 ECTS points) or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Approval and Enrolment 
The scholarship for the PhD degree is subject to academic approval, and the candidate will be enrolled in one of the general degree programmes at DTU. For information about our enrolment requirements and the general planning of the PhD study programme, please see DTU's rules for the PhD education. 

Assessment
Assessment of the candidates will be carried out by Associate Professor Mikkel Heuck and Professor Per Lynggaard.

We offer
DTU is a leading technical university globally recognized for the excellence of its research, education, innovation and scientific advice. We offer a rewarding and challenging job in an international environment. We strive for academic excellence in an environment characterized by collegial respect and academic freedom tempered by responsibility.

Salary and appointment terms

The period of employment is 3 years.

You can read more about career paths at DTU here.

Further information 
Further information may be obtained from Associate Professor Mikkel Heuck (mheu@dtu.dk).

You can read more about our department at www.electro.dtu.dk.

If you are applying from abroad, you may find useful information on working in Denmark and at DTU at DTU – Moving to Denmark. Furthermore, you have the option of joining our monthly free seminar “PhD relocation to Denmark and startup “Zoom” seminar” for all questions regarding the practical matters of moving to Denmark and working as a PhD at DTU. 

Application procedure

DTU Electro  
DTU Electro employs more than 300 skilled researchers with competencies in electrical and photonics engineering. As a department, we strive towards creating sustainable energy and a greener internet, as well as strengthening cyber security and health technology. Working with industry and public organizations is one of our top priorities to find and implement new solutions to our society. We aim to offer education, research, and innovation of the highest standard, and our focus on application-oriented research enables us to work across many engineering disciplines and research areas, such as IT and the medical and health sciences. We have a close collaboration with researchers from all over the world, just as we collaborate with industry and public authorities about the dissemination of solutions based on electrical and photonics engineering as their key enabling technologies.

HSE Manager **at atNorth

**At atNorth, we build and operate critical infrastructure for the digital future. As an HSE Manager, you will play a key role in ensuring our data center campus in Skovlunde operate safely, sustainably, and in full compliance with legal and ISO requirements. Working closely with site, project, and contractor teams, you will lead the practical implementation of atNorth’s HSE framework and help embed strong safety and environmental practices into daily work.

**Key responsibilities:

**

• Support implementation and maintenance of atNorth's Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Framework and Integrated Management System (IMS)

• Help embed strong occupational health, safety and environmental practices

• Ensure compliance with applicable HSE legislation, permits, company standards, client requirements, ISO 45001 and ISO 14001

• Monitor daily site activities to verify implementation of risk controls and promote safe behaviours

• Support incident reporting and investigations, ensuring lessons learned are shared and actions are effective

**

• Bachelor’s degree in Occupational Health & Safety, Environmental Studies, Engineering, or similar, or equivalent practical experience

• Confident communicator, able to engage with employees, contractors, and site management

• Proactive, collaborative, and comfortable working across multiple sites and stakeholders

• Fluency in English. Fluency in Danish is strong advantage.

**About The AtNorth Culture

We don’t just talk about culture; we nurture it. Through regular one-to-one engagements and monthly wellbeing surveys, we listen carefully to our teams, ensuring that every voice is heard and every opportunity for improvement is embraced.

We recognize that innovation and collaboration thrive where people feel truly connected, which is why we come together each week to share ideas, strengthen relationships, and nurture a sense of belonging, sometimes over a simple breakfast and good conversation.

At atNorth, we are building a community where you can do your best work and shape a sustainable future together. #99

From discovery to deployment, you’ll shape the data, triggers and lifecycle journeys that support client growth.

**Join our Marketing Automation team

**WHY WORK AT JOE & THE JUICE

**JOE & THE JUICE is a people-centric food and beverage company built around culture, offering much more than just juice, sandwiches, and coffee.

We believe in four simple virtues that shape everything we do:

• Positive Attitude

• Inclusion

• Social Ties

• Growth

For us, this means that when you choose a cup-half-full mindset, welcome people from every background, build real friendships across the bar by creating great guest experiences, and use every shift as a chance to learn something new, you become more than just a Juicer; like us, you continue to search and find purpose and meaning in what you do.

From your first day, you'll be part of an international network of Juicers who support each other, celebrate wins together, and push each other to grow. You will learn by doing and move through our Moneyball career path, our internal system that tracks your performance and fast-tracks you toward promotion. Most of our leaders have earned their stripes behind the bar (fun fact: over 75% of our employees started as Juicers!), so you will always be part of a company built on that same journey. If you love a fast-paced environment, music, and people, and you like the idea of turning a job into a lifestyle, JOE can become a place to build skills, friendships, and a career that takes you across cities, countries, and roles.

**JOB SUMMARY

**The Senior Associate Accounts Payable is responsible for ensuring accurate, compliant, and timely processing of supplier invoices and payments globally, safeguarding financial integrity and operational efficiency. The role delivers high-quality Accounts Payable execution, supports month-end and audit processes, and acts as a reliable point of contact for suppliers and internal stakeholders. As part of the Finance team, this position contributes to strong financial governance, VAT compliance, and continuous process improvement, supporting the company's scalability and commercial performance. The role is a full-time position and reports to the AP Manager.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

**

• Process and validate supplier invoices, ensuring accurate coding, proper approvals, VAT compliance, and high-quality data integrity.

• Manage supplier communication and vendor onboarding, resolving invoice and payment-related queries in a timely, structured, and service-oriented manner while coordinating effectively with internal stakeholders.

• Perform monthly reconciliations, including vendor statement reconciliations, vendor subledger reviews, and balance sheet reconciliations to ensure financial accuracy and completeness.

• Support month-end closing activities by ensuring Accounts Payable accuracy and timely reporting in line with internal controls and accounting standards.

• Contribute to audit processes by providing documentation, analysis, and reconciliation support to ensure compliance and transparency.

• Drive continuous improvement within Accounts Payable processes by identifying inefficiencies, enhancing controls, and supporting automation or standardization initiatives.

• Ensure adherence to company policies, financial controls, and regulatory requirements, maintaining strong governance within the AP function.

**KEY EXPECTATIONS

**In this role, you take ownership of your workload, manage moderately complex tasks, and help improve processes. You work independently, propose solutions, and adapt quickly when priorities shift. Your solid knowledge makes you a dependable contributor who helps drive team performance.

**OUR BENEFITS

**We offer a benefits package that includes a paid pension plan, health insurance, parental leave, and additional vacation. Besides that, we provide some JOE-ified benefits:

• Our global headquarters is conveniently located in the heart of beautiful Copenhagen, where over 200 friendly faces come together!

• Fantastic office facilities, including a fully staffed JOE & THE JUICE bar, where we serve delicious breakfast, daily lunch, refreshing juices, and top-notch barista coffee.

• At JOE, we embrace a flat hierarchy that values every opinion, creating a welcoming space for your ideas and suggestions to thrive.

• Lively monthly social calendar filled with fun activities like running club, wine tasting, creative evenings, and Friday bars - there's always something exciting happening!

• As part of our team, you'll have the opportunity to take on a BTC (Behind the Counter) shift in one of our bars twice a year, adding a unique touch to your experience.

• Ready to turn a job into a lifestyle?

**ABOUT JOE & THE JUICE

**Founded in Copenhagen in 2002, JOE & THE JUICE has grown into a global fast-casual concept with more than 500 locations across 25+ countries and over 7,000 employees worldwide, with our sights set on 1,000 stores by 2028.

Our people-centric culture and sustainability agenda are part of our Nordic heritage, and remain central to our commitment to a better future. Along the way, internal workshops and mentorship sharpen your skills, while exchange programs and international assignments can take you across our markets.

Ready to embark on this exciting journey? Apply today and become a part of JOE & THE JUICE!

**The Impact You'll Make

**As a Customer Experience Account Manager, you will play a key role in strengthening relationships with some of our most important customers across Europe while helping create long-term customer value through strong relationships, operational excellence, and cross-functional collaboration.

You will join Danfoss Turbocor®, the pioneer and market leader in oil-free centrifugal compressor technology for commercial HVAC and refrigeration systems. As demand for sustainable cooling and heating solutions continues to grow, Danfoss Turbocor® is helping shape the future of the industry.

To support our continued growth, we are looking for a Customer Experience Account Manager who is excited to build strong customer partnerships and help deliver exceptional business outcomes.

You will act as a trusted partner to customers and internal stakeholders, helping navigate complex situations, coordinating across functions, and ensuring successful outcomes for strategic customer accounts. Your ability to combine relationship management, operational insight, and problem-solving will directly contribute to customer satisfaction, business growth, and long-term customer partnerships.

As part of a newly established and rapidly growing team, you'll have the opportunity to help shape processes, influence how we work, and make a visible impact from day one. Success in this role requires a proactive and self-driven approach, strong collaboration skills, and the ability to thrive in a dynamic international environment.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**As the primary partner for your customer portfolio, you will serve as the key link between customers and the business, ensuring successful execution while strengthening long-term relationships.

**You Will

**

• Act as a trusted business partner for a portfolio of strategic customer accounts across Europe

• Coordinate complex customer requirements, major business opportunities, commercial commitments, and operational activities to ensure successful execution and long-term customer success

• Build and maintain strong relationships with customers and key stakeholders, creating long-term partnerships based on trust and collaboration

• Partner closely with Sales, Supply Chain, Operations, Customer Service, and other functions to remove barriers and deliver business-critical outcomes

• Use data, insights, and analytical thinking to anticipate challenges, drive resolution, and continuously improve customer outcomes and account performance

As part of a fast-growing team, you will also contribute to establishing new ways of working, improving customer-facing processes, and helping scale a world-class customer partnership function.

**What We're Looking For

**We are looking for a proactive and relationship-oriented professional who enjoys building strong partnerships, coordinating across functions, and finding solutions in a dynamic and fast-paced environment.

**Essential Qualifications

**

• Experience acting as a trusted partner to customers, coordinating across functions, resolving complex challenges, and building long-term business relationships

• Experience working with ERP and CRM systems, including SAP SD (Sales & Distribution) and Salesforce CRM

• Strong analytical, critical-thinking, and problem-solving skills, with the ability to remain calm, accurate, and fact-based under pressure

• Fluency in Danish and English, along with excellent written and verbal communication skills

• The ability to manage multiple priorities, handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion, and build strong relationships across cultures, stakeholders, and functions

**Preferred Qualifications

**Experience working within manufacturing or another industry with complex products and customer requirements would be beneficial. Experience in Danfoss or a similar global matrix organization, as well as exposure to high-growth or start-up environments, would be an advantage.

Additional language skills in German, French, or Italian would be highly appreciated.

**What You'll Get From Us

**You'll help engineer a better future by contributing to solutions that make a real difference around the world.

You'll work with innovative technology that is helping transform the HVAC and refrigeration industry through more energy-efficient and sustainable solutions. You'll join a growing team where your ideas, initiative, and contributions will help shape the future of customer partnerships within the business.

We'll support your career growth with mentoring, learning opportunities, and access to global career paths.

You'll have the flexibility, autonomy, and support you need to do your best work while maintaining a healthy work-life balance.

You'll be part of an inclusive workplace where people of all backgrounds are respected, valued, and empowered to succeed.

You'll receive a competitive rewards package that includes benefits such as an annual bonus, pension plans, health insurance, and more. As a global company, these benefits vary by country and contract.

**Ready to Make a Difference?

**If you're excited by the opportunity to build strong customer partnerships, work with market-leading technology, and help deliver sustainable solutions in a global environment, we'd love to hear from you.

Even if your experience doesn't align perfectly with every preferred qualification, we encourage you to apply. We recognize that different backgrounds, experiences, and perspectives strengthen our teams and contribute to better outcomes for our customers and our business.

For information about the recruitment process, please contact Talent Acquisition Partner, Gerd Veierskov, +45 3057 1882

**Our Commitment to Transparency

**Salary ranges listed reflect only primary location and currency. For local salary ranges and specific benefits in your preferred hiring location, please ask your Talent Acquisition representative for more information.

The actual salary offer will carefully consider a wide range of factors, including your skills, qualifications, experience, and location. Any benefits listed do not promise or guarantee any particular benefit or specific action. They may depend on country or contract specifics and are subject to change at any time without prior notice.

jobs.occupation: IT Security Specialist, Security Operations - Aarhus or Gdansk
jobs.description:
Are you driven by detecting, investigating and stopping security threats, and do you want to help strengthen how a global company protects its business every day?

“Our Security Operations team protects Arla’s systems and data around the clock. In this role, you will take ownership of key parts of our detection and response capabilities, work closely with our security service providers to continuously improve them, and share your expertise with colleagues across IT,” says Poul Henrik Tang Jensen, Senior Manager, Head of IT Product.

How you will make an impact

You will join IT Security Operations within IT Foundation, where you will take ownership of assigned Security Operations capabilities across endpoint, identity, network, application and cloud environments. Our technology landscape includes Microsoft and Palo Alto security technologies across SIEM, XDR, endpoint and identity.

You will work closely with our managed security service providers, who perform much of the day-to-day security monitoring, investigation and technical execution. Your role is to ensure these services deliver the detection, response and protection capabilities Arla needs.

Your key responsibilities will include:

• 
Taking ownership of assigned Security Operations capabilities and ensuring they remain effective, relevant and aligned with Arla’s risks and business needs.

• 
Overseeing security monitoring and investigations performed by our managed security service providers, challenging findings and providing technical direction on complex cases and incidents.

• 
Coordinating incident response across service providers and internal teams, including containment, eradication, recovery, escalation and follow-up.

• 
Driving improvements to detection rules, correlation logic, automation workflows and incident-response playbooks, working with our service providers on implementation.

• 
Assessing vulnerabilities and security-control weaknesses

• 
Managing the technical quality and performance of our security service providers, setting priorities and ensuring agreed improvements are implemented.

• 
Providing practical, risk-based security advice and assessments to projects and product teams.

• 
Leading Security Operations improvement initiatives and sharing security expertise across IT.

What will make you successful

You take ownership and follow issues through to a clear conclusion. When a security incident unfolds, you remain calm, analytical and decisive. You are comfortable working independently, while recognising when collaboration or escalation is needed. The ideal candidate brings:

• A relevant bachelor’s or master’s degree in IT, cybersecurity or a related field, or equivalent professional experience.

• Typically 5+ years of relevant cybersecurity experience, including substantial experience within Security Operations, security monitoring, investigation and incident response.

• Experience taking ownership of complex security investigations, incidents or operational security improvements, including coordinating technical activities across internal teams and external security providers.

• Solid technical knowledge of SIEM, SOAR, EDR, network and identity-security monitoring, and vulnerability management.

• Practical understanding of attacker techniques and security frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK, NIST and ISO 27001.

• Good understanding of security logging, telemetry, evidence collection and forensic-analysis principles.

• Good understanding of security queries, scripting and automation, enabling you to assess technical solutions, challenge implementation choices and drive improvements with security service providers.

• Experience working with and providing technical direction to managed security service providers, while collaborating effectively with internal technology and product teams.

• A relevant professional security certification, or equivalent demonstrable expertise.

• Experience with technologies such as Microsoft Sentinel, Defender XDR, KQL, Palo Alto or similar enterprise security platforms would be an advantage.

What do we offer?

This position is based in either Aarhus, Denmark or Gdansk, Poland. You will be part of an on-call rotation, approximately every seventh week, to provide support in case of critical issues.

You will join a skilled and collaborative IT Security Operations team with a central role in protecting a global market leader. You will have real ownership of our Security Operations capabilities and the opportunity to lead technical workstreams and improvement initiatives.

Would you like to join us?

If you want to help keep Arla secure and make our Security Operations capabilities even stronger, we would love to hear from you. Please apply as soon as possible, as we review applications on an ongoing basis and may close the recruitment once the right candidate has been found.

For more information, please contact Poul Henrik Tang Jensen, Senior Manager, Head of IT Product Security Operations, at pohtj@arlafoods.com.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

Procurement Category Manager for Filling equipment (Capex), Aarhus, Düsseldorf or Bremen.

Are you ambitious, driven, and looking to make a significant impact in a fast-changing environment, where you will take lead to ensure sourcing of production equipment to our dairies is optimized and cost competitive? And, do you know how to set strategic direction for your category, build and lead supplier relations to ensure a compliant and competitive supplier portfolio?

You will join a team of procurement colleagues, whom are passionate to ensure that the supplier base availably for production equipment is not just capable to deliver to quality and standards fit for future, they are also dedicated to ensure healthy competition in sourcing projects. Together with key stakeholders, we define the required sourcing strategy ahead and we aim to manage supplier relations accordingly,” says Procurement Senior Director Ninna Normand Helles.

How You Will Make an Impact

Being based in one of our offices in either Aarhus, Düsseldorf or Bremen, you will take global ownership of the Capex category of filling equipment. You will take lead to define, execute and mature the category strategies. You will manage strategic Supplier Relations and ensure to define and manage a portfolio of compliance and relevant suppliers within your category to ensure competitive sourcing can be performed in all capex projects and tenders.

Besides your category responsibility, you will take sourcing lead of key Capex projects and engage actively with the Project Manager to ensure relevant, compliant and competitive supplier selection in the project. This included definition of tender packages in the project, creation of sourcing plan in alignment with the project team, selection and onboarding of suppliers, management of tenders, negotiations and finalization of contracts.

Successfully navigating the complexity of your sourcing projects as well as your designated sourcing category, your key responsibilities will include:

• Defining and driving Category strategy, commitment and engagement of key stakeholders and execution of relevant actions to deploy strategic direction.

• Ensure a compliant and relevant supplier portfolio in your category by establishing framework agreements with relevant suppliers to cover business demand and ensure competition.

• Establishing, developing and lead strong, long-lasting and dynamic supplier relationships and ensure annual SRM plans are conducted.

• Lead and manage execution all sourcing activities in key Capex projects with high level of complexity and time dependencies, including sourcing plan, supplier selection, tendering, negotiation and contracting.

• Set sourcing and negotiation strategy and take lead to execute accordingly to ensure competitive sourcing and objective supplier evaluation and rewarding.

• Working closely together with key stakeholder internally to ensure successful and competitive execution of sourcing projects.

• Conduct supplier and site visits to maintain knowledge of equipment and competences and challenges among suppliers as well as internally at Arla sites.

In terms of travel, you can expect approximately 20-30 days per year to maintain supplier relations and visit Arla dairies at various locations in Europe.

What Will Make You Successful

Your qualifications include a Master’s degree and at least 5 years of experience in a similar role from a global organization. Your innate project management mindset, coupled with strong analytical skills, allows you to seamlessly transition from a high-level strategic view to execution and diving deep for valuable insights. You excel in business partnering, building positive relationships, and effectively managing stakeholders at all levels of the organization. Your thoughtful communication and flexible project management ensure smooth and efficient processes.

Having profound understanding of complex negotiations, capex contracts, and the commercial and strategic aspects behind them is equally important in this role. Your experience therefor includes, but is not limited to:

• At least 5 years of extensive experience in strategic sourcing related to Capex/production equipment.

• Profound experience as sourcing lead of complex tender projects and negotiations.

• Experienced Category Management and know how to set and drive a category strategy, and how to establish a compliant and relevant supplier portfolio for your category.

• Good technical understanding and knowledge of Capex/production equipment and understanding of the supplier base across capex categories. Specific knowledge from the food and beverage industry, is a considerable advantage.

• Your fluency in spoken and written English is excellent.

You are fearless when it comes to challenging the status quo, and your courage and exceptional stakeholder management skills empower you to negotiate effectively and rally the right individuals when introducing new ideas. Your genuine interest in our business field drives you to proactively conduct research, ensuring a deep understanding of the global supply market. You thrive in a dynamic, international work environment where objectives and priorities are continuously evolving and developing.

What Do We Offer?

Join a high-performing team with a great culture and spirit, where you’ll have the opportunity to develop your skills and make a real impact. At Arla, we’re committed to professional growth and promoting from within. Our positive and collaborative culture brings out the best in everyone, and you’ll be part of a market leader that produces nutritious, household-favorite brands in a sustainable way - benefiting customers, our farmer-owners, and the world.

Would You Like to Join Us?

We are conducting interviews for this position on an ongoing basis, so please apply as soon as possible. For additional information, please submit our application without further hesitation, as we will close the recruitment when the right candidate has been found.

In case of further questions, you may contact Procurement Senior Director Ninna Normand Helles at ninoh@arlafoods.com

Our global procurement organization is spread across Denmark, Sweden, Germany, the Netherlands, UK, Poland, and Hong Kong. This position will report to Senior Procurement Director of Capex, MRO, utilities and chemicals.

Shape the Future of Dairy

Arla is a global leader in the dairy industry, committed to enabling good food choices that make life better, providing people with nourishment, while taking care at every step to ensure Arla is a choice they can feel good about. If you are looking to shape the future with an ambitious global cooperative that truly cares about your growth, where everyone feels valued and empowered, and collaboration is the core of culture, Arla is a choice you can feel good about.

jobs.occupation: 170023 Professor of Psychotherapy (Part-Time or Clinical Appointment, Fixed-Term for 5 Years)
jobs.description:
Professor of Psychotherapy
 (Part-Time or Clinical Appointment, Fixed-Term for 5 Years)

  Department of Clinical Medicine
 Faculty of Health and Medical Sciences
  University of Copenhagen

  The University of Copenhagen invites applications for a professorship in Psychotherapy. Depending on the qualifications and current position of the successful applicant, the appointment will be made either as a part-time professor combined with a senior researcher position, or as a clinical professor combined with a consultancy at one of the hospitals listed below.

  • Copenhagen University Hospital, Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg, the Mental Health Centre Copenhagen

  • Copenhagen University Hospital – Herlev and Gentofte, Center Stolpegaard

  It is a requirement for appointment that the applicant is accepted for both the professorship and the consultancy/position as senior researcher. In order to be considered for the position, the applicant must send two applications: one to the Faculty (the professorship) and one to the hospital (the consultancy/senior researcher position) cf. the simultaneously advertised position of the consultancy/position as senior researcher. This also applies to applicants who are already employed at one of the hospitals. The advertisements for the consultancies/senior researcher positions are available at:

   	
• Copenhagen University Hospital, Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg: https://www.sundhedsjobs.dk 	
• Copenhagen University Hospital – Herlev and Gentofte: https://www.sundhedsjobs.dk   Both the professorship and the consultancy/position as senior researcher will be financed by the relevant hospital.

  Find information about the department.

  Job description
 In the consideration of applications for the professorship, the main emphasis will be on the applicant's ability to document a high level of original scientific work at an international level within the area of psychiatry or psychology.

  The professor’s responsibilities will primarily consist of:

   	
• Research, including publication/academic dissemination. The realization of psychotherapeutic treatment of patients with psychiatric disorders, including new technologies, implies great potential. The professorship aims to ensure the scientific development of psychotherapeutic treatment of patients with psychiatric disorders, including outcome - and process studies, and new technologies as a supplement to psychotherapeutic practice, and to ensure implementation in clinical practice.   	
• Research-based teaching, including associated examination. The professor shall conduct research-based teaching in psychotherapy within different psychiatric disorders, including new technologies. 	
• Research leadership, including guidance and supervision of researchers. The professor shall overall plan and develop research initiatives within psychotherapy and aid in implementing results into clinical practice. 	
• Obligation to share knowledge with the rest of society, including participation in public debate 	
• Academic assessments   Required qualifications 
 To be qualified for a professorship, you will be assessed according to these five overall criteria for recognising merit at the University of Copenhagen: Research, Teaching, Innovation & Societal impact, Organizational contribution, and Leadership. Applicants are encouraged to read the University of Copenhagen's Guidance on the merit criterion Innovation and Societal Impact. Find information about each criterion.

  Furthermore, each applicant must be able to:

   	
• Document a high degree of original academic production at an international level, including considerable contributions to the development of the academic discipline 	
• Manage research and other management functions, e.g. engage in the university’s external academic activities, as well as knowledge and technology transfer 	
• Provide research-based teaching   The professor is also required to possess good interpersonal and communicative skills.

  Terms of employment 
 The position is covered by the Job Structure for Academic Staff at Universities 2025. The position is a fixed-term positions limited to a period of five years. Extension is possible.

  The employers in the combined position may, where necessary, exchange information regarding matters that are of significant relevance to the employment relationship.

  Terms of employment especially for the professor (part time)
 For the position as professor the average weekly working hours are approximately 11 hours per week. Salary and other terms and conditions of appointment are set in accordance with the Agreement between the Ministry of Finance and AC (Danish Confederation of Professional Associations) or other relevant professional organisations.

  This form of employment shall remain in effect until, pursuant to the applicable Job structure for Aacademic Staff, the appointment of non-medical professionals as Clinical Professors becomes possible and an agreement on salary and employment terms for such positions has been concluded with the relevant professional organisations. Upon fulfilment of these conditions, the employment shall be converted to an appointment as Clinical Professor, in accordance with the description set out below.

  Terms of employment especially for the clinical professor
 For the clinical professorship the appointee will receive a pensionable annual honorarium of 219.882,33 DKK (1 August 2026 level)

  Questions
 For further information please contact Head of Department Nicolai W. Albrechtsen, nicolai.albrechtsen@regionh.dk.

  Foreign applicants may find the university’s International Staff Mobility useful.

  Application
 The application must be submitted in English and must include the following documents:

   	
• Application (Including motivations for applying for this position (Maximum 2 pages)) 	
• Curriculum vitae (Including information about external funding) 	
• Diplomas (Master’s and PhD and other relevant certificates) 	
• Uploads of maximum 10 publications to be considered in the assessment 	
• Self-declaration form (Template under ‘Nyttige links’ - Upload the completed and mandatory form as “Other relevant material”) 	
• Teaching portfolio (Guidelines / Template for inspiration under Nyttige links) 	
• Research plan (3‐5 pages) 	
• Teaching plan 	
• A complete list of publications   Application procedure 
 After the expiry of the deadline for applications, the authorized recruitment manager selects applicants for assessment on the advice of the Appointments Committee. All applicants are then immediately notified whether their application has been passed for assessment. The Dean then appoints an expert assessment committee in order to make an assessment of the selected applicants for the specific post. Selected applicants are notified of the composition of the committee. When the assessment committee has completed the assessment, each applicant has the opportunity to comment on the part of the assessment that relates to the applicant him/herself. You can read about the recruitment process at the university's Job Portal.

  Please note that the applicant will be contacted if the assessment committee requires further documentation.

  The applicant will be assessed according to the Ministerial Order no. 242 of 13 March 2012 on the Appointment of Academic Staff at Universities.

  The University of Copenhagen encourages all interested applicants to apply for this position.

**Job Description Summary

**The Production Engineer – Calibration & Maintenance is responsible for the calibration, maintenance, and lifecycle management of production, inspection, measurement, and test equipment used in a regulated medical device manufacturing environment.

The role works closely with Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, equipment owners, and external service providers to ensure equipment remains calibrated, maintained, compliant, and available for production.

Responsibilities include day-to-day calibration and preventive maintenance coordination, HxGN EAM administration, calibration assessments, controlled procedures and work instructions, supplier coordination, and equipment compliance.

This is a hands-on Production Engineering role supporting manufacturing operations across scanner/system assembly, mechanical and electrical/electronic assembly, software configuration/loading, packaging and labeling, and testing/final acceptance.

**Job Description

****Roles & Responsibilities

**

• Coordinate the site calibration program, including calibration schedules, call-in activities, equipment status, due dates, and timely completion.

• Coordinate internal and external calibration activities, including equipment preparation, shipment, return, documentation review, and release back to production.

• Ensure new, returned, overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment is appropriately assessed and controlled before use.

• Act as SME for calibration and maintenance activities in HxGN EAM, maintaining asset records, calibration setups, preventive maintenance schedules, work orders, task plans, and supporting documentation.

• Perform and support calibration assessments, including equipment requirements, criticality, acceptance criteria, calibration methods, frequencies, and maintenance needs.

• Develop and maintain calibration and maintenance procedures, SOPs, and work instructions in collaboration with equipment owners, SMEs, and Quality.

• Coordinate preventive and corrective maintenance activities for production and test equipment while minimizing disruption to manufacturing.

• Support investigations, risk assessments, and product-impact assessments related to overdue, failed, or out-of-tolerance equipment, and provide input to NC/INV/CAPA activities where applicable.

• Coordinate external calibration and maintenance suppliers, including quotations, service activities, documentation, and AGORA purchase orders.

• Support internal and external audits by ensuring calibration and maintenance records are complete, traceable, compliant, and audit-ready.

• Monitor calibration and maintenance performance and drive improvements in equipment compliance, availability, data quality, and execution efficiency.

**Required Qualifications

**

• Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, Metrology, Maintenance, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.

• Experience with calibration, preventive maintenance, equipment management, or Production Engineering in a regulated manufacturing environment.

• Understanding of calibration principles, equipment control, documentation, traceability, and manufacturing process requirements.

• Experience with computerized maintenance or Enterprise Asset Management systems, preferably HxGN EAM or comparable systems.

• Experience working within controlled procedures, work instructions, and change management processes.

• Experience coordinating suppliers, service activities, quotations, and purchase orders.

• Knowledge of GMP and Quality Management System requirements within regulated manufacturing.

**Desired Characteristics

**

• Experience within medical device manufacturing or another highly regulated manufacturing environment.

• Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with high attention to detail.

• Hands-on and practical approach to supporting manufacturing equipment and production operations.

• Structured working style with strong ownership and ability to manage recurring deadlines.

• Strong collaboration skills across Manufacturing, Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and external suppliers.

• Clear written and verbal communication skills.

• Comfortable balancing equipment compliance, production continuity, quality requirements, and operational priorities.

• Proactive and improvement-focused approach to equipment reliability and calibration/maintenance processes

******Relocation Assistance Provided: No

jobs.occupation: Product Manager – Notifications | Help Dalux Users Focus on What Matters
jobs.description:
Product Management at Dalux – Turning Information into Attention

Construction projects generate an enormous amount of information. Files change. Tasks are assigned. Deadlines approach. Comments are added. Reviews require action. Issues are reported. People are mentioned. Workflows progress. But more information does not necessarily make people better informed.

Dalux is looking for a Product Manager to take dedicated ownership of Notifications and help us answer a deceptively difficult product question:

How do we make sure users know what requires their attention – without overwhelming them with information?

Notifications exist throughout our products today, across email, mobile, and in-product experiences. As Dalux has grown, so has their complexity. We believe this area deserves dedicated product ownership and a coherent strategy across our products.

Your responsibilities will include:

• Notification Strategy: Define a coherent product direction for how Dalux communicates important events and required actions to users.

• Product Discovery: Understand when users need to be informed, when they need to take action, and when a notification simply creates unnecessary noise.

• Customer Insights: Research how different users manage information and attention across complex projects and busy working days.

• Cross-product Ownership: Map and improve notification experiences across Dalux products rather than optimizing individual notifications in isolation.

• Channels & Preferences: Develop experiences spanning in-app notifications, email, mobile push, notification preferences, subscriptions, following, mentions, reminders, and digests.

• Relevance & Prioritization: Explore grouping, prioritization, timing, and deduplication to ensure important information stands out.

• Actionability: Make notifications useful by ensuring users understand why they received them, what has changed, and what action they should take.

• Product Analytics: Use quantitative and qualitative insights to understand which notifications create value and which create noise.

• Shared Capabilities: Work with Development and other Product Managers to create common notification principles and platform capabilities that can be reused across Dalux.

About You

You probably don't currently have "Notifications Product Manager" as your job title – and that's perfectly fine.

We're looking for an experienced Product Manager who finds the underlying problem interesting and has the product and systems thinking required to solve it.

We believe you:

• Have strong Product Management experience, preferably from B2B SaaS, collaboration, productivity, workflow, communication, or similar software.

• Have excellent product discovery and UX instincts.

• Think systematically and can turn many individual use cases into coherent product concepts.

• Understand the tension between keeping users informed and creating notification fatigue.

• Are comfortable owning a horizontal capability spanning multiple products and development teams.

• Can combine user research with product analytics to understand behavior.

• Care about interaction details and understand how seemingly small product decisions can have a large cumulative impact on user experience.

• Can simplify complex systems involving events, recipients, relevance, timing, preferences, and communication channels.

• Communicate fluently in English, written and spoken.

Construction Technology Experience Is Welcome But Not Required .

Experience from collaboration, communication, workflow, or productivity software would be particularly relevant.

What To Expect At Dalux

At Dalux, you'll join a product-driven company where ideas quickly become reality and where you'll have a direct impact on the products we build.

We offer:

• A collaborative and informal work environment with flat hierarchies

• High ownership, trust, and the freedom to drive initiatives

• Talented and dedicated colleagues in an international team

• A central Copenhagen office, flexible work hours, and no dress code

• Monthly social events and an active community

• Attractive benefits including health insurance, lunch, fitness facilities, and free parking

• Opportunities for professional growth and development

Ready for the next step?

We are reviewing applications on an ongoing basis, so please submit your resume and application as soon as possible.

About Dalux

Founded in 2005, Dalux is a Danish Contech company revolutionizing the construction industry with innovative software built on geometric processing and 3D computer graphics.

Over the past years, we’ve grown by 40% annually and now have over 900 employees across 50+ offices in more than 25 countries. All product development takes place in our Østerbro, Copenhagen office, where we focus on building the future of construction technology. We place great value on our strong social community and close collaboration with colleagues, which is why we primarily work from our Copenhagen location.

As soon as possible

Reporting to: Senior Director, Clinical Operations

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

Every Hemab trial site starts with a signed contract. As our programmes move into larger, multinational studies in rare bleeding disorders, the speed and quality of site and vendor contracting directly determines when patients can enrol. You'll own that path: getting clinical trial agreements and budgets negotiated, signed and well managed so sites activate on time, and building the contracting processes Hemab will rely on as we scale.

What you'll do

• Own site contracting end to end for Hemab's clinical trials, including clinical trial agreements, site budgets, confidentiality agreements and amendments, so that sites activate on the timelines our study teams have committed to.

• Negotiate fair-market-value site budgets and payment terms across countries, landing agreements that sites will sign quickly and that hold up to audit and internal budget controls.

• Personally negotiate the difficult points, such as indemnity, subject injury, intellectual property, publication rights and data protection, instead of passing them on, and judge when a position is worth holding.

• Partner with Clinical Operations study teams to forecast contracting timelines, flag risks to first-patient-in early and agree on fixes before they turn into delays.

• Build Hemab's clinical contracting toolkit: agreement and budget templates, fallback-position playbooks, contract tracking and clear approval workflows that work across Copenhagen and Cambridge.

• Make sure every agreement meets GCP, data protection, transparency-reporting and anti-bribery requirements, working with Legal, Quality and Finance so our contracts are inspection-ready.

• Oversee contracting delegated to CROs and other vendors: set the standards, monitor performance, and negotiate work orders and change orders that protect budget and timelines.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Substantial hands-on experience negotiating clinical trial agreements and site budgets directly with hospital and academic sites, at a pharma company, biotech or CRO.

• Working knowledge of the contract issues specific to clinical research (indemnity and insurance, subject injury, IP and publication rights, GDPR and HIPAA) and how they vary between countries.

• A track record of moving a portfolio of agreements to signature against site-activation deadlines, including unblocking stalled negotiations.

• Experience working in an ICH-GCP environment, including the compliance obligations that apply to site payments, such as transparency reporting and anti-corruption rules.

• The ability to prioritise competing requests and communicate clearly with study teams, legal counsel and site contract offices across time zones, explaining contract risk in plain terms.

• Professional fluency in written and spoken English.

Nice to have

• Contracting experience in rare-disease or hematology trials, including specialist treatment centres that enroll small numbers of patients.

• Experience building contracting processes, templates or systems at a growing biotech.

• Familiarity with contract lifecycle management or CTMS tools, or with contracting for trials run under the EU Clinical Trials Regulation.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This is the actual shape of working somewhere at this stage: It's genuinely energising for the right person and genuinely frustrating for the wrong one. If you want a place where the operating manual is already written, this might not be it – but if you want to help write it, this might be exactly it.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. If any part of your experience with us falls short of it, tell us.

All applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, creed, gender, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, pregnancy, sex, marital status, gender expression or identity, genetic information, sexual orientation, citizenship, or any other legally protected class.

About Hemab

Hemab is building preventative treatments for serious, underserved bleeding disorders. These are therapies designed to work with the body's own biology and stop bleeds before they start, instead of treating them after they happen. We're patient-first, science-led and clinical-stage - with a pipeline that takes different scientific approaches to different patient needs.

We went public via our 2026 IPO, and we're scaling across two homes: Cambridge, MA, USA, and Copenhagen, Denmark.

The role

As Director, Application Management, you'll build the capabilities Hemab needs to run its business and regulated systems reliably as we grow. Working within IT & Digital, you'll take ownership from solution selection through implementation and ongoing management, making sure technology works for the people who depend on it.

You'll have room to shape how Application Management works at Hemab, deciding what we need now, what can wait and where external partners make more sense than building internally.

What you'll do

• Lead business system implementations from business case and solution selection through go-live, adoption and ongoing management.

• Turn business needs into practical technology solutions that fit Hemab's priorities, architecture and stage of growth.

• Own vendor selection, including RFI/RFP activities, solution evaluation and recommendations.

• Manage implementation partners and application vendors, holding them accountable for delivery, quality and service.

• Work with business owners to make sure systems, controls, training and ways of working are ready before launch.

• Establish application lifecycle management covering performance, upgrades, changes, renewals and vendor relationships.

• Partner with System Owners and Quality to keep regulated and GxP applications compliant and appropriately controlled.

• Build change and release management capabilities, using external specialists where appropriate.

• Work across Quality, Information Security, Data & AI, Legal and IT Operations to make sound technology decisions and build internal capabilities as Hemab grows.

What you'll bring to Hemab

• Experience leading enterprise application implementations from selection through adoption and ongoing management.

• Experience working with regulated systems in biotech, pharma or another regulated life-sciences environment.

• Practical knowledge of GxP requirements, system lifecycle management and the controls needed to maintain compliance.

• Experience managing application vendors, implementation partners and outsourced services.

• Evidence of delivering complex, cross-functional technology projects while managing competing business needs.

• Ability to work with senior stakeholders, make clear recommendations and take accountability for delivery.

Nice to have

• Experience helping a biotech scale from early clinical development towards later-stage maturity.

• Experience building an Application Management function or introducing new ways of working.

• Experience establishing change and release management using external partners.

What to expect, honestly

Hemab is still building a lot of its own structure. Systems here tend to get created as we need them, not handed down in advance. Whoever takes this role will likely build some of their own process instead of inheriting a finished one. We work across two hubs and multiple time zones - bridging that well takes real, deliberate effort. And because we're growing quickly, priorities can shift with less notice than they would at a larger, more established company.

This is the actual shape of working somewhere at this stage: It's genuinely energising for the right person and genuinely frustrating for the wrong one. If you want a place where the operating manual is already written, this might not be it – but if you want to help write it, this might be exactly it.

Why Hemab

At Hemab, your work ultimately connects back to something simple. People living with serious bleeding disorders get something they've never had before - the chance to prevent a bleed, instead of reacting to one after it happens. You'll be joining at a stage where individual decisions still carry real weight, and where your work can help turn promising science into a preventative treatment that actually reaches patients.

How we treat our people is meant to be an extension of how we think about patients: with care, honesty, and respect. We're still building the consistency to back that up across every hiring process, every time. We'd say that plainly instead of pretending otherwise. **

As the Regional Perfo & Transformation Manager at Satair, you will act as the primary representative for the Commercial Process, Performance & Transformation (ASCX) team in your region. jobs.description:
Do you enjoy working with the structures behind fair and competitive pay? And would you like to take ownership of how job architecture, salary structures and Reward practices work across countries and entities?

This is your opportunity to take ownership of key Reward frameworks and help us mature how we work with Reward across ABENA.

As our new Global Reward Specialist, you will take ownership of key areas of our global Reward approach across countries and entities, from job architecture, salary structures and benchmarking to pay equity and Pay Transparency.

It is a role for someone who enjoys both the detail and the bigger picture: working hands-on with Reward data and frameworks while helping HR and leaders make consistent, well-informed decisions and building robust business processes.

And you will not be starting from a blank page. Important foundations are already in place. Your role is to take them further: strengthen our Reward framework, mature our approach to Pay Transparency, and turn structures and data into robust global reward practices that support consistent and well-informed decisions across ABENA.

Your key responsibilities will include

• Own and further develop ABENA’s reward framework, including pay policy, salary and bonus structures, pay ranges and related governance.

• Own and continuously improve our global job architecture, ensuring consistent job evaluation, levels and career paths across the organization.

• Drive and mature our Pay Transparency efforts, including pay equity analyses, pay-gap reporting, related governance and long-term compliance.

• Lead relevant recurring reward processes such as annual salary reviews and compensation analyses.

• Turn reward data into clear recommendations supporting pay decisions, internal equity and competitiveness.

• Advise HR and leaders on reward decisions, job leveling, promotions, new roles and organizational changes.

• Develop communication, training and guidance materials that strengthen reward capabilities and ensure consistent understanding and application of reward principles across ABENA.

What we are looking for

• A proven track record working within Reward, Compensation & Benefits, ideally from an international organization.

• Hands-on experience with job architecture, job evaluation, salary structures, and compensation.

• Strong knowledge of pay equity and EU Pay Transparency, with the ability to turn requirements into practical processes and governance.

• Strong analytical skills and the ability to translate compensation data into clear insights and recommendations.

• A pragmatic and hands-on approach, with the confidence to advise and challenge HR colleagues and leaders across countries and functions.

• Strong Excel and HR systems understanding, together with fluent English and Danish.

Your Team, Our Culture and Values

You will join our Group HR team, working alongside experienced HR specialists and generalists who work closely together, share ideas, and use each other’s different perspectives and expertise. Even when things are busy, we make room for laughter and a good atmosphere. We value collaboration and openness. For us, it is important that we support one another, and that it is genuinely enjoyable to come to work. Creating and maintaining a positive atmosphere and a great team spirit is something we are all responsible for.

Your leader at ABENA will be Lotte Blanner, HR Director, who describes her leadership style as follows:

“Trust and clear direction. I actively seek and value your input in our shared work, and I listen to your ambitions so I can support both your tasks and your development through honest feedback and clear priorities. I value people who take ownership and show initiative. You can count on me to stand by you and back you up along the way. We aim high but set realistic ambitions and take a pragmatic approach to the realities we work within”

At ABENA, you become part of a global company with a clear purpose: making a real difference in people’s everyday lives. Across the organization, we are guided by three core values: Trust, Fairness, and Cooperation. They shape how we work together, make decisions, and take responsibility for moving ABENA forward.

We look forward to hearing from you and receiving your application.

If you are interested in the position, please send your CV as soon as possible. We review applications as we receive them and will close the search once we have found our new colleague.

Read more about our recruitment process here.

If you would like to know more about the role, feel free to contact HR Director Lotte Blanner at +45 5172 7195.

jobs.description:
Legal Counsels for Legal & Compliance department at Novo Nordisk Engineering

If you’re energised by varied legal and compliance work and you thrive on supporting some of the world’s largest pharma engineering projects, we’d love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for two Legal Counsels to join our Legal & Compliance team in Virum, Denmark. You will join a small, dedicated team of colleagues who daily provides timely, commercially relevant legal and compliance advice that enables our line of business to deliver complex engineering projects.

Your role is key in ensuring that NNE navigates complex legal, contractual, and compliance matters effectively, while supporting our colleagues and projects across Denmark, India, and the US. You will report directly to the General Counsel, who heads the Legal & Compliance team globally.

This is a generalist, hands-on role where your time split roughly equally between legal and compliance work. You will see the practical impact of your advice across the organisation, and you will be given responsibility from the outset, while working alongside experienced colleagues who will support your continued development.

If you are qualified as a Danish attorney (advokat), you can retain your practising certificate in this role.

How you might spend your days

As a Legal Counsel, you’ll be:

• Drafting, reviewing and negotiating consultancy agreements and a wide range of other commercial contracts, including supplier, software, framework and data processing agreements

• Advising projects on contractual matters, change orders and claims

• Driving key elements of our compliance programme across business ethics, data protection, confidentiality and AI governance, including internal audits

• Developing and maintaining legal and compliance policies, standards and procedures

• Delivering training and awareness activities across the business

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Taking ownership from the outset, act proactively and look for solutions.

• Collaborating effectively across projects, disciplines and geographies. You build strong, trust-based relationships with stakeholders across the organisation.

• Delivering high-quality work on time and know how to prioritise when things move quickly. You balance legal requirements, business realities and risk.

• Curious, keen to learn and look for ways to improve how we work. You approach new and complex matters with an open mind and challenge constructively when needed.

Information Security Consultant at Novo Nordisk Engineering

If you're energised by information security and thrive in a collaborative environment where you can learn from experienced colleagues while helping protect users, devices, and data, we'd love to hear from you!

Who we are

We are a leading pharma engineering company shaping the future of API pharma engineering globally. Leveraging the expertise of 2,000+ employees across Denmark, India, and the US, we design, build and optimise pharmaceutical manufacturing facilities that are essential to the health and well-being of patients everywhere.

Our success is driven by passion, innovation, and collaboration — with our customers and across our teams and disciplines. If you share our dedication to a noble cause and our passion for API pharma engineering, then NNE is the place for you.

About the role

We are looking for an Information Security Consultant to join our Information Security team in Global IT.

As a team, we are working on keeping NNE’s users, devices and data secure — from handling security incidents to strengthening our security platforms and advising the business on security risks.

Your contribution will be important in protecting NNE day to day and in making security a natural part of how our development and service delivery teamwork.

This is a great opportunity for a recent graduate or someone early in their career: you will work alongside experienced colleagues, take ownership of a wide range of day-to-day security tasks, and gradually take on more complex work as you build your skills.

How you might spend your days

As an Information Security Consultant you’ll be:

• Handling security incidents, such as phishing triage and investigations, together with experienced colleagues

• Maintaining and improving our security setup across our Microsoft security platforms

• Supporting device management, including personal devices (BYOD) and security groups

• Answering security-related questions from colleagues and contributing to security risk assessments

• Taking part in security initiatives and projects in close collaboration with our development and service delivery teams

Who you are

We care about who you are as a person. In the end, how you work, and your energy is what impacts the results we achieve as a team. As a person, you are:

• Proactive and happy to take the initiative on security improvements

• Curious and eager to learn, especially when new technical problems come up

• Interested in building relationships with colleagues and explaining security in plain language

• Structured in how you plan and follow through on your tasks

• Comfortable working with colleagues across teams, disciplines and cultures

What you bring to the role

In all positions, there are some things that are preferred, and others, a bonus. If you do not meet all the qualifications listed below, you are welcome to offer alternative experience that you think would be valuable in this role:

• You have a recent degree in IT, computer science, cybersecurity or a related field, or up to around one or two years of relevant work experience

• You understand core security concepts such as identity and access, endpoint security and data protection

• You are motivated to develop hands-on skills in areas such as incident handling and security configuration

• You communicate clearly in English, both written and spoken

• It’s a plus if you already have some experience with Microsoft security tools (e.g. Entra ID, Defender, Intune or Purview), scripting such as PowerShell, or SIEM tools – but we will help you learn them

Why choose NNE?

NNE is short for Novo Nordisk Engineering. And for all of us who work here, NNE means so much more.

**The Impact You'll Make

**At Danfoss Sensing Solutions, we develop advanced sensing technologies supporting applications across the Danfoss portfolio. As demand for data centre infrastructure, energy-efficient cooling, and environmental monitoring continues to grow, we are expanding our capabilities to develop the next generation of sensing solutions.

As our Senior Mechanical Engineer, you will strengthen our mechanical engineering expertise within R&D and play an important role in developing future sensing platforms, with a particular focus on gas sensing and data centre applications.

You will help transform new ideas into robust, manufacturable products by driving mechanical architecture and packaging development from early concepts through industrialization. You will also provide technical expertise across mechanical design, packaging, and manufacturability while working closely with colleagues across multiple engineering disciplines.

This is an individual contributor role without people management responsibilities. Instead, your impact will come through technical leadership, influencing engineering decisions, sharing best practices, and strengthening our mechanical engineering capabilities.

**What You’ll Be Doing

**You will lead mechanical development activities across innovation and new product development projects, ensuring solutions are technically robust, scalable, and aligned with customer needs.

**

• Developing robust encapsulation, sealing, and environmental protection solutions for sensors operating under demanding industrial conditions

• Driving mechanical work packages in innovation and product development projects in close collaboration with sensing specialists, electronics, firmware, manufacturing engineers, product management, and external partners.

• Supporting prototyping, design reviews, risk assessments, testing activities, and supplier collaboration to enable successful industrialization.

**You have a strong foundation in mechanical engineering combined with hands-on product development experience. You are comfortable taking ownership of complex mechanical challenges while collaborating across engineering disciplines.

• A Bachelor's or Master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Mechatronics, or a related engineering discipline.

• Extensive experience developing industrial products from concept through production, including complex mechanical design challenges.

• Hands-on experience with mechanical design of sensors, electronic products, or other highly integrated mechanical systems.

• Strong experience with 3D CAD tools such as Inventor.

• Experience with injection-moulded components and Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) principles.

• Knowledge within areas such as sealing and joining technologies, thermal management, tolerance analysis, rapid prototyping, or high-volume manufacturing.
