Do you understand complex business processes, question assumptions and turn real needs into solutions developers can build? Join our product team in Aarhus and help shape the in-house systems supporting global commodity trading, risk management and financial operations!

We are looking for an experienced Senior Business Analyst, who can bridge business stakeholders and our development team. You will get close to the users, understand how the business creates value and manages risk, and translate complex needs into clear, prioritized backlog items. The goal is simple: to ensure that we build the right things, not only build things right.

This is an operational and influential role in a collaborative product team. You will be expected to ask “why”, create clarity, speak up and help the team make pragmatic decisions in a complex domain. You will not be coding, but you have enough technical understanding to discuss services, data and integrations credibly with developers.

Your role and responsibilities

In this role, you will work directly with end users and business stakeholders to understand their processes, pain points and goals. You will constructively question requirements to uncover the real need behind requests and challenge initiatives that do not create sufficient value. Based on these insights, you will map and document business processes, data flows and system-supported capabilities, translating business needs into clear epics, user stories and acceptance criteria that the development team can act on.

In addition, you will:

• Partner closely with the Product Owner and support prioritization based on business value, risk and dependencies.

• Participate actively in refinement and act as the go-to person for business questions during development.

• Maintain the big-picture view of how changes affect services, integrations and downstream processes across the trade lifecycle.

• Use AI tools to accelerate analysis and documentation, while critically reviewing and improving the output.

• Help the team and the business identify practical, responsible ways of applying AI in everyday workflows.

The environment you will join

You will become part of an agile product team, with a closely involved Product Owner and a culture where decisions are made together. There is no ivory tower. We expect colleagues to contribute their perspective, challenge ideas respectfully and take shared ownership of the outcome.

The team builds and develops in-house systems covering the trade lifecycle from capturing derivative trades through risk management to invoicing. The users work within Global Risk Management, and the solutions operate in a service-oriented landscape based on .NET and Azure, with a combination of on-premises infrastructure and Kubernetes.

The role is based at our Aarhus office, where close day-to-day collaboration matters. Depending on business needs, you should also expect occasional visits to Middelfart.

What we are looking for

We imagine that you have several years of experience as a Business Analyst, Business Architect, Product Owner, Functional Consultant or in a comparable role. More importantly, you have repeatedly demonstrated that you can understand complexity and turn it into concrete, value-creating deliverables.

You have demonstrated the ability to understand complex business processes and translate them into clear, actionable deliverables. You are also comfortable writing user stories and acceptance criteria and contributing effectively in agile or Scrum-based product teams.

We also imagine that you bring:

• Practical use of AI tools in daily work, for example to analyze information, draft requirements, summarize stakeholder input or map processes, combined with sound critical judgement.

• Clear communication skills and the ability to bring business and technical stakeholders into alignment

• Ability to align stakeholders constructively, including at senior level

• Sufficient technical understanding to discuss services, data and integrations without needing to be a developer.

• Professional proficiency in English. Danish is an advantage because much of the team’s daily collaboration takes place in Danish.

It will be a strong advantage if you also have:

• Knowledge of commodity or energy trading, derivatives, risk management or financial back-office processes such as trade capture, settlement, invoicing or hedging.

• Experience with ETRM or CTRM systems.

• A background in software development or a hybrid technical/business role before moving closer to the business side.

Who you are

• Curious and motivated to understand how the business makes money and manages risk.

• Pragmatic and able to balance an ideal solution with what creates value now.

• Comfortable expressing an opinion, asking difficult questions and making complex topics understandable.

• Collaborative, accountable and motivated by being part of a product team rather than a separate analysis function.

• Interested in new tools, including AI, and thoughtful about where they genuinely improve quality and speed.

What we offer

At Bunker Holding, you will work in an international business where technology supports global trading and risk management. You will join experienced colleagues in Aarhus, gain direct access to both users and developers, and work with complex systems where your analysis helps shape priorities and solutions

You can expect a collaborative and practical environment, professional development opportunities, pension and health insurance, and flexible working arrangements that support a sustainable work life. Normal support hours are centred around the working day, and any holiday on-call coverage is handled through a rotating arrangement.

Ready to apply?

If this sounds like the challenge you are looking for, we would be happy to hear from you. Please upload your CV and application. We review applications on an ongoing basis and schedule interviews when we identify suitable candidates.

We believe diverse perspectives improve our decisions and solutions. Therefore, we encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every single preference listed above. For any questions about the position, feel free to reach out to Team Lead, Jane Ingildsen at +45 2791 6688.

Bunker Holding

Bunker Holding is a global leader in purchasing, selling and supplying marine fuel and lube oil, while also providing risk management and other vital services to the shipping industry. The company operates through more than 1,600 ports worldwide and is present in 33 countries with 56 offices and more than 1,400 employees.

Bunker Holding is the largest company in USTC, a family-owned group with activities across energy, shipping, logistics, risk management, mobility, IT and sustainable solutions.

•

•

Do you enjoy keeping a team moving without getting in the way? Are you the kind of producer who loves making work life easier for your team through process? And are you also quite silly?

We're expanding one of our games and looking for a Senior Producer to help drive new content and features for our players. You'll work very closely with the executive producer and game director, supporting them in setting a clear production plan within time and budget constraints, while making sure the team has everything they need to do their best work.

You'll also be part of a cross-studio producer team where you can exchange ideas, challenge each other, and share knowledge and complementary skills.

**Here's What That Looks Like Day To Day

**

• Implement and refine production processes and tools, shaping how we work and grow as a studio

• Drive the project forward by removing roadblocks and keeping delivery dates realistic

• Facilitate the team’s day-to-day rhythm (stand-ups, planning, reviews, post-mortems)

• Plan updates, roadmaps, and marketing beats together with the leads, and communicate plans clearly to stakeholders

• Manage the project long-term: priorities, scope, timelines, risks, and follow-up

• Take on team and people responsibility, including 1:1s, development reviews, and salary conversations

Last, but not least: There's plenty of room to shape this role to fit you.

**Must-haves

**

• Experience going through at least one full game production cycle

• Experience as a producer on at least one shipped game

• Experience with live service and online games

• Experience working with external stakeholders

• A deep understanding of the game development process

• A strong belief in nurturing team wellbeing because a sustainable pace and motivation directly shape the quality of what ships

• Experience with people management (development talks, hiring, 1:1s) and team production (version control, stand-ups, sprints, reviews)

• You’re ready to tell us where we’re going wrong and help us improve

**What Always Matters To Us At Triband

**We've always believed that games are made by teams, not solo superstars, and good ideas can come from anyone. We love people who bring curiosity, generosity, flexibility, and strong opinions, especially when those opinions come with reasoning, openness, and a willingness to validate ideas properly.

We also care a lot about experimentation. Sometimes the weird idea is not the right fit. Sometimes the weird idea is the entire game! The trick is being able to explore it together, learn from it, and not get too precious when the experience tells us we're wrong.

**Practicalities

**

• We don't offer relocation support or visa sponsorship for this role.

• We work a 37-hour work week, with core hours 10-15, and the freedom to start and finish anywhere between 7 and 18.

• We work on-site at our cozy office in central Copenhagen.

• No crunch. People over deadlines.

• Our working language is English.

**We offer

**

• Silly but ambitious projects, and the chance to work on and impact great games that reach millions of players.

• A playful and ambitious work environment where experimentation is encouraged.

• Friendly and kind colleagues who love making each other laugh as much as making games.

• A professional development budget to invest in your growth.

• Social activities like Friday bars, hobby nights, board game nights, team events, you name it.

• Daily lunch at a local restaurant just a walk across the lakes away, with plant-based options (and soft ice on Thursdays).

• Six weeks of vacation (five standard plus one extra on us).

• Paid parental leave at full salary for the periods covered by state reimbursement.

• Child's first sick day on us, no questions asked.

• Pension plan and private health insurance.

• Endless amounts of coffee.

**WHAT THE TRIBAND?

**Triband is the award-winning studio behind the WHAT THE? comedy game series, which is played by millions worldwide. From our home in central Copenhagen, more than 60 wonderful humans are united by our mission to make everyone laugh. To do so, we focus on exploring comedy through gameplay. We like to break player expectations, use wonderful music, slick art, and create a quirky atmosphere. We experiment a lot, and it doesn't always work out, but we always learn something.

We put people first and strive to create a safe and creative working environment. We believe that teams, not individuals, make games, and we believe diversity makes for better teams. For these reasons, we look for people who bring new perspectives and will challenge us and our way of doing things.

For more info about Triband, check out: triband.net/about

jobs.occupation: Graduate Cloud Infrastructure Engineer – Medical Software
jobs.description:
MagVenture is an established medical device company specialized in the TMS technology (Transcranial Magnetic Stimulation), which is rapidly being adopted for treatment and investigation of a number of difficult mental and physical disorders such as depression and pain.

MagVenture is on a rapid international growth journey with many exciting new products to come and that is why we need a new colleague to strengthen our software and cloud operations.

Would you like to join this growth adventure? - then apply!

The job – working with Azure infrastructure and databases

You will become part of our growing software activities and play an important role in the deployment, operation, and maintenance of our cloud-based medical software solution.

Working closely with experienced software developers, engineers, Product Managers, and external technology partners, you will help manage our cloud infrastructure and databases, currently hosted on Microsoft Azure, and support the reliable operation of applications used by clinics worldwide.

The role offers an opportunity for a recently graduated engineer or IT professional with some practical experience in cloud platforms such as Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud to develop hands-on skills in cloud infrastructure, database management, automation, cybersecurity, and medical software.

You will gradually take on more responsibility as you become familiar with our systems, working alongside experienced colleagues and external specialists.

The role will be based out of our Headquarters in Farum, Denmark. Danish visa is required.

Tasks

You will support the deployment and ongoing operation of our cloud infrastructure and databases, primarily within Microsoft Azure. Your responsibilities will include:

• Setting up and configuring new customer environments, including domains, certificates, and regional deployments.

• Assisting with software releases, upgrades, and deployment activities.

• Monitoring cloud availability, database performance, capacity, and system health using cloud monitoring tools.

• Supporting incident investigation, troubleshooting, backup monitoring, and recovery activities.

• Helping maintain cloud and database security, access management, credentials, and environment configurations.

• Supporting Infrastructure as Code (IaC), automation, and integration with development pipelines.

• Monitoring cloud resource utilization and supporting cost optimization.

• Maintaining technical documentation and supporting cybersecurity, regulatory compliance, and audit requirements.

• Collaborating with internal development teams and external partners to continuously improve our cloud infrastructure.

Qualifications

We acknowledge a broad set of backgrounds, but typically look for:

• Recently completed or soon-to-be-completed degree in Software Engineering, Computer Science, IT Engineering, Cloud Computing, or a related technical discipline.

• Practical experience with cloud platforms and databases (Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, or similar) through student jobs, internships, university projects, or previous employment.

• Basic understanding of cloud infrastructure, networking, databases, and application deployment.

• Familiarity with Infrastructure as Code tools such as Terraform, Bicep, or CloudFormation is an advantage.

• Experience with scripting, automation, CI/CD pipelines, or monitoring tools is considered a plus.

• Interest in cybersecurity, cloud operations, and reliable software systems.

• Structured and analytical approach with strong attention to detail.

• Good organizational and project management skills, with the ability to work across international teams and stakeholders.

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English; Danish is an advantage.

Experience with regulated environments, healthcare software, or data protection requirements is considered a plus.

Who are you?

• You are an ambitious recent graduate or early-career professional looking to develop your career in cloud engineering within a high-tech medical device company.

• You already have some hands-on experience with cloud technologies and enjoy understanding how systems work, solving technical problems, and improving reliability and performance.

• You are comfortable taking responsibility for your tasks, eager to learn from experienced colleagues, and enjoy working with people from different technical backgrounds.

• As a person you have a positive attitude with a helpful and curious mindset, and you value honest and direct communication.

What can you expect from us?

MagVenture is an innovation focused company with a low-key, family owned culture. We practice work life balance and flexibility. We offer an exciting journey with plenty of challenges and room for development – both personally and professionally – working with great colleagues supporting each other. We are eager to welcome you to our modern headquarters in Farum with an excellent lunch prepared by a local chef every day.

How to apply?

We are hoping to find the right candidate, starting as soon as possible, preferably before the year-end. We will call for interviews on an ongoing basis, so you are encouraged to submit your application as soon as possible.

We look forward to receiving your motivated application and CV.

Do you want to know more about us?

MagVenture currently employs 240 employees, and we are a privately owned Danish company. MagVenture is the sister company of Tonica Elektronik that was founded in 1991, and has, since then, grown organically from a location in a small basement to becoming a global market-leading manufacturer of magnetic stimulators.

Our products are used for a wide range of psychiatric and cognitive research purposes as well as neuro-rehabilitation, neurology & diagnostic. Our mission is to pioneer safe, effective, and reliable magnetic stimulation therapies, offer innovative and versatile research solutions and work to expand access to magnetic stimulation worldwide.

Learn more at www.magventure.com

jobs.occupation: Technical expert in inks & coatings, plastics: Technical Product Specialist or Head of Product Development
jobs.description:
About Octarine

Octarine Bio is a Copenhagen-based biotech company making safe, sustainable, bio-based pigments. Our PurePalette™ platform uses precision fermentation and renewable raw materials to produce colourants that can replace petrochemical and mined pigments.

We are a team of around 15 people, working across pigment manufacturing, formulation and application development, and commercial development. As our pigment manufacturing processes reach full commercial scale, and our first pigment products are now in the hands of customers and partners, we are looking for someone with deep domain expertise in one or more of our core application areas (dyeing, printing, coatings and plastics) to make PurePalette™ work in real industrial applications and turn successful customer trials into lasting commercial products.

The role

You will be the technical owner of the PurePalette™ product range and the link between our lab and our customers. You will translate what the market needs into clear performance targets, work with our scientists to meet them, and make sure our pigment products perform once they reach a customer's processes.

We are looking for an applications expert in inks and coatings, plastics, or both, or in a closely related pigment application field. The title and scope will match your experience:

• Technical Product Specialist if you are earlier in your career and want a role with a lot of room to grow as the company scales.

• Head of Product Development if you have the experience to lead the product and applications function, shape the product roadmap and build a team.

In both cases you will report directly to our Chief Scientific Officer and work closely with our commercial team.

What you will do

Own the product, technically

• Be the technical expert for all PurePalette™ products and the first point of contact for technical questions from customers, partners and colleagues.

• Define the performance and quality parameters customers expect in each application, such as colour strength, dispersibility, heat stability, light and weather fastness, migration, rheology, and wash and rub fastness.

• Plan and coordinate the internal and external testing needed to prove each parameter, and turn the results into clear data packages for customers.

• Own, write and maintain our technical and product documentation, including Safety Data Sheets (SDS), Technical Data Sheets (TDS), Certificates of Analysis (CoA), product specifications and application guides.

Make our pigments work for customers

• Work with customers, distributors and partners to implement PurePalette™ products in their processes, from first lab trial to production run.

• Own the technical side of our partnerships with masterbatchers, ink manufacturers, dyehouses and research institutes. Set up project plans, manage technology transfer between parties, and troubleshoot problems until the product works in the target application.

• Handle technical customer feedback and complaints, find the root cause and feed lessons back into product and process development.

Decide what to develop next

• Identify where bio-based pigments offer real value to end users, and where they can genuinely meet customers' performance expectations.

• Work with Octarine scientists to map which applications our current pigments suit, and which applications we should target with future products.

• Work with our formulation and application scientists to refine formulations (dispersions, masterbatches, inks, dye and print pastes) to meet customer requirements.

• Work with our R&D and process teams to develop and implement strategies that improve pigment performance, for example through stabilisation, surface treatment or particle engineering.

• Benchmark our products against incumbent pigments and competing bio-based alternatives.

Connect technical and commercial

• Act as the bridge between Octarine's technical and commercial teams, translating customer needs into technical requirements and technical results into customer value.

• Join customer meetings, site visits and trade fairs as the technical voice of the company.

• Contribute technical content to sales materials, grant applications and investor discussions, and help capture new inventions for our IP portfolio.

What you bring

Pigment applications are many markets, not one. Printing inks alone span flexo, gravure, offset, screen and digital printing, and each places different demands on a pigment. The end markets differ just as much, from packaging and textiles to toys, consumer goods and coatings, each with its own performance, safety and regulatory requirements.

We need someone who knows this landscape in depth. You should understand the technical and performance requirements of each sub-application and market, judge where our pigments have a realistic and valuable fit, and work with our scientists to develop products that meet those requirements.

Specifically, we are looking for:

• An MSc or PhD in chemistry, polymer or materials science, chemical engineering, colour science or a related field, or equivalent industrial experience.

• Hands-on industrial experience applying pigments or colourants in textiles, inks and coatings, plastics and masterbatch, or a closely related field. For the Head of Product Development level, we expect around 5 or more years, including leading projects or people.

• A practical understanding of pigment dispersion and of how pigment properties such as particle size, surface chemistry and thermal stability affect performance in the final product.

• Experience with colour measurement (spectrophotometry, CIELAB, ΔE) and with standard ISO, EN or ASTM test methods for pigment and application performance.

• Experience writing or maintaining SDS, TDS and CoA documents, and working knowledge of REACH and CLP.

• Experience working directly with customers or external partners on trials, scale-up or technology transfer.

• The ability to explain technical results clearly to scientists, customers and commercial colleagues.

• A structured, self-driven way of working, and comfort with the pace and ambiguity of an early-stage company.

• Fluent written and spoken English.

• The confidence to take full ownership of the role from day one. You will set your own priorities, make decisions within your remit and drive projects to completion without close supervision, keeping the CSO informed rather than waiting for direction.

Nice to have

• Experience in both inks and coatings and plastics.

• Experience with textile dyeing or printing.

• Experience with organic pigments, natural colourants or other bio-based materials.

• Knowledge of food contact and product safety requirements, such as EU 10/2011, the Swiss Ordinance, EuPIA guidelines, EN 71-3 or ZDHC.

• Experience with quality systems such as ISO 9001, or with setting product specifications for a new product.

• An existing network in the European ink, coatings, masterbatch or textile industries.

What we offer

• A central role in bringing a new class of sustainable pigments to market, with real influence over which products we build and how.

• Direct work with the founding team and a short path from idea to decision.

• A small, highly skilled team of scientists across synthetic biology, fermentation, downstream processing, formulation and application.

• For earlier-career candidates, a role that can grow with the company. For senior candidates, the chance to build and lead the product function.

• Real autonomy and ownership of your work, and the chance to make a lasting impact at a fast-growing company developing new materials for industries that urgently need to change.

Practical details

Location: Copenhagen, Denmark. On-site is strongly preferred; hybrid working is possible for the right candidate.

Start date: As soon as possible

Reports to: Chief Scientific Officer

Employment: Full-time, permanent

Travel: Some travel to customers and partners within Europe

Right to work: Applicants must already have the right to live and work in Denmark. We are unfortunately not able to sponsor work visas at this time.

How to apply

Apply with your CV. Please highlight the pigment applications you have worked on and a technical problem you solved in a customer's process.

We review applications on a rolling basis and will fill the position as soon as we find the right person, so we encourage you to apply early.

We welcome applicants of all backgrounds and are happy to answer questions about the role before you apply.

Does it excite you to build the marketing engine for an upcoming obesity and metabolic health launch, and do you have experience with turning brand strategy into integrated, compliant go-to-market plans? If this sounds like you, and you are ready to take on a broad area of responsibilities, then you could be our new colleague.

**Your new position

**As Senior Director, Global Marketing Strategy, you will build and lead the marketing capabilities that bring Zealand Pharma’s medicines to healthcare professionals and patients. The role translates brand strategy into customer engagement, channel, and campaign plans, and creates the foundation for a scalable marketing organization. You will be the commercial voice in building the core brands towards a successful launch.

**We Offer Exciting Responsibilities

**

• Define brand strategy, including positioning, segmentation and brand building to a strong value proposition

• Develop the go-to-market and marketing strategy, translating brand strategy into integrated, multichannel plans

• Build the marketing function, including team structure, processes, and agency and vendor partnerships

• undefined

• Experience with omnichannel and digital engagement strategies for healthcare professionals and patients

**Your new team

**You will be a member of the global commercial organization reporting into the Senior Vice President. You will be part of building the area and will work closely with our external partners and with key stakeholders, e.g. Medical Affairs, R&D, Market Access, Alliance Management.

**Let’s bond and be bold

Making bonds is at the core of everything we do. From discovering and developing the best new peptide drugs for patients, to engaging with our partners or connecting with each other. We bond through curiosity and playfulness as a team, allowing ourselves to challenge common thinking and drive future innovation. Join us and let’s bond and be bold.

For further information, please contact Senior Vice President Mette Zacho, MZacho@zealandpharma.com .

We are committed to an inclusive recruitment process and welcome applications from all job applicants.

**About Zealand Pharma A/S

**Zealand Pharma A/S (Nasdaq: ZEAL) is a biotechnology company focused on advancing medicines for obesity and metabolic health. Combining more than 25 years of peptide R&D expertise with a proprietary data platform that leverages advanced data-driven and AI/ML approaches, Zealand Pharma aims to lead a new era in obesity and metabolic health. To date, more than ten Zealand Pharma-invented drug candidates have entered clinical development, of which two products have reached the market and three candidates are in late-stage development. The Company has collaborations with global pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners for research, development, and commercialization. Founded in 1998, Zealand Pharma is headquartered in Copenhagen, Denmark, with a U.S. presence in Boston, Massachusetts. Learn more at www.zealandpharma.com.

Sophion Bioscience is looking for an ambitious, customer-focused Vice President of Research & Development to lead and further develop our R&D organization.

This is a central leadership role with responsibility for Sophion’s technology strategy, product development execution, engineering capabilities, and R&D organization. You will ensure that priorities, resources, budgets, and development activities are managed with clarity and discipline, enabling us to deliver high-quality products that create measurable value for customers.

You will report to the CEO and as a member of the Senior Leadership Team, you will contribute to Sophion’s overall direction and continued growth.

About the role

As VP R&D, you will lead and develop Sophion’s multidisciplinary R&D organization, setting a clear direction and creating the structure, leadership, and ways of working needed to deliver on our ambitions.

You will translate product and portfolio priorities into clear R&D priorities, roadmaps, and resource commitments, ensuring alignment and accountability across the organization. Working closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management, you will ensure R&D brings strong judgment and execution discipline to the development of differentiated and commercially successful products.

A key part of your mandate will be to strengthen the R&D organization and its leadership. You will develop leaders, build effective teams, establish clear governance and decision-making, and create a culture of collaboration, ownership, and delivery.

You will attract, develop, and retain talented people and ensure that R&D continues to grow in capability, maturity, and performance.

About Us

Since 2000 Sophion Bioscience has pioneered Automated Patch Clamping for ion channel research. Today, we specialize in automated solutions for pre-clinical life sciences.

We work closely with academic institutions, contract research organizations, and leading biotech and pharmaceutical companies to create effective assays for screening and characterization. Our solutions empower the study of drug targets and candidates at the bench, reducing development time in discovery and reducing risk in clinical trials.

Through the continued development of our Automated Patch Clamp portfolio (QPatch & Qube) and our new Organ on a Chip platform (Ethica), we offer uncompromised data quality in a user-friendly environment, from assay setup to advanced data analysis.

We are driven by curiosity, teamwork, and a genuine passion for helping scientists succeed. We work in an open and collaborative environment where people share knowledge freely, support each other across roles and borders, and take pride in doing things properly. Our culture is informal, trusting, and grounded in respect — for colleagues, customers, and the science we enable. Even as we grow globally, we remain a company where people feel welcome, included, and able to make a meaningful impact.

We are headquartered in Denmark and have subsidiaries in the United States, Japan, and China.

What You'll Do

• Set and execute Sophion’s R&D and technology strategy in alignment with the company’s overall direction and priorities.

• Lead and develop the R&D organization, including its structure, leadership capabilities, ways of working, and competencies.

• Clearly communicate R&D priorities, progress, risks, and trade-offs across Sophion and to the Leadership Team and Board.

• Own the R&D budget and ensure resources are allocated to the activities that create the greatest strategic and customer value.

• Drive portfolio and resource management, translating product priorities into actionable development roadmaps and execution commitments while balancing short- and long-term priorities.

• Ensure customer needs inform development decisions by driving broad R&D engagement with the market, key opinion leaders, and key accounts.

• Strengthen development governance, decision-making, accountability, milestones, KPIs, and transparent reporting.

• Drive continuous improvement in product quality, performance, reliability, and maintainability.

• Work closely with Innovation, Market & Product Management to assess opportunities and convert agreed priorities into robust and commercially viable products.

• Maintain appropriate quality and compliance standards across R&D activities.

• Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders

Who You Are

You are a strategic and hands-on R&D leader who can turn complex scientific and technical opportunities into high-quality products.

You bring clarity to complex situations and combine strong judgment with disciplined execution. You build strong teams, set clear priorities, use resources effectively, and deliver commitments.

You are engaging and decisive, and you build trust through transparency, communication, sound judgment, and consistent follow-through. You are comfortable moving between strategic questions and operational details without losing sight of R&D and company priorities.

We expect that you:

• Master’s degree in science, engineering, technology, or a related field.

• Proven R&D leadership experience in complex, multidisciplinary product development, leading leaders and sizeable teams of specialized engineers and scientists across hardware, software, firmware & bioscience.

• Strong communicator with the ability to set the agenda, shape strategy, and communicate in a clear direction across the organization and with customers and investors.

• Track record of taking products from concept to successful global market use.

• Experience from life science tools, diagnostics, MedTech, laboratory instrumentation, or similar quality-critical environments is preferred.

• Demonstrated ability to improve execution, prioritization, organizational capability, and product quality.

• Strong strategic, customer, communication, and decision-making skills, with the ability to work effectively across functions and deliver results.

• Strong interpersonal, negotiation, and problem-solving skills, with professional English proficiency.

How to Apply

Please apply via LinkedIn.

If you have questions about the role, you are welcome to contact Helene Fife on hef@Sophion.com

Start Date

As soon as possible.

We review applications on an ongoing basis and close the recruitment process once we have found the right candidate. If this opportunity excites you, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible.

_Please do not contact us or apply if you are a recruiter, consultant or outsourcing company.

**Deliver with focus. Scale with intent 🚀

**Are you a delivery leader who knows how to guide enterprise customers through complex set-ups without over-engineering the journey? Do you care deeply about building scalable, repeatable SaaS delivery rather than one-off custom projects?

At Performativ, we’re building the infrastructure layer for modern wealth management. As our Engagement Manager, you’ll lead the enterprise rollout of our SaaS platform helping customers onboard successfully through structured delivery, clear communication, and lightweight technical engagement.

This is not a professional services consulting role. You won’t be buried in endless customer-specific code or heavy customizations. Instead, you’ll work cross-functionally to help customers adopt our product the right way: cleanly, securely, and in line with platform best practices so they can scale on top of us, not around us.

**What You Will Do

**

• Own enterprise set-up programs end to end (kick-off through go-live and hyper-care) against an agreed plan and scope (Statement of Work).

• Enable customers to integrate Performativ via standard platform patterns (APIs, SSO, configuration) without custom buildouts, working with product and engineering to flag gaps early and advocate for scalable paths.

• Own plan, scope, and change control, keeping scope tied to contract and change visible and decided rather than quietly absorbed, and support the Technical Program Lead on requirements, design documents, and acceptance-criteria sign-off.

• Run customer communication, cadence, and governance with reporting that keeps meetings short, and manage risk, dependency, and issue tracking (including customer-side).

• Lead a clean handover to Customer Success at go-live or hyper-care exit, including train-the-trainer sessions and supporting materials.

• Represent the program in internal capacity and exception reviews, bringing requests the plan cannot absorb back as options rather than committing on the spot.

• Build repeatable playbooks, documentation, and artefacts that make the next program faster. You will be measured on this, not only on your own delivery.

**How You Will Work

**You will run multiple programs at once, in a delivery pod alongside the Technical Program Lead, Integration Engineers, Data Migration Specialists, and Product Engineers. None report to you. Rather you get things done through clarity and relationships, not authority. You will report to the COO. This is an in-office role based at our Copenhagen office.

**What We're Looking For

**

• 7+ years in program or engagement management, consulting, product management, or another delivery-facing role, with a track record of leading complex, multi-stakeholder implementations end to end.

• Comfort being firm with customers on scope and timeline while keeping the relationship stronger for it.

• Any industry background welcome. Experience with enterprise customers (banks, asset managers, regulated industries), balancing urgency against long-term maintainability highly advantageous.

• Structured and highly organized, producing written plans, governance cadences, and reporting that stakeholders can act on.

• Broad technical literacy across enterprise SaaS delivery: API-based integrations, SSO and security configuration, and data migration and mapping, including enough SQL to read and question a mapping. You do not build the integration, but you understand it well enough to scope it, question it, and know when something does not add up.

• Ability to build working fluency in the customer's business domain fast: within 90 days, able to discuss topics such as advice and suitability workflows and customer reporting without a subject-matter expert in the room.

• ITIL Foundation, PMP or PRINCE2 Certification would be beneficial.

**Technical Fluency

**

• You’re not, necessarily, a developer, but you’re comfortable with APIs, data structures, auth flows (OAuth/SAML), and deployment models.

• You can dive into logs, payloads, and basic SQL or Python when needed to unblock yourself or a customer - but you prioritize scalable fixes over tactical workarounds.

• You advocate for platform-aligned solutions, not special cases.

**What This Role Is Not

**This role sits in operations, not engineering or commercial, and is project-based: once delivery is complete, you roll on to the next engagement. As a SaaS provider, we do not build bespoke software; delivery works within the bounds of the product.

**We Can Offer

**

• Trust and responsibility to shape how Performativ delivers for its largest customers.

• A competitive salary and benefits package.

• A fast-growing, VC-backed fintech scaleup, working alongside professionals from leading institutions (Goldman Sachs, McKinsey, BCG, Amazon and others).

• Career acceleration through professional development and leadership opportunities.

jobs.occupation: Team Lead IT Operations – parental cover
jobs.description:
Do you want to shape how a global organisation sources, supports and governs its IT, and make sure colleagues can rely on it wherever they sit?

Corporate IT serves the Novo Nordisk Foundation (NNF), Novo Holdings and affiliated organisations. As Team Lead for IT Operations, you will be accountable for stable, secure IT services across Denmark, Europe, the US and Asia, delivered by a core team of four employees and a strong set of external partners. 2027 is a defining year: you will be developing a sourcing strategy and participate in negotiations with potential vendors, build the support model for the new NNF headquarters, and set the scope and roadmap for our shared ITSM platform.

This is a one-year parental cover. You report to the Head of Corporate IT, join the Corporate IT leadership team, and work closely with business stakeholders. The position is based in Hellerup, Denmark, with some travel. NNF is an office-based organisation; however, flexible working, including working from home, can occasionally be agreed with your manager.

In 2027, you will be responsible for:

• 
Developing our future sourcing strategy. Lead the development of our future sourcing strategy and participate in the negotiations with potential vendors, together with the Head of Corporate IT and business stakeholders.

• 
Establishing the support model for the new NNF headquarters. Define and put in place the IT support model in preparation for the inauguration of the new headquarters in 2028.

• 
Determining the scope and aspirations for the shared ITSM platform, ServiceNow. Assess the scope and potential of the shared platform and implement roadmap accordingly.

• 
Owning service quality across our locations. Be accountable for stable, secure IT support in Denmark and internationally, and follow up on agreed service levels through our partners and local contacts.

• 
Managing vendors and costs. Own day-to-day vendor relationships and contracts, and contribute to budget follow-up, invoice control and allocation of global IT costs.

• 
Leading and developing the Operations team. Set priorities, create clear ownership and build a culture of accountability, knowledge sharing and continuous improvement.

• 
Being the escalation point. Coordinate timely resolution of major operational issues with internal and external partners, including IT Architecture and Cyber Security. This requires flexibility if a major incident occurs.

What you bring

You have solid experience from IT operations or service delivery, with responsibility for managing suppliers, services and people. You set direction, create structure and follow through, and you communicate clearly with vendors, business stakeholders, leaders and your team. A relevant education is preferred, although substantial relevant experience may also be considered.

• 
Experience from an international organisation with an outsourced IT environment.

• 
Documented experience negotiating and managing complex IT-vendor or sourcing agreements, ideally including a renegotiation or re-sourcing.

• 
Experience setting up or changing IT-support or service models, for example for new offices or sites.

• 
Practical understanding of IT service management and ITSM platforms, including scope and roadmap decisions. Experience with ServiceNow, our ITSM platform, is an advantage.

• 
Ability to work with business stakeholders and leadership on strategy and priorities.

• 
Fluent in Danish and English, spoken and written.

We believe that you will thrive in this role if you have a strong personal drive and a curious mind. You are known for taking ownership and going the extra mile to ensure the right solutions are implemented and followed through. You bring positive energy and are not afraid to roll up your sleeves to get the job done.

Application and Information

We encourage you to send your application as soon as possible and no later than 19 November 2026. We will screen applicants on a regular basis.

To apply, please send your CV and cover letter by clicking the “Apply now” button.

Factbird helps manufacturers improve performance with an AI-enabled, plug-and-play manufacturing intelligence suite. Real-time visibility on the shop floor. Connected operations. Data that actually turns into improvement, not just reports.

We’re expanding our Northern European sales team in Copenhagen and looking for a Business Development Representative to help us keep building momentum and opening doors in a market where we already have a solid presence. You’ll work from our Copenhagen office and support our Danish and Swedish markets, so we’re looking for someone fluent in both languages.

This is a great role for someone early in their sales career who wants more than a script to follow: someone who wants to help shape our outbound approach, sharpen their craft with modern prospecting tools, and sell something that makes a real difference on the factory floor.

About the Role

As a BDR at Factbird, you won’t just be executing outreach. You’ll be helping sharpen the playbook for how we generate pipeline in Denmark and Sweden. That means a mix of hands-on prospecting and real input into strategy: which accounts to target, which messages resonate, and which channels and tools actually move the needle.

You’ll spend your time identifying the right accounts, reaching the right people, testing what works, and turning interest into qualified meetings and sales opportunities.

This is a phone-first role. Phone calls remain your primary tool, but you’ll also run structured multi-channel campaigns across email and LinkedIn, and use AI-powered prospecting tools to work smarter, not just harder.

Key Responsibilities

We’re looking for someone who understands that outbound success comes from a combination of activity, discipline, messaging, and follow-through. This role is aligned with market expectations for outbound development work, including periods where 100-200 call attempts per day may be required, depending on territory focus, campaign goals, and lead quality.

What you'll do

• 
Build qualified pipeline through targeted outbound prospecting into manufacturing and industrial accounts across Denmark and Sweden

• 
Respond to inbound leads, qualify interest, and convert it into meetings

• 
Research target accounts to understand business context, likely pain points, and buying relevance

• 
Identify the right decision-makers and stakeholders within target organizations

• 
Book discovery meetings for the Account Management team and create qualified opportunities

• 
Maintain strong prospect data quality and keep HubSpot accurate and up to date

• 
Track your performance against KPIs and stay disciplined about activity and follow-up

• 
Work closely with the Account Management and Marketing teams to sharpen targeting, messaging, and handoff quality

• 
Bring insights from prospect conversations back to the team: what’s resonating, what isn’t

How we'll measure success

KPIs will be defined with your manager, but here's what we're tracking:

• 
Sales-qualified leads generated

• 
Discovery meetings booked and completed

• 
Conversion from leads to qualified opportunities

• 
Outreach volume, especially calls

• 
Inbound lead response time

• 
CRM discipline and data quality

This role is for someone who wants to see a direct line between their daily work, the strategies they help build, and commercial growth.

About you

You want to build a career in sales, and you’re ready for a role where you get real ownership, not just a list of calls to make. You’re comfortable in an outbound environment, curious about tools and experimentation, and motivated by the opportunity to improve fast. We’re looking for someone with:

• 
1-3 years of experience as an SDR in a B2B SaaS environment

• 
Fluency in Danish and Swedish, and strong English

• 
A strong interest in pipeline generation and outbound prospecting

• 
Comfort working in a phone-first sales development role

• 
The ability to succeed in a high-activity environment, including periods of 100-200 calls per day

• 
Curiosity about the manufacturing world and interest in learning how manufacturers operate

• 
Strong follow-through and personal ownership

• 
Experience working in a CRM, ideally HubSpot

• 
Hunger for a long-term career in sales

If you’re excited by building pipelines, learning fast, and helping bring modern software into manufacturing environments, we’d love to hear from you.

Why Factbird?

People are at the heart of everything we build. We believe great products come from empowered teams — and we work hard to create an environment where you can do your best work and have space for life beyond it.

• 
Flexible working hours — we trust you to manage your time

• 
Competitive salary — compensation that reflects your skills, experience, and impact

• 
Internet reimbursement — stay connected wherever you choose to work from

• 
Thoughtful, human onboarding — step-by-step support from day one

• 
Individual Development Plan conversations — bi-yearly career development aligned to your ambitions

• 
Company-wide kickoffs & team days — we come together regularly across teams and regions

• 
A global, inclusive culture — diverse backgrounds and perspectives, actively celebrated

Join Us

If this role feels like a match, we’d be excited to hear from you and explore how you could help shape the future of data collection and production monitoring at Factbird.

And if someone in your network comes to mind who might be a great fit, feel free to share this opportunity with them.

Please note that applications will be reviewed after November 20th.

At Factbird, we believe that great work starts with people feeling respected, valued, and included. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer and are committed to building a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to thrive.

All employment decisions at Factbird are made based on business needs, role requirements, and individual qualifications, without discrimination based on gender, gender identity or expression, age, disability, marital or family status, nationality, ethnic or social origin, religion or belief, sexual orientation, or any other characteristic protected under applicable European and local employment laws.

We celebrate diversity in all its forms and believe that different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences make our teams stronger and our work better. We warmly encourage all qualified candidates to apply and to bring their whole selves to Factbird.

For more information or questions please contact us at khma@factbird.com

**Business Consultant - AECO Technical Advisory

****Position Overview

**Autodesk Consulting is looking for a Business Consultant to join our Northern Europe team. This remote role supports strategic customers across the region.

This is a senior individual contributor role combining business consulting, AECO industry expertise and executive advisory. You’ll work with some of Autodesk’s largest customers to shape transformation strategies, define target operating models, and develop business cases and roadmaps that deliver measurable business outcomes.

You’ll advise senior leaders, structure complex business challenges and lead strategic advisory engagements from discovery through executive decision-making. While you won’t configure or implement solutions, you’ll understand how Autodesk and complementary technologies fit within customers’ broader business and technology ecosystems, partnering with technical specialists to turn strategy into actionable delivery plans.

**Main Responsibilities

**

• Build trusted relationships with customer executives, business leaders and transformation teams, acting as a strategic advisor throughout the engagement

• Understand customer objectives, challenges and operating context to define outcome-driven transformation strategies

• Assess operating models, business processes, organizational capabilities, data and digital workflows to identify opportunities for improvement

• Define target-state operating models, transformation roadmaps, business cases, success measures and benefits realization plans

• Lead executive workshops, facilitate decision-making and align stakeholders across complex organizations

• Advise customers on how Autodesk and complementary AECO technologies support business outcomes through effective workflows, data management and interoperability

• Identify and prioritize opportunities for data, automation and AI based on business value, organizational readiness, governance and adoption

• Partner with Solution Architects, technical consultants and customer-facing teams to shape advisory engagements, validate strategic recommendations and develop credible delivery roadmaps

**Minimum Qualifications

**

• Substantial experience in AECO, management consulting or business transformation, with a proven track record of independently leading complex strategy and transformation engagements

• Deep expertise in at least one of the following: construction, infrastructure, engineering consultancy, utilities, or a closely related project-based, asset-intensive industry

• Strong working knowledge of Autodesk technologies or comparable AECO tool ecosystems, with the ability to discuss capabilities, workflow fit, data, interoperability and business value. Hands-on implementation expertise is not required

• Strong understanding of operating models, organizational change, governance, business cases and benefits realization

• Practical understanding of data-centric workflows, enterprise systems, automation, responsible AI and technology adoption

• Ability to lead through influence across cross-functional and international teams, with excellent communication and executive presentation skills

• Fluent English is required. Dutch and other European languages are highly valued

• Willingness to travel to customer meetings and Autodesk events across Northern Europe (up to 50%)

• Proven experience advising executives, structuring complex problems, facilitating high-stakes workshops and driving decisions

****Learn More

******About Autodesk

**Welcome to Autodesk! Amazing things are created every day with our software – from the greenest buildings and cleanest cars to the smartest factories and biggest hit movies. We help innovators turn their ideas into reality, transforming not only how things are made, but what can be made.

We take great pride in our culture here at Autodesk – it’s at the core of everything we do. Our culture guides the way we work and treat each other, informs how we connect with customers and partners, and defines how we show up in the world.

When you’re an Autodesker, you can do meaningful work that helps build a better world designed and made for all. Ready to shape the world and your future? Join us!

**Salary transparency

Offers are based on the candidate’s experience and geographic location, and may exceed this range. In addition to base salaries, our compensation package may include annual cash bonuses, commissions for sales roles, stock grants, and a comprehensive benefits package.

**Sales Careers

**Working in sales at Autodesk allows you to build meaningful relationships with customers while growing your career. Join us and help make a better, more sustainable world. Learn more here: https://www.autodesk.com/careers/sales

**Belonging

**We take pride in cultivating a culture of belonging where everyone can thrive. Learn more here: **https://www.autodesk.com/company/global-belonging

Do you want to be a valued part of the critical infrastructure that serves communities across Europe and beyond? Are you looking for an opportunity where you can make an impact, shape decisions, and accelerate your career?

If so, we are looking for dedicated, curious, and highly motivated graduates to join the DFDS Graduate Programme starting in September 2027.

**Be part of the movement - and play your part

**About The Role The DFDS Graduate Programme is a two-year fast-track programme for recent graduates with an interest in and passion for the maritime industry.

During the programme, you will complete three rotations across different areas of our Ferry Division. You will begin at our headquarters in Copenhagen, followed by a mandatory international rotation at one of our European hubs. Your final rotation at our headquarters will be tailored to your skills, interests, and our business needs.

Throughout the programme, you will gain broad exposure to both the operational and commercial sides of our Ferry Division while building valuable industry knowledge and professional experience.

Ferry Operations offers broad end-to-end exposure with sustainability, standardisation, and digitalisation at the heart of everything we do.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Help design and develop the vessels of tomorrow, supporting our green transition through electrification, ammonia, and green methanol initiatives.

• Support the operation and maintenance of our fleet of more than 70 RoRo, RoPax, and passenger vessels, covering everything from dry dock planning to crisis management and contingency handling.

• Contribute to our standardisation and digitalisation journey across eight owned terminals and more than 20 third-party terminals, where safety remains our highest priority.

• Support fleet planning, equipment optimisation, and our intercontinental rail setup, connecting ferry and logistics operations across our network.

In the commercial part of our Ferry Division, you will work alongside colleagues across Europe, supporting both B2B and B2C markets.

**Examples Of Interesting Tasks Could Be To:

**

• Support local and global sales teams and assist with key account management, ensuring our network is successfully marketed and sold across regions.

• Drive continuous improvement in customer service and booking processes through standardisation and digitalisation initiatives.

• Collaborate with IT teams to enhance and optimise our digital customer offerings.

• Work with operational teams to optimise routes and vessel capacity to meet customer demand.

• Support revenue management activities, including pricing optimisation and commercial performance analysis.

Across all rotations, you will work closely with highly skilled colleagues and engage with customers, suppliers, and partners throughout the maritime value chain. To support your development, each rotation will include both a dedicated manager and a mentor who will help you successfully navigate your learning journey.

Alongside hands-on experience at DFDS, you will participate in the Danish Shipping Education Programme, delivered by Danish Shipping. This programme consists of webinars, four seminars in Denmark, and one international seminar, covering key topics across the maritime industry.

****About You

****At DFDS, we believe the strongest teams are built on diversity, inclusion, and different perspectives. We are looking for candidates who:

• Have graduated from a relevant master’s degree by the start of the Graduate Programme in September 2027, preferably within maritime studies, supply chain, freight forwarding, logistics, sustainability, business, finance, engineering, or a related field.

• Have gained relevant experience through a student job, internship, exchange programme, or other extracurricular activities.

• Have no more than two years of full-time professional experience after completing your master's degree.

• Demonstrate strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

• Are collaborative team players who enjoy working with others and creating impact.

• Are curious, proactive, and eager to learn and develop professionally.

• Have an international mindset and are excited about working across cultures and locations.

Working at DFDS **Join the movement and grow with us

**As part of the DFDS Graduate Programme, you will become part of a strong graduate network across the company and build valuable connections across our international business. We offer a steep learning curve, meaningful responsibility from day one, and three interesting rotations designed to accelerate your professional development.

Are we a match? Apply now.  If your skills, experience, aspirations, and personality match this opportunity, we would love to hear from you.

Please Apply By Uploading Your CV no Later Than 30 November 2026. When Applying, You’re Also Asked To Answer The Following Questions:

• Why are you interested in joining the DFDS Graduate Programme?

• How will the programme help kickstart your career?

• How do you expect to contribute to the programme and DFDS?

• What do you believe will be your biggest challenge(s) during the programme?

**We look forward to hearing from you.

**Visit our Graduate site here to learn more and meet some of our people.

Join our Sitaware Extensions Program and help deliver customised integrations and extensions to Systematic's defence product suite, from sensor interfaces to radio drivers. As Senior Software Developer, you will combine software design, implementation and testing in a close-knit team working in an exciting domain.

The job

You will contribute to the delivery of high-quality integrations and extensions, from requirements analysis through software design, implementation and testing. Beyond hands-on development, you will help apply and improve our development process, and share your knowledge to support the team's growth.

In short, you can look forward to:

• Designing, implementing, documenting and debugging features, working primarily on back-end development (Java) and occasionally on front-end development (Angular)

• Analysing requirements, breaking them into technical tasks, and clarifying acceptance criteria

• Implementing and troubleshooting interfaces to hardware and external systems, such as sensors and radio interfaces

• Developing and maintaining unit and integration tests, and designing for testability

• Identifying issues and recommending improvements to code, tooling, pipelines and processes

Joining the team

You will be part of the Product Extension Team of around seven developers, test engineers and architects, part of the Sitaware Extensions Program within Defence Services. The team delivers customised integrations and extensions to Systematic's defence product suite, focusing on software- and hardware-related integrations such as sensor interfaces, radio drivers and interoperability with external systems, and continuously improves its own testing and development practices, methods and tools. This is a newly created position, so you will have real scope to shape how the role develops as the team continues to grow.

Your qualifications

To succeed in this role, you bring several years of software development experience gained in a structured, team-based environment, along with:

• Bachelor's or Master's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Software Technology or similar

• Hands-on experience with Java (or a related object-oriented technology) for backend development, and Angular (or a similar modern framework) for frontend development

• Fluent English; Danish is a nice-to-have

Alongside this, we value:

• Strong analytical abilities, with a focused and open mindset

• The ability to communicate intent and purpose clearly, both in writing and conversation

• Enjoys collaborating closely within a cross-functional team

Onboarding includes two three-day stays in Aarhus, and you should expect occasional travel of around two to ten days a year, mostly within Europe. Some onsite hardware testing may also be required, depending on integration needs.

Please note that you must be able to present a clean criminal record and have lived in a NATO and/or an EU country for the past seven years as we work with security-classified projects. Read more here.

Welcome to Systematic Copenhagen

When you join us in Copenhagen, you're not just getting a desk at one of the city's best locations—you are stepping into a workplace where community matters. Our Employees Club keeps things lively with monthly social events, and our office catering makes sure you are always well taken care of. Whether you are into casual games or just good company, you will find both at our foosball table or during our relaxed Friday bar gatherings.

Never stop developing

Systematic is uniquely people-centric, truly international and proudly rooted in Denmark with more than 1100 employees. Together, we write intelligent and innovative code to drive progress and improve lives. We develop IT solutions that make a real difference where it matters most. This is why we never stop developing. Here, there is room to be professional and personal. It is not just a place to work but a place to belong.

Start your development here

We will be assessing applications on an ongoing basis as we wish to welcome our new colleague as soon as possible, so click Apply Now and send us your CV today. If you have any questions, you are always welcome to contact us on tel. +45 8943 2000 and ask for Andreas Markussen, Senior Manager.

**💰 🇩🇰 up to 46,000 DKK gross/month (depending on seniority level)

**Intro

Monta powers the EV charging ecosystem. With 300,000+ monthly users and millions of charge sessions every month, our platform accelerates the electrification of mobility.

This is a fast-moving place. The problems are hard, the pace is quick, and the bar is high. If you like real ownership, figuring things out, and seeing the direct impact of your work, you’ll do well with us.

AI is built into how we work. It helps us ship faster, make better decisions, and stay lean. Everyone at Monta is expected to use AI tools thoughtfully - and to find smart ways to use them to move the work forward.

Our principles keep us grounded: Build Together & Finish, Sweat the Details, Customer First, and Aim for the Moon.

The best part of Monta is the people - sharp, ambitious, and good to be around. You’ll be challenged, supported, and trusted to deliver.

We’re looking for a Jun/Mid Level Engineer who’s ready to roll up their sleeves, take ownership, and build with us - through the grind and the wins.

This Is What You Will Achieve

• Owned an OCPP hardening project - chased down a recurring class of vendor quirks (malformed messages, connection drops, the long tail of hardware oddities), shipped the fix, and measurably cut failed sessions or disconnections for that device family.

• Helped shift the team from reacting to incidents to preventing them, through alerting and observability work that catches problems earlier.

• Made real progress on OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPI standards work that other services and front-ends across Monta now rely on.

What You Will Do

• Build and maintain backend services in NetOps' OCPP and charge point domain - protocol handling, message processing, device state, integrations with hardware vendors.

• Debug things that only break in the field. A charge point in Belgium disconnects every 40 minutes - you'll read the OCPP traffic, reproduce it against our emulator, find the cause, and fix it.

• Improve observability and alerting. Add the metrics, dashboards, and alerts that mean the next person doesn't have to guess.

• Take part in on-call once you're ramped up, with a team that treats a rough night as a reason to fix the system, not a rite of passage.

• Automate manual work away - a meaningful part of NetOps' job is removing the human steps that don't scale as our network grows.

• Collaborate across Product, Support, and the operations teams who live with the consequences of what we ship. You won't work in a silo.

**A Brief Overview Of Our Tech Stack

**

• Kotlin services (JVM), with Java where it already lives

• PHP/Laravel monolith - parts of our charge point domain still run here

• OCPP 1.6 / 2.0.1 and OCPI protocol handling

• Event-driven work with Kafka where message volume calls for it

• Observability via Prometheus, Grafana, and OpenSearch/Kibana

• AWS + Kubernetes, with Terraform for infrastructure

What We’re Looking For

• 1–4 years of backend engineering experience, or a strong junior track record with real production exposure. You write clean, readable code and finish what you start.

• Comfortable in a JVM language - Kotlin preferred, Java fine, and we'll help you get there from another stack if the fundamentals are strong. Willingness to touch PHP in our legacy monolith when the work calls for it.

• You enjoy debugging, genuinely - logs, traces, packet-level detail, weird one-off reports from a single customer.

• A sense of ownership - you follow your work into production, watch it, and flag problems early rather than waiting to be asked.

• Nice to have: curiosity about the physical world (our systems talk to metal boxes with electricity in them); clear communication - you can explain what broke and why to someone who isn't an engineer; advanced, deliberate use of AI tools in your daily engineering workflow.

• Bonus points for: exposure to OCPP, OCPI, EV charging, or the EV industry as a driver or enthusiast; IoT, embedded, or telemetry systems where devices in the field misbehave; event-driven architectures (Kafka) or high-volume message processing; reliability/monitoring/on-call experience (Prometheus, Grafana, SLOs); Kubernetes, Terraform, or infrastructure-as-code exposure.

**If the mission excites you but your experience isn’t a perfect 1:1 match, apply anyway - we care about potential, not perfection.

**AI Competency

• You’ll be expected to work with AI-powered tools. Some we use:

• GitHub Copilot / Claude Code

• ChatGPT / Gemini / Claude

• Notion AI (docs, knowledge, meeting notes)

• Analytics & ML: Langfuse, PyTorch, Mastra

• AI-enhanced testing & monitoring (e.g., generative QA, Grafana ML)

• We don’t expect mastery of all - but we expect comfort learning, experimenting, and adopting AI responsibly.

Why Monta

• Impact, not easy mode - your work matters, and you’ll feel it every day.

• Ownership from day one - we don’t micromanage, we expect you to deliver.

• The grind is real - priorities shift, and flexibility is sometimes needed to get things across the finish line. But so are the rewards: impact, growth, and a team that has your back.

• The people are extraordinary - talented, driven, and fun to work with. You’ll be challenged, supported, and inspired in equal measure.

What We Offer

• A yearly education budget and extra days off to use it.

• A friendly and social company culture with movie nights, Friday bars, pub crawls, and more.

• Free lunch every day.

• Pension & health coverage to keep you secure for today and tomorrow.

• Paid parental leave to support life's big moments.

• Warrants program - be part of our growth story.

• Flexible working hours; as long as you're at key meetings and delivering great work, we trust you to manage your schedule.

Please send us your application in English.

To succeed in this position, your spoken and written English skills need to be proficient. Since Monta is a globally active company, you'll be communicating often and regularly with our co-workers and partners around the world, making your professional English knowledge essential.

Please note that we don't accept unsolicited applications from headhunters or recruitment agencies. Unsolicited applications sent to our company or co-workers are considered to be the property of Monta, and we won't agree to pay any referral compensation or recruiter fee without a signed agreement.

Find out more by visiting https://monta.com/uk/careers/

Do you want to join a global leader in renewable energy infrastructure? If so, CIP Fund Solutions (CIP FS) is looking for an Analyst to join our office in Copenhagen, Denmark.

Team

The team consists of Financial Controllers based in London, Sheffield, Madrid, and Copenhagen, creating a diverse and international working environment. Role

You will become an integral part of our expanding team in Accounting, Compliance, and Controlling team for EMEA. We are committed to supporting your professional development and providing valuable learning opportunities.

The role offers broad exposure to finance, accounting, compliance, and corporate administration across a portfolio of international renewable energy investments. You will work closely with internal stakeholders, banks, auditors, legal advisers, corporate service providers, and other external counterparties. Responsibilities will consist of but are not limited to:

• Assisting with bank-access administration and the maintenance of authorized users and signatories

You

We look for the following in a candidate:

• Structured problem-solving skills and a responsible approach to tasks

• Close attention to detail and a high level of accuracy

• An interest in operational finance, accounting, compliance

• Ability to follow up effectively with internal and external stakeholders
